title: feat: Add multi-auth token support and ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL passthrough (CLI only)
body:

- CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (original, highest priority)
- ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN (for API proxies and gateways)
- ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (direct Anthropic API)

Also adds ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and related env vars passthrough to SDK.

**⚠️ CLI Only**: This feature currently only works with the CLI (run.py). The Electron UI does not yet support these new authentication options and will require additional work.

Changes:
- New core/auth.py with centralized auth logic
- Updated core/client.py to use auth helpers
- Updated cli/utils.py to show auth source and base URL

- Updated 5 modules: `runners/ai_analyzer/claude_client.py`, `runners/insights_runner.py`, `merge/ai_resolver/claude_client.py`, `analysis/insight_extractor.py`, `integrations/linear/updater.py`

## Testing

Created and ran comprehensive test suite with 6 tests:
- ✓ Priority order correct
- ✓ Error handling correct
- ✓ SDK env var compatibility works
- ✓ SDK env vars collected correctly
- ✓ CLI Utils integration works
- ✓ Client integration works

All tests pass.

## Additional Notes

**Future Work Needed:**
- Integrate multi-auth support into Electron UI settings
- Add UI controls for ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL configuration
- Update UI environment variable handling

This PR focuses on CLI functionality. UI integration will require separate work.

Claude issue summary:

## Issue: electron-rebuild fails on Windows - node-pty compilation error

  ### Environment
  - OS: Windows
  - Node: v22.14.0
  - npm: 11.1.0

  ### Problem
  Installation fails during `npm install` with the following error:

  ✖ Rebuild Failed

  An unhandled error occurred inside electron-rebuild
  node-gyp failed to rebuild 'D:\Koding\Autoclaude\auto-claude-ui\node_modules\node-pty'

  ### Root Cause
  The `node-pty` package is a native Node.js module that requires C++ compilation tools. On Windows, these tools are not
   installed by default, causing `node-gyp` to fail during the rebuild process.

  ### Solution Options

  **Option 1: Install Windows Build Tools (Recommended)**
  ```powershell
  # Run as Administrator
  npm install --global windows-build-tools

  Or manually install Visual Studio Build Tools 2022 with "Desktop development with C++" workload from:
  https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/downloads/#build-tools-for-visual-studio-2022

  Option 2: Skip native rebuild (Quick test)
  cd auto-claude-ui
  npm install --ignore-scripts
  npm run build
  npm start
  Note: Terminal features may not work with this approach.

  Option 3: Use prebuilt binaries
  cd auto-claude-ui
  npm install --force

  Additional Context

  This is a common issue on Windows when installing Electron apps that depend on native modules like node-pty. The
  module requires native compilation which needs Visual Studio C++ build tools.

title: feat(security): add SECURITY_STRICT_MODE for hardened defense
body:
## Summary

This PR adds an optional strict security mode that provides enhanced protection against prompt injection and data exfiltration attacks.

### When `SECURITY_STRICT_MODE=true`:

**Blocked Commands:**
- `eval`, `exec`, `sh`, `bash`, `zsh` - These can bypass command validation by spawning new shells or executing arbitrary code

**New Validated Commands:**
- `curl`: POST/PUT to external hosts blocked (GET allowed, localhost unrestricted)
- `wget`: POST to external hosts blocked (GET allowed, localhost unrestricted)

### Files Changed
- `base.py`: Split BASE_COMMANDS into SAFE/DANGEROUS/NETWORK categories with mode-aware functions
- `network_validators.py`: New validators for curl/wget that prevent data exfiltration
- `validator_registry.py`: Mode-aware validator loading
- `hooks.py`: Updated to use mode-aware functions
- `.env.example`: Documented SECURITY_STRICT_MODE setting
- `SECURITY.md`: New comprehensive security model documentation

### Backward Compatibility
- **Normal mode (default)** maintains full backward compatibility
- Existing projects work without any changes
- Strict mode is **opt-in** via environment variable

### Testing
Inline tests verify:
- Mode switching works correctly
- Dangerous commands excluded in strict mode
- curl/wget validators block external POST but allow GET
- Localhost requests remain unrestricted

## Motivation

During a security review of this project, I identified that commands like `eval`, `exec`, and shell spawners (`sh`, `bash`, `zsh`) could be exploited via prompt injection attacks. Similarly, `curl` and `wget` could be used for data exfiltration.

This PR provides a configurable option for users who need stricter security without breaking backward compatibility.

- [x] curl/wget validators allow GET requests

title: Auto Claude doesn't work with GitHub Organization repositories
body:
## Bug Report

### Description
Auto Claude (Desktop UI v2.5.0) is unable to access repositories from GitHub organizations, despite successful authentication and verified access via GitHub CLI.

### Environment
- **Platform**: macOS (Intel)
- **Auto Claude Version**: 2.5.0
- **GitHub CLI**: v2.83.1
- **Authentication Method Tested**: 
  - GitHub OAuth (via GitHub CLI) ✓ Working
  - Personal Access Tokens (fine-grained) ✗ Not working
  - Classic tokens ✗ Not working

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Authenticate via GitHub OAuth in Auto Claude Settings
2. Enter organization repository URL: `https://github.com/imaginationeverywhere/ppsv-charities`
3. Try to save settings

### Expected Behavior
Auto Claude should detect and allow access to organization repositories that the user has access to.

### Actual Behavior
Connection Status returns: "GitHub API error: 404 Not Found"

### What Works
- `gh auth status` - Shows authenticated as mojaray2k with proper scopes (gist, read:org, repo)
- `gh repo view imaginationeverywhere/ppsv-charities` - Successfully displays repo
- `gh repo list imaginationeverywhere` - Successfully lists org repos
- Git clone via SSH - Works perfectly
- Direct authentication via GitHub CLI - No issues

### What Doesn't Work
- Personal Access Tokens (fine-grained) with resource owner set to organization
- Personal Access Tokens (classic) with repo scope
- GitHub OAuth flow in Auto Claude UI
- All tested tokens show "404 Not Found" from GitHub API

### Additional Details
- User is a member of the organization
- Organization does not use SSO
- Token permissions verified and set correctly
- Same tokens work with `gh` CLI but fail in Auto Claude

### Suggested Root Cause
Auto Claude may not properly support GitHub organization repositories, or there may be an issue with how it constructs GitHub API calls for org-owned resources.

title: Fix GitHub organization repository support
body:
## Summary

Fixed Auto Claude's inability to access GitHub organization repositories. Organization members can now successfully authenticate and work with org repos.

## Problem
- Organization repositories were returning 404 errors despite user having access via GitHub CLI
- The `/user/repos` endpoint wasn't fetching organization repositories
- Repository URLs weren't being normalized, causing errors when full GitHub URLs were provided

## Solution

### 1. Enhanced repository listing
- Added `affiliation=owner,collaborator,organization_member` parameter to `/user/repos` endpoint
- Now correctly fetches repositories from all organizations the user is a member of

### 2. Added repository reference normalization
- New `normalizeRepoReference()` utility handles multiple URL formats:
  - `owner/repo` (standard format)
  - `https://github.com/owner/repo`
  - `https://github.com/owner/repo.git`
  - `git@github.com:owner/repo.git`
- Prevents 404 errors from malformed input

### 3. Applied normalization consistently
- All GitHub API calls now normalize repository references before making requests
- Updated: repository-handlers.ts, issue-handlers.ts

## Testing
- Verified with organization repo: `imaginationeverywhere/ppsv-charities`
- Tested authentication via GitHub OAuth and gh CLI
- All existing functionality preserved

## Files Changed
- `auto-claude-ui/src/main/ipc-handlers/github/utils.ts` - Added normalizeRepoReference utility
- `auto-claude-ui/src/main/ipc-handlers/github/repository-handlers.ts` - Enhanced org repo support & normalization
- `auto-claude-ui/src/main/ipc-handlers/github/issue-handlers.ts` - Applied normalization to all issue API calls

## Fixes
Closes #20

title: Feature: Per-Project GitHub Repository Configuration
body:
## Summary

Currently, Auto Claude stores GitHub repository configuration globally, which means the same repository is applied to ALL projects. This is a poor UX pattern and doesn't align with how Claude Code Desktop handles project-specific configurations.

**Request:** Implement per-project GitHub repository configuration, similar to Claude Code Desktop.

## Problem

- Users have multiple projects with different GitHub repositories
- Setting a GitHub repo in one project affects all other projects
- No way to configure organization repos for specific projects while using personal repos for others
- This is especially problematic when working with organization repositories (imaginationeverywhere/ppsv-charities) and personal projects simultaneously

## Current Behavior

1. User goes to **Settings** → **GitHub Integration**
2. Enters repository: `imaginationeverywhere/ppsv-charities`
3. This repository is now applied to ALL projects (quik-nation, the-g-code, etc.)
4. No way to override per-project

## Desired Behavior (Like Claude Code Desktop)

1. **Global Settings**: Optional default GitHub token (can be shared)
2. **Project Settings**: Each project has its OWN GitHub repository configuration
3. Project repo should override global settings if specified
4. UI should be in **Project Settings**, not Global Settings

## Example Workflow

```
Project: quik-nation-ai-boilerplate
  └─ GitHub Token: (inherited from global)
  └─ GitHub Repo: quiknation/quik-nation-ai-boilerplate ✓

Project: ppsv-charities
  └─ GitHub Token: (inherited from global)
  └─ GitHub Repo: imaginationeverywhere/ppsv-charities ✓

Project: the-g-code
  └─ GitHub Token: (inherited from global)
  └─ GitHub Repo: [not configured - skip GitHub Issues] ✓
```

## Implementation Notes

- GitHub token can remain global (shared across projects)
- Repository reference should be per-project in `.auto-claude/.env`
- Update UI to show project-specific repo in project settings
- Maintain backward compatibility with existing global config

## Files Affected

- `auto-claude-ui/src/renderer/components/project-settings/GitHubIntegrationSection.tsx`
- `auto-claude-ui/src/main/ipc-handlers/github/utils.ts` - Already reads from project `.env` ✓
- `auto-claude-ui/src/renderer/pages/ProjectSettings.tsx`

## Why This Matters

This aligns Auto Claude with Claude Code Desktop's UX pattern where each project can have project-specific settings while sharing common configurations (like authentication tokens).

## Related

- PR #24: Fix GitHub organization repository support (complements this feature)

title: fix: implement automated version management to prevent version mismatches (#27)
body:
## Problem

Fixes #27

Version 2.5.5 was displaying as 2.5.0 in the updater because `package.json` wasn't updated when the git tag was created. This caused confusion for users who downloaded v2.5.5 but saw v2.5.0 in the updater.

## Solution

This PR implements a comprehensive automated version management system to **prevent this issue from ever happening again**:

### 🤖 1. Version Bump Script (`scripts/bump-version.js`)

An automated script that handles the entire version update process:
- ✅ Updates `package.json` with new version
- ✅ Creates git commit automatically
- ✅ Creates git tag automatically
- ✅ Prevents human error in version management
- ✅ Supports semver bumps (major/minor/patch) or specific versions

**Usage:**
```bash
node scripts/bump-version.js patch   # 2.5.5 -> 2.5.6
node scripts/bump-version.js minor   # 2.5.5 -> 2.6.0
node scripts/bump-version.js major   # 2.5.5 -> 3.0.0
node scripts/bump-version.js 2.6.0   # Set specific version
```

### ✅ 2. Version Validation Workflow (`.github/workflows/validate-version.yml`)

A GitHub Action that automatically validates version consistency:
- ✅ Runs automatically on every git tag push
- ✅ Validates `package.json` version matches the git tag
- ✅ **Fails CI if versions mismatch** with clear error messages
- ✅ Prevents releases with incorrect versions from being published

This ensures that if someone manually creates a tag without updating `package.json`, the CI will catch it immediately and prevent the release.

### 📚 3. Documentation (`RELEASE.md`)

Complete documentation for the release process:
- Step-by-step release guide
- Troubleshooting for version issues
- Release checklist
- Examples and best practices

### 🔧 4. Fixed Current Version

- Updated `auto-claude-ui/package.json` from 2.5.0 to 2.5.5
- Updated `CLAUDE.md` with release section

## Impact

- ✅ **Prevents version mismatch issues from happening again** - automated validation
- ✅ **Automates release process** - reduces manual steps and errors
- ✅ **CI validation catches manual errors** - safety net for manual releases
- ✅ **Clear documentation** - maintainers know the correct process

## Testing

The validation workflow will run automatically on the next tag push. To test:

1. Create a test tag: `git tag v2.5.6-test`
2. Push it: `git push origin v2.5.6-test`
3. The workflow will validate the version matches

## Checklist

- [x] Version automation script created
- [x] GitHub Action validation workflow created
- [x] Documentation added (RELEASE.md)
- [x] CLAUDE.md updated with release section
- [x] package.json version fixed (2.5.0 -> 2.5.5)
- [x] Commit message follows convention
- [x] Issue #27 referenced

---

**Note:** This PR ensures that issue #27 can never happen again through automation and CI validation.

title: Fix Windows Python detection and initialization popup issues
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes three critical issues that were preventing Windows users from using Auto Claude UI effectively:

1. **Python command not found on Windows** (`spawn python3 ENOENT`)
2. **Initialization popup not closing automatically** after successful setup
3. **Python dependency installation failing** due to pip detection issues

## Issues Fixed

### 🐛 Issue 1: Python Detection on Windows

**Problem:**
- All Python-dependent services hardcoded `python3` as default command
- Windows uses `python` or `py`, not `python3`
- Resulted in `spawn python3 ENOENT` errors when:
  - Creating tasks
  - Generating AI titles
  - Running agents
  - Installing dependencies

**Solution:**
- Created `python-detector.ts` utility with intelligent cross-platform detection
- **Windows**: tries `py -3` → `python` → `python3` → `py`
- **Unix/Mac**: tries `python3` → `python`
- Verifies each candidate is actually Python 3.x
- Updated all services to use auto-detection

### 🐛 Issue 2: Initialization Popup Won't Close

**Problem:**
- After successful project initialization, popup stayed open
- Users had to manually close it
- No error feedback on failure

**Root Cause:**
- Race condition in Dialog's `onOpenChange` handler
- Couldn't distinguish user close vs programmatic close
- React state batching caused timing issues

**Solution:**
- Added `initSuccess` state flag to track completion
- Updated close logic to check flag before triggering skip
- Added error state and UI display for failures
- Added comprehensive debug logging

### 🐛 Issue 3: Dependency Installation Failing

**Problem:**
- Python 3.13+ creates `pip3.exe` instead of `pip.exe`
- PythonEnvManager looked for wrong filename
- Dependencies never installed even with valid venv

**Solution:**
- Changed to use `python -m pip` (universal across versions)
- Added automatic pip bootstrapping via `python -m ensurepip`
- Works on all Python versions and platforms

## Files Changed

### New Files
- `auto-claude-ui/src/main/python-detector.ts` - Cross-platform Python detection

### Modified Files
**Python Detection:**
- `auto-claude-ui/src/main/agent/agent-process.ts`
- `auto-claude-ui/src/main/title-generator.ts`
- `auto-claude-ui/src/main/terminal-name-generator.ts`

**Initialization Popup:**
- `auto-claude-ui/src/renderer/App.tsx`
- `auto-claude-ui/src/renderer/stores/project-store.ts`

## Testing

✅ TypeScript compilation passes
✅ No type errors
✅ All imports resolved

**Manual Testing Needed:**
- [ ] Test initialization popup on fresh project
- [ ] Test task creation on Windows
- [ ] Test AI title generation
- [ ] Test dependency installation in new venv
- [ ] Verify error handling works

## Impact

**Before:**
- Windows users couldn't create tasks or run agents
- Initialization popup was confusing
- Dependencies failed to install on Python 3.13+

**After:**
- ✅ Works on Windows, Mac, and Linux
- ✅ Supports Python 3.9 - 3.13+
- ✅ Popup closes automatically on success
- ✅ Clear error messages on failure
- ✅ Dependencies install reliably

Bug fix for "Request Changes" in Human Review not applying fixes.

**Problem:** Clicking "Request Changes" caused the task to immediately return to human_review without applying any fixes.

**Root causes:**
- `QA_FIX_REQUEST.md` was written to main project instead of worktree
- QA process ran against main project path (missing `implementation_plan.json`)
- Early return in `qa_commands.py` and `loop.py` if QA already approved, ignoring pending human feedback

**Fixes:**
- Write `QA_FIX_REQUEST.md` to worktree spec directory
- Run QA process with worktree path where build files exist
- Check for human feedback before "already approved" early return
- Process human feedback by running QA fixer first
- Reset staged changes in main when going back to QA
- Add check for already-staged changes to prevent duplicate work

## Test plan

- [x] TypeScript build passes

title: UI stuck at 10% 'Analyzing' while backend completes successfully - task_logs.json parsing failures
body:
## Summary

The Electron UI shows a task stuck at 10% progress on "Analyzing project structure..." for 24+ hours, while the Python backend actually completed all work successfully (8/8 subtasks, QA approved, ready to merge). The UI never updates because `task_logs.json` encounters JSON parsing errors during live updates, causing `TaskLogService` to fail silently and freeze the progress display.

This leads users to believe tasks are stuck and delete completed work.

## Environment

- **Auto-Claude UI Version**: v2.3.0
- **Latest Commit**: `a20b8cf` (Enhance task status handling...)
- **OS**: macOS 14.6.0 (Darwin 24.6.0)
- **Node.js**: v24.11
- **Python**: 3.14 (in venv)
- **Project**: Medium-sized React/TypeScript project

## Problem Description

### What the User Saw

1. Started a new task via Auto-Claude UI
2. Progress bar showed "Analyzing project structure... 10%"
3. Progress remained at 10% for ~24 hours despite high CPU activity
4. Terminal showed repeated JSON parsing errors in `task_logs.json`
5. User assumed task was stuck and deleted it
6. **Actual state**: All work was complete, QA approved, ready to merge

### What Actually Happened (Backend)

The Python backend (`spec_runner.py` → `run.py` → agents) completed successfully:

- ✅ All 8 subtasks completed
- ✅ 90/90 unit tests passing
- ✅ TypeScript build: SUCCESS
- ✅ Type check: SUCCESS  
- ✅ Lint: 0 errors
- ✅ QA validation: APPROVED at 2025-12-18T16:17:00Z
- ✅ 11 commits on feature branch
- ✅ Status in `implementation_plan.json`: `"qa_signoff": { "status": "approved" }`

### Root Cause

The Electron UI's `TaskLogService` (`src/main/task-log-service.ts`) watches `task_logs.json` and attempts to parse it every few seconds. During active agent sessions, the file is being written to concurrently, resulting in **transient malformed JSON**.

**Terminal errors observed:**
```
[TaskLogService] Failed to load logs from .../task_logs.json: 
  SyntaxError: Expected ',' or '}' after property value in JSON at position 128794 (line 584 column 7712)

[TaskLogService] Failed to load logs from .../task_logs.json:
  SyntaxError: Expected ',' or '}' after property value in JSON at position 346013 (line 1984 column 8331)

[TaskLogService] Failed to load logs from .../task_logs.json:
  SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input
```

When parsing fails, `TaskLogService.loadLogsFromPath()` catches the error, logs it, and **returns `null`**. The UI receives no updates, and the progress bar freezes at its last known state (10%).

## Expected Behavior

1. **UI should show task progress** even if `task_logs.json` has transient parsing errors
2. **Progress should advance** as phases complete (10% → 25% → 50% → 75% → 100%)
3. **Final status should reflect QA approval**, not show "stuck at Analyze 10%"
4. **User should see "Ready to Merge"** notification when QA approves

## Actual Behavior

1. ✗ UI shows "Analyzing... 10%" indefinitely
2. ✗ Progress bar never advances past 10%
3. ✗ No indication that backend completed successfully
4. ✗ User deletes what they believe is a stuck task (losing completed work)

## Technical Details

### File Sizes at Completion

```
task_logs.json: 884,531 bytes (864 KB)
Lines: 6,432
```

### Progress Tracking Logic

From `auto-claude-ui/src/main/agent/agent-process.ts:216-221`:

```typescript
// Reset phase progress on phase change, otherwise increment
if (phaseChanged) {
  phaseProgress = 10; // Start new phase at 10%
} else {
  phaseProgress = Math.min(90, phaseProgress + 5); // Increment within phase
}
```

**Problem**: When the first phase ("Analyze") starts, progress is set to 10%. If subsequent progress updates fail due to JSON parsing errors, it never advances.

### JSON Parsing Logic

From `auto-claude-ui/src/main/task-log-service.ts:43-50`:

```typescript
try {
  const content = readFileSync(logFile, 'utf-8');
  const logs = JSON.parse(content) as TaskLogs;
  return logs;
} catch (error) {
  console.error(`[TaskLogService] Failed to load logs from ${logFile}:`, error);
  return null; // ← Silent failure
}
```

**Problem**: No retry logic, no incremental parsing, no fallback to last known good state.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a new task on a medium-to-large project (triggers long-running spec creation)
2. Observe terminal output for `[TaskLogService]` JSON parsing errors
3. Note that UI progress remains at "Analyzing... 10%" despite errors
4. Let task run to completion (~hours for complex projects)
5. Check `implementation_plan.json` - will show `"qa_signoff": { "status": "approved" }`
6. UI still shows "Analyzing... 10%" - disconnect between UI and reality

## Impact

- **Critical**: Users delete completed work thinking tasks are stuck
- **Wasted compute**: Hours of Claude API usage discarded
- **Loss of trust**: Users lose confidence in Auto-Claude's reliability
- **Poor UX**: No visibility into actual backend progress

## Suggested Fixes

### 1. Graceful JSON Parsing (Short-term)

```typescript
// task-log-service.ts
private loadLogsFromPath(logFile: string): TaskLogs | null {
  try {
    const content = readFileSync(logFile, 'utf-8');
    const logs = JSON.parse(content) as TaskLogs;
    this.lastKnownGoodState = logs; // Cache last good parse
    return logs;
  } catch (error) {
    console.warn(`[TaskLogService] JSON parse failed, using cached state:`, error.message);
    return this.lastKnownGoodState ?? null; // Fall back to cache
  }
}
```

### 2. File Locking or Atomic Writes (Medium-term)

Ensure Python agents write to `task_logs.json.tmp`, then atomically rename to `task_logs.json` to prevent reading mid-write.

### 3. Streaming JSON or NDJSON Format (Long-term)

Replace single JSON object with newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) where each log entry is a separate line. Allows reading partial files without parsing errors.

### 4. Direct IPC from Python Backend (Long-term)

Instead of polling file changes, have Python agents send progress updates via IPC/WebSocket directly to Electron main process.

### 5. UI Fallback to `implementation_plan.json` (Short-term)

If `task_logs.json` fails to parse, read `implementation_plan.json` to determine actual phase/subtask status:

```typescript
// Check subtask completion percentage
const completed = phases.flatMap(p => p.subtasks).filter(s => s.status === 'completed').length;
const total = phases.flatMap(p => p.subtasks).length;
const progress = Math.round((completed / total) * 100);
```

## Evidence

### Terminal Output Showing Repeated Errors

```
[TaskLogService] Failed to load logs from .../task_logs.json: SyntaxError: Expected ',' or '}' after property value in JSON at position 128794 (line 584 column 7712)
[TaskLogService] Failed to load logs from .../task_logs.json: SyntaxError: Expected ',' or '}' after property value in JSON at position 346013 (line 1984 column 8331)
[TaskLogService] Failed to load logs from .../task_logs.json: SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input
```

*(Repeated dozens of times during task execution)*

### Worktree Contents Prove Completion

```bash
$ git log --oneline auto-claude/001-example-feature --not main | head -5
abc1234 qa: Sign off - all verification passed
def5678 auto-claude: subtask-4-2 - Export new utility functions
ghi9012 fix: Restore implementation plan status after accidental reset
jkl3456 auto-claude: subtask-4-1 - Run full test suite and fix any failures
mno7890 auto-claude: subtask-3-2 - Visual verification and edge case testing
```

### QA Report Confirms Approval

From `.auto-claude/specs/.../qa_report.md`:

```markdown
## Verdict

**SIGN-OFF**: APPROVED ✓

**Reason**:
All automated verification steps pass:
- All 8 implementation subtasks completed
- 90/90 unit tests passing for new functions
- TypeScript compilation succeeds with no errors
- Lint passes with 0 errors
- Production build succeeds
```

## Related Issues

After searching, no duplicate issues found for this specific problem (UI stuck at 10% with JSON parsing failures).

Possibly related:
- #38 - Planning phase failures (validation mismatch, but different symptom)
- #11 - Tasks skip to human review (missing auth, but different symptom)

## Workaround (For Users Who Hit This)

If your UI shows a task stuck at "Analyzing... 10%" for hours:

1. **Check the actual status** in the worktree:
   ```bash
   cat .worktrees/{task-name}/.auto-claude/specs/{task-name}/implementation_plan.json | grep "qa_signoff" -A 5
   ```

2. **If QA approved**, the work is done! Merge it:
   ```bash
   git checkout main
   git merge auto-claude/{task-name}
   git worktree remove .worktrees/{task-name}
   ```

3. **If still in progress**, check last subtask status:
   ```bash
   cat .worktrees/{task-name}/.auto-claude/specs/{task-name}/implementation_plan.json | grep '"status"' | tail -5
   ```

---

**Request**: Please prioritize this issue as it causes users to discard completed work, wasting both time and API costs.

title: macOS does not hold token at ~/.config/claude/credentials.json but in keychain
body:
### Bug Description

It is incorrectly assumed for Mac osx that the token is to be found at `~/.config/claude/credentials.json`.

### Expected Behavior

It to be read from the keychain. A wrapper could be created:

To use a Python helper to retrieve your Claude Code API key from the macOS Keychain, you can use the standard subprocess module to call the macOS security command.
1. Python Helper Script
This script retrieves the password for a specific service name. By default, Claude Code uses the service name Claude Code-credentials or Claude Code. 
```python
# get_keychain_key.py
import subprocess
import sys

def get_key_from_keychain(service_name):
    try:
        # -s specifies the service name
        # -w displays only the password/secret to stdout
        command = ["/usr/bin/security", "find-generic-password", "-s", service_name, "-w"]
        
        # Execute the command and capture output
        result = subprocess.run(command, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True)
        return result.stdout.strip()
    except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
        # Item not found or keychain is locked
        return None

if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Check both common service names used by Claude Code
    api_key = get_key_from_keychain("Claude Code-credentials") or \
              get_key_from_keychain("Claude Code")
    
    if api_key:
        # Output ONLY the key to stdout for Claude Code to read
        sys.stdout.write(api_key)
    else:
        sys.stderr.write("Error: Could not retrieve Claude key from Keychain.\n")
        sys.exit(1)
```
Use code with caution.

2. Alternative: Using the keyring Library
For a cleaner, more "Pythonic" approach that doesn't rely on raw shell commands, use the keyring library. 
Install: pip install keyring
Script:
```python
import keyring
import sys

api_key = keyring.get_password("Claude Code-credentials", "claude")
if api_key:
    sys.stdout.write(api_key)
else:
    sys.exit(1)
```
Use code with caution.

title: Fix file explorer to show hidden directories
body:
## Problem
Users couldn't access hidden directories like `.claude`, `.auto-claude`, `.github`, `.vscode`, etc. when creating tasks or adding file references.

## Root Cause
File explorer filtered out ALL files/directories starting with `.` except `.env`, making important configuration directories invisible.

## Solution

### 1. Allow hidden directories to be visible
- Changed filter to only hide hidden FILES, not directories
- Hidden directories like `.claude`, `.github`, `.vscode`, `.idea` now visible
- Users can now reference files from these important configuration directories

### 2. Keep useful hidden files visible
- `.env`, `.gitignore`, `.env.example`, `.env.local` still shown
- Other random hidden files (`.DS_Store`, etc.) still filtered out

### 3. Updated IGNORED_DIRS
- Removed `.auto-claude` (contains user specs/data)
- Removed `.vscode` and `.idea` (users may need IDE config)
- Kept truly problematic dirs: `.git`, `node_modules`, `.cache`, `.worktrees`

## Testing
✅ Hidden directories now appear in Project Files browser
✅ Can drag and reference files from `.claude`, `.auto-claude`, `.github`, etc.
✅ Irrelevant hidden files still filtered out

When users authenticate with Claude during the setup wizard, the OAuth token is now automatically saved to the active Claude profile instead of being ignored. This PR also integrates Claude authentication directly into the setup wizard, eliminating the need for users to manually run claude setup-token in a terminal.

  Before: OAuth token detected but not saved → users had to manually authenticate in terminal → confusing UX

  After: OAuth token automatically saved to active profile → wizard handles both GitHub and Claude auth → seamless first-time setup

###   Type of Change

  - Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
  - New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
  - Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)

###   Related Issues

  Fixes credential persistence issue where OAuth authentication reported success but token could not be found when running Auto Claude features (Roadmap, Task automation, etc.)

###   Changes Made

  Core Fix (Bug)

  - Modified claude-integration-handler.ts: Updated handleOAuthToken() to save tokens to active Claude profile when terminal ID doesn't match profile-specific pattern
    - Previously only saved tokens from terminals matching claude-login-(profile-\d+)-
    - Now saves to active profile for ANY terminal (e.g., during GitHub OAuth flow)
    - Emits success/failure events to renderer process

  Wizard Integration (Feature)

  - Created ClaudeOAuthFlow.tsx: New component for Claude authentication during setup
    - Handles ready/authenticating/success/error states
    - Auto-detects token via onTerminalOAuthToken event listener
    - Opens terminal running claude setup-token when user initiates auth
    - Auto-advances to next step after showing success message
  - Updated GitHubSetupModal.tsx: Integrated Claude auth into wizard flow
    - Changed step type: 'auth' | 'repo' | 'branch' → 'github-auth' | 'claude-auth' | 'repo' | 'branch' | 'complete'
    - Split authentication handlers: handleAuthSuccess → handleGitHubAuthSuccess + handleClaudeAuthSuccess
    - Updated progress indicator to show "Authenticate" and "Configure" steps
    - New wizard flow: GitHub Auth → Claude Auth → Repo Detection → Branch Selection → Complete

  Documentation

  - Added comments in App.tsx: Clarified difference between GitHub tokens (for repo operations) and Claude tokens (for AI features)

  Checklist

  - I have run pre-commit run --all-files and fixed any issues
  - I have added tests for my changes (if applicable)
  - All existing tests pass locally
  - I have updated documentation (if applicable)
  - My code follows the project's code style

###   Testing

  Manual Testing Required

  To verify the complete fix, test as a new user would experience it:

  1. Remove existing credentials (simulate new user):
  # Remove Claude profile tokens
  rm -rf ~/.config/auto-claude-ui/config/claude-profiles.json
  2. Run the setup wizard:
    - Launch Auto Claude UI
    - Create or select a project
    - Complete GitHub authentication (Step 1)
    - Complete Claude authentication (Step 2) - NEW
    - Confirm repository detection (Step 3)
    - Select base branch (Step 4)
  3. Verify token persistence:
    - Check that OAuth token was saved: Look for console message [ClaudeIntegration] OAuth token auto-saved to active profile
    - Test Roadmap generation (requires Claude credentials)
    - Test Task automation (requires Claude credentials)
    - Both should work without "token cannot be found" errors
  4. Edge case testing:
    - Try authenticating multiple times (should not duplicate)
    - Cancel wizard partway through and restart
    - Skip wizard and manually authenticate later (existing flow should still work)

  ### Expected Behavior

  - OAuth token appears in terminal output → automatically saved to active profile
  - Wizard completes without requiring manual claude setup-token command
  - AI features (Roadmap, Tasks) work immediately after wizard completion
  - Console shows: [ClaudeIntegration] OAuth token auto-saved to active profile: [profile-name]
  - Event emitted to renderer with success: true

###   Regression Testing

  Ensure existing authentication flows still work:
  - Manual claude setup-token in terminal (profile-specific terminals)
  - Switching between Claude profiles
  - Rate limit detection and profile switching

###   Additional Notes

  Why This Fix Was Needed

  The original code only saved OAuth tokens from terminals with IDs matching the pattern claude-login-(profile-\d+)-. During the GitHub setup wizard, terminals had different IDs, so tokens were detected but discarded with the log message:

  [ClaudeIntegration] OAuth token detected but not in a profile login terminal

  This caused a confusing UX where authentication appeared successful but features requiring credentials would fail silently.

  Architecture Context

  Auto Claude UI uses a Claude Profile system for multi-account support:
  - Profiles stored in ~/.config/auto-claude-ui/config/claude-profiles.json (encrypted)
  - Each profile can have a different OAuth token
  - getProfileEnv() provides CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN to spawned processes
  - Active profile determines which credentials are used

  Token Types (Important Distinction)

  This PR handles Claude AI tokens (sk-ant-oat01-...), not GitHub tokens:
  - GitHub tokens (gho_... / ghp_...): For GitHub API access (repo operations)
  - Claude tokens (sk-ant-oat01-...): For Claude AI access (Roadmap, Tasks, Ideation)

  Both are required but serve different purposes and are obtained through different OAuth flows.

title: Quality and Stability Alignment Before Continuing Feature Expansion
body:
### Problem Statement

The current development pace prioritizes continuous feature additions while several existing issues remain unresolved. Over time, this creates accumulating technical debt, increasing code complexity, and a product that is harder to stabilize and confidently rely on.

Without a deliberate moment to consolidate, fix, and structure the work already delivered, the project risks becoming less predictable to maintain and less valuable to users in the short and medium term. Addressing stability now is essential to preserve long-term momentum and product credibility.

### Proposed Solution

I propose a one to two-week stabilization phase during which feature development is intentionally paused to focus on product quality and foundation. This phase would aim to:

- Resolve all known bugs and regressions
- Refactor rushed or fragile code paths
- Deliver a first genuinely stable and usable version of Auto Claude
- Ensure the tool can be reliably used for the next 2–3 months without major disruption

In parallel, GitHub Projects should be used as the single source of truth to:

- Centralize and track all existing issues
- Collect and prioritize future feature requests
- Clearly separate bug fixing, technical debt, and new feature development

This creates clarity for developers, confidence for users, and a stronger base for future iterations.

### Alternatives Considered

An alternative would be to continue shipping features while fixing issues incrementally. In practice, this approach tends to compound problems: issues accumulate faster than they are resolved, priorities shift frequently, and meaningful refactoring becomes increasingly difficult.

A short, intentional stabilization period is the most efficient way to realign quality, reduce risk, and reset direction.

title: UsageMonitor passes encrypted token to API, causing "Failed to fetch usage" errors
body:
### Bug Description

The UsageMonitor class in usage-monitor.ts passes the encrypted OAuth token (enc:...) directly to the Anthropic API instead of decrypting it first. This causes the API call to fail, resulting in continuous "Failed to fetch usage" log messages and the usage monitor falling back to an unimplemented CLI method.

In auto-claude-ui/src/main/claude-profile/usage-monitor.ts at line ~102:

// Fetch current usage (hybrid approach)
const usage = await this.fetchUsage(activeProfile.id, activeProfile.oauthToken);
The code passes activeProfile.oauthToken directly, but this value is encrypted (prefixed with enc:) when stored. The token should be decrypted using profileManager.getProfileToken() before being passed to the API.

### Expected Behavior

The usage monitor should decrypt the token before making API calls:

// Get decrypted token from profile manager (oauthToken is encrypted with enc: prefix)
const decryptedToken = profileManager.getProfileToken(activeProfile.id);
const usage = await this.fetchUsage(activeProfile.id, decryptedToken);

### Steps to Reproduce


Configure a Claude profile with an OAuth token (token gets encrypted and stored with enc: prefix)
Enable proactive usage monitoring in auto-switch settings (proactiveSwapEnabled: true)
Observe console logs showing:

[UsageMonitor] API method failed, falling back to CLI
[UsageMonitor] CLI fallback not implemented, API method should be used
[UsageMonitor] Failed to fetch usage
These messages repeat every 30 seconds (the default usageCheckInterval)

### Error Messages / Logs

```shell
[UsageMonitor] CLI fallback not implemented, API method should be used
[UsageMonitor] Failed to fetch usage
[UsageMonitor] CLI fallback not implemented, API method should be used
[UsageMonitor] Failed to fetch usage
```

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Component

Electron UI (auto-claude-ui/)

### Auto Claude Version

2.5.6

### Operating System

Windows

### Python Version

_No response_

### Node.js Version (for UI issues)

_No response_

### Additional Context


The token encryption was introduced in profile-storage version 3 using Electron's safeStorage API. The getProfileEnv() function in rate-limit-detector.ts correctly handles decryption (lines 273-276), but the usage monitor doesn't follow the same pattern. Related code that correctly decrypts tokens:
rate-limit-detector.ts:getProfileEnv() - uses profileManager.getProfileToken()
claude-integration-handler.ts:invokeClaude() - uses profileManager.getProfileToken()

title: fix: Replace space with hyphen in productName to fix PTY daemon spawn
body:
Spaces in productName cause ENOENT errors when spawning the PTY daemon on macOS. The path gets truncated at the space, causing spawn to fail.

Changes 'Auto Claude' to 'Auto-Claude' to maintain readability while fixing the path handling issue.

## Summary

When the app is packaged on macOS, `process.execPath` includes the product name in the path (e.g., `/path/to/Auto Claude.app/Contents/MacOS/Auto Claude`). The PTY daemon client at `src/main/terminal/pty-daemon-client.ts:126` spawns a child process using this path. The space in "Auto Claude" causes path handling issues, resulting in ENOENT errors where only `/path/to/Auto` is recognized.

title: Feature request: “Single-install” + Devcontainer-first execution mode (zero host deps, works with worktrees)
body:
### Problem Statement

Problem / Motivation

I really love Auto-Claude’s workflow and UI, but I’m struggling to adopt it in teams where:
	1.	There are too many host dependencies to install (Node + Python + Docker Desktop + various setup steps). This is a big adoption barrier—especially for onboarding or locked-down corporate laptops.
	2.	Most of our codebases are developed in devcontainers, and getting Auto-Claude to run validation/build/test commands inside the devcontainer currently feels like extra plumbing. Since the tool creates worktrees, it’s even easier to get “runs on host” vs “runs in container” mismatches.

Overall: the project’s value is highest when setup is trivial and environment differences disappear.



### Proposed Solution

Feature request

A) “Single install” distribution option (one thing to install / one file to download)

Please consider shipping one of the following (or equivalent):
	•	A single self-contained binary (e.g., via PyInstaller / Nuitka / similar) for the backend + bundled UI, so users download one installer and go.
	•	Or a single package manager entrypoint:
	•	brew install auto-claude (macOS) / winget (Windows) / apt (Linux), with everything bundled.
	•	Or a single Docker image that includes everything needed to run Auto-Claude (UI optional), with minimal host requirements.

The goal is: a new user should be able to install Auto-Claude with one command or one download, without separately installing Node/Python/etc.

Acceptance criteria (example):
	•	Fresh machine → install Auto-Claude via one step → point it at a repo → run.
	•	No separate “install Python/Node” docs for the common path.

B) Devcontainer-first execution mode (run commands in-container automatically)

Add a “Devcontainer Mode” (or “Container Execution Provider”) so that:
	•	Auto-Claude can detect devcontainer config (.devcontainer/devcontainer.json etc.)
	•	Worktree-aware commands (validate/test/build) automatically execute inside the devcontainer, not on the host.
	•	It works with both:
	•	devcontainer exec … (VS Code Dev Containers CLI)
	•	and/or docker compose exec … for compose-based devcontainers

Key requirement: worktree compatibility
Auto-Claude creates worktrees (e.g., .worktrees/<task>). Devcontainer execution should run in the correct worktree path so tests validate the actual changes.

Suggested UX:
	•	Project setting: Execution environment
	•	Host (default)
	•	Devcontainer (devcontainer CLI)
	•	Docker Compose service (select service)
	•	And a “health check” button: verify container is running, can git status, can run configured test command.

Acceptance criteria (example):
	•	Repo with devcontainer, dependencies only installed inside container
	•	User runs “Start task” in UI
	•	Auto-Claude creates worktree
	•	Validation commands run inside the devcontainer in that worktree
	•	No extra wrapper scripts needed per-project

C) Optional: Make Memory Layer “plug-and-play”

If the Memory Layer requires Docker Desktop, consider offering:
	•	An embedded/local DB option (sqlite or similar) for “lite mode”
	•	Or let the Docker container distribution include it, so the host does not need Docker Desktop for the common path

Why this would be a big win
	•	Removes the #1 adoption blocker: long install/setup.
	•	Aligns with how many teams build software today: containerized dev environments.
	•	Reduces “works on my machine” drift between host and container.
	•	Makes onboarding as easy as “install once, open repo, run”.

title: fix(updater): HTTP 300 error when downloading updates if branch/tag names collide
body:
## Bug Description

The auto-update feature fails with HTTP 300 (Multiple Choices) when a GitHub release tag has the same name as a branch.

## Error Message

```
HTTP 300: {"message":"'v2.6.0' has multiple possibilities: 
https://github.com/AndyMik90/Auto-Claude/tarball/refs/heads/v2.6.0, 
https://github.com/AndyMik90/Auto-Claude/tarball/refs/tags/v2.6.0"}
```

## Root Cause

In `auto-claude-ui/src/main/updater/update-installer.ts`, the code uses `release.tarball_url` directly:

```typescript
const tarballUrl = release.tarball_url;
```

This URL uses an ambiguous format (`/tarball/v2.6.0`) that GitHub can't resolve when both a branch AND a tag have the same name.

## Suggested Fix

Use an explicit tag reference URL instead:

```typescript
// Use explicit tag reference URL to avoid HTTP 300 when branch/tag names collide
const tarballUrl = `https://api.github.com/repos/${GITHUB_CONFIG.owner}/${GITHUB_CONFIG.repo}/tarball/refs/tags/${release.tag_name}`;
```

This tells GitHub explicitly that we want the tag, not the branch.

## Environment

- macOS
- Auto Claude v2.5.5 → v2.6.0 update

title: Multiple CLI Agents
body:
### Problem Statement

Auto-Claude is designed as a desktop workflow for “autonomous multi-session AI coding” with a Kanban board, parallel agents, agent terminals, and git worktrees for safe isolation. It currently emphasizes “Run Claude Code in up to 12 terminals… with one-click task context injection” and parallel/self-validating flows. 

In practice, teams often need multi-agent planning and execution:

Claude may be best for planning/architecture and high-context reasoning.

Codex CLI / Gemini CLI / Cursor agent / Grok may be better for:

quick fixes
repetitive refactors
boilerplate generation
fast iterations and cheaper runs

Today, Auto-Claude’s task execution model is effectively “Claude-only” (by design focus), which creates a gap:

No standardized way to assign tasks to different CLI agents from the same Kanban board
No governance to optimize cost vs complexity (simple tasks still consume expensive agent time)
No consistent mechanism to normalize outputs (diffs/logs/status) across different agent CLIs

No “agent capability routing” (which agent should pick this card?)

Auto-Claude already provides the right workflow shell; it needs an agent abstraction layer to support multiple agent runtimes while preserving the existing Kanban-driven workflow. 


### Proposed Solution

Extend Auto-Claude so that each Kanban task can be executed by a selected agent provider (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, etc.)

title: fix(task): prevent specs deletion when merge fails or is rejected
body:
Fixes a critical bug where task specs were permanently deleted when a merge operation failed, causing all tasks to disappear from the dashboard.

## Root Cause

When a merge fails or is rejected during human review, the cleanup code in `execution-handlers.ts` ran `git clean -fd` to remove untracked files from the failed merge. However, this command also deleted:
- `.auto-claude/specs/` - all task specifications and plans
- `.worktrees/` - isolated work environments

These directories are untracked (in .gitignore) and were being wiped out.

## Solution

Modified the `git clean` command to exclude critical Auto Claude directories:

```diff
- spawnSync('git', ['clean', '-fd'], ...)
+ spawnSync('git', ['clean', '-fd', '-e', '.auto-claude', '-e', '.worktrees'], ...)
```

This preserves:
- Task specs, plans, and QA reports in `.auto-claude/`
- Isolated worktree environments in `.worktrees/`

title: fix(task-store): prevent log duplication across tasks with same specId
body:
## Summary

Fixes a bug in the task store where `appendLog()` was incorrectly appending logs to multiple tasks when they shared the same `specId`, causing log duplication and confusion.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

**File**: `auto-claude-ui/src/renderer/stores/task-store.ts` (line 145)

**Before:**
```typescript
t.id === taskId || t.specId === taskId  // Bug: matches by both id and specId
```

**After:**
```typescript
t.id === taskId  // Fixed: only matches by id
```

## Problem Description

The `appendLog` function was using both `t.id === taskId` AND `t.specId === taskId` to determine which task should receive a log entry. This caused logs to be duplicated across multiple tasks when they shared the same `specId`.

### Example Scenario

```typescript
// Two tasks in the store:
Task A: { id: "task-001", specId: "spec-042", logs: [] }
Task B: { id: "spec-042", specId: "spec-100", logs: [] }

// When calling:
appendLog("spec-042", "New log entry")

// BEFORE (buggy): Both Task A and Task B receive the log
// AFTER (fixed): Only Task B receives the log
```

### Impact

- Log pollution: Logs appeared in wrong tasks
- User confusion: Users saw logs from unrelated specs  
- Data integrity: Task logs were incorrectly associated

## Testing

✅ All tests pass:
- Python tests: 1145 passed
- Frontend tests: 364 passed (includes task-store test suite)
- Pre-commit hooks: All passing

## Checklist

- [x] I have run `pre-commit run --all-files` and fixed any issues
- [x] All existing tests pass locally
- [x] My code follows the project's code style

## Additional Notes

**Why this fix is correct:**

The `appendLog` function receives a `taskId` parameter, which should always be a task's unique `id` field. The previous logic that also checked `specId` was incorrect because:

1. Multiple tasks can share the same `specId` (e.g., during follow-up work)
2. Logs should only be appended to the specific task being executed, not all tasks with the same spec

**Breaking Changes**: None - this is a bug fix that restores correct behavior

The "Open Terminal" and "Open Project in Terminal" buttons successfully create terminals (backend returns `success: true`), but the terminals are not displayed in the "Agent Terminals" view.

1. Complete a task and navigate to "Human Review" phase

title: fix(python): use venv Python for all Python process spawning
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes Python process spawning across the entire codebase to use the venv Python (`pythonEnvManager.getPythonPath()`) instead of system Python (`findPythonCommand()`).

**Initial fix (commit 419070d):**
- Fixed `CONTEXT_REFRESH_INDEX` handler spawning hardcoded `python`

**Extended fix (commit bcc2144):**
After scanning the codebase, found and fixed 7 additional services that had the same issue:

| Service | Purpose | Fixed |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `agent-queue.ts` | Ideation and roadmap spawning | ✅ |
| `agent-process.ts` | Task execution spawning | ✅ |
| `terminal-name-generator.ts` | Terminal name generation | ✅ |
| `title-generator.ts` | Task title generation | ✅ |
| `insights/config.ts` | Insights executor | ✅ |
| `changelog-service.ts` | Changelog generation | ✅ |
| `worktree-handlers.ts` | Worktree merge operations | ✅ |

**CodeRabbit review fixes (commit ff44644):**
- Removed unused `parsePythonCommand` imports
- Fixed `worktree-handlers.ts` MERGE handler to spawn directly with pythonPath
- Fixed `changelog/generator.ts` to spawn directly with pythonPath
- Fixed `changelog/version-suggester.ts` to spawn directly with pythonPath

## Problem

On macOS, system Python is version 3.9, but the codebase uses Python 3.10+ syntax (`dict | None`). The venv at `auto-claude/.venv` has Python 3.11+ with all required packages installed (`claude_agent_sdk`, `dotenv`, etc).

Various features (ideation, roadmap, task execution, insights, etc.) were silently failing because:
1. System Python doesn't have required packages installed
2. System Python doesn't support the syntax used in the codebase

## Solution

All Python process spawning now uses `pythonEnvManager.getPythonPath()` which returns the venv Python path. Each service has proper error handling when the Python environment isn't ready.

The `parsePythonCommand()` function (which split paths by spaces for Windows `py -3` style commands) is no longer needed since we're using full absolute paths to the venv Python.

title: fix: prevent init dialog race condition causing duplicate initialization
body:
## Summary
- Fix race condition in the init dialog where the Initialize button could be clicked multiple times
- Reorder state updates in `handleInitialize()` success path to close dialog BEFORE re-enabling button
- Prevents duplicate initialization attempts from rapid clicks

## Problem
When initialization succeeded, the state updates were ordered as:
1. `setIsInitializing(false)` - re-enables the button
2. `setShowInitDialog(false)` - closes the dialog

This created a brief window where the button was clickable while the dialog was still visible.

## Solution
Reorder the state updates so the dialog closes FIRST:
1. `setShowInitDialog(false)` - closes the dialog
2. `setPendingProject(null)` - clears pending state
3. `setIsInitializing(false)` - re-enables the button

## Test plan

- [ ] Click Initialize rapidly multiple times

title: feat(ollama): add real-time download progress tracking
body:
## Summary

Add comprehensive real-time download progress tracking for Ollama model downloads in the onboarding wizard.

### Key Features

- **Real-time Progress Bars**: Animated progress indicators showing download percentage (0-100%)
- **Speed Calculation**: Live download speed display (MB/s, KB/s, or B/s) using useRef for accurate delta tracking
- **Time Remaining**: Estimated time to completion based on current download speed
- **NDJSON Parsing**: Proper handling of newline-delimited JSON streaming from Ollama API
- **Event Streaming**: IPC progress events emitted from main process to renderer during downloads
- **Clean Component Integration**: Seamless integration with OllamaModelSelector component

### Technical Implementation

**Backend (memory-handlers.ts)**:
- Parse NDJSON (newline-delimited JSON) from Ollama stderr
- Calculate percentage from completed/total bytes
- Emit progress events via IPC_CHANNELS.OLLAMA_PULL_PROGRESS

**Frontend (OllamaModelSelector.tsx)**:
- Register progress listener on component mount with automatic cleanup
- Track previous state using useRef for accurate speed calculation
- Display progress bar with percentage, speed, and time remaining
- Format time remaining (hours/minutes/seconds)

**Types & API**:
- Add onDownloadProgress listener to ElectronAPI interface
- Return cleanup function for proper event listener removal
- Use IPC_CHANNELS.OLLAMA_PULL_PROGRESS constant

### Testing
- ✅ TypeScript compilation (0 errors)
- ✅ Production build successful
- ✅ All 3 embedding models show progress tracking
- ✅ Mock implementation for browser testing

### UI/UX Improvements
- Progress bar fills smoothly from 0-100%
- Real-time speed updates (samples every 100+ ms)
- Time estimates update as speed changes
- Graceful handling of slow/fast connections
- Clean separation of concerns (progress tracking from download logic)

---

**Related**: Addresses the user's need for download feedback when pulling Ollama models. Users previously saw "Downloading..." with no progress indication.

title: Structure code into Feature Base and move to NPM
body:
# Project Modernization Summary

## Overview

This PR implements a comprehensive refactoring of Auto Claude's architecture, following SOLID, DRY, and KISS principles to create a more maintainable, scalable, and intuitive codebase. The changes focus on structural simplification, dependency management, and improved developer experience.

## Key Changes

### 🏗️ Architecture Refactoring

**Moved to `Apps/` Structure:**
- **`Apps/backend/`** - Python CLI framework, agents, specs, and QA pipeline  
- **`Apps/frontend/`** - Electron desktop application
- Eliminated the nested `auto-claude/auto-claude/` structure that violated DRY principles

**Benefits:**
- Clear separation of concerns (Single Responsibility Principle)
- Easier navigation and onboarding for new developers
- Simplified import paths and dependency management
- Better scalability for future component additions

### 📦 npm-Based Dependency Management

**Root-Level Package Management:**
- Added comprehensive `package.json` with unified scripts for all operations
- Simplified installation to single command: `npm run install:all`
- Streamlined development workflow with consistent npm scripts
- Enhanced developer experience with standardized commands

**Script Examples:**
```bash
npm run install:all        # Install both backend & frontend deps
npm start                  # Build and run desktop app
npm run dev               # Development mode with hot reload
npm run test:backend      # Run Python test suite
npm run package:win       # Build Windows installer
```

**Benefits:**
- Follows DRY principle - eliminates duplicate setup instructions
- KISS principle - single entry point for all common operations
- Reduces cognitive load for developers
- Enables better CI/CD pipeline integration

### 🧹 Code Cleanup & Modernization

**Removed Redundant Complexity:**
- Eliminated Docker dependencies (LadybugDB is now embedded)
- Simplified memory system architecture
- Streamlined frontend build configuration
- Updated all import paths and references to new structure

**Security & Quality Enhancements:**
- Updated pre-commit hooks configuration
- Enhanced linting rules and code quality standards
- Improved gitignore patterns for better artifact management
- Added comprehensive `.env.example` files for both apps

### 🔄 Improved Development Workflow

**Simplified Setup Process:**
```bash
# Before (complex, multiple steps)
cd auto-claude/auto-claude && python -m venv venv
cd venv && pip install -r requirements.txt
cd ../frontend && npm install

# After (simple, single command)  
npm run install:all
```

**Better Testing & Validation:**
- Unified test running through npm scripts
- Improved CI/CD workflows with better caching
- Enhanced pre-commit hook integration
- Streamlined build and packaging processes

## Migration Impact

### For Developers
- **Easier Onboarding:** New contributors can get started with a single command
- **Clearer Structure:** Logical separation between backend and frontend concerns  
- **Better Documentation:** Updated `CLAUDE.md` with comprehensive setup instructions
- **Modern Tooling:** Leveraging npm's ecosystem for dependency management

### For Users
- **Smoother Updates:** Automated version bump script ensures consistency
- **Better Performance:** Removing Docker dependencies improves startup time
- **Cross-Platform:** Enhanced build workflows for Windows, macOS, and Linux
- **Reliable Releases:** Improved CI/CD pipeline with better error handling

## Technical Improvements

### Code Architecture (SOLID Principles)
- **Single Responsibility:** Clear separation between UI (frontend) and logic (backend)
- **Open/Closed:** Extensible Apps structure allows adding new components
- **Dependency Inversion:** Frontend depends on backend abstractions, not implementations

### Code Quality (DRY Principle)
- Eliminated duplicate configuration files
- Centralized common scripts and utilities
- Unified packaging and distribution logic
- Consistent environment handling across apps

### Maintainability (KISS Principle)
- Simplified project structure reduces cognitive overhead
- Standardized npm scripts provide familiar interface
- Clear documentation reduces support burden
- Reduced complexity in build and deployment processes

## Backward Compatibility

### Breaking Changes
- All auto-claude imports and paths updated to Apps/backend structure
- Environment files moved from auto-claude/ to Apps/backend/
- Some CLI commands updated to reflect new structure (documented in CLAUDE.md)

### Migration Guide
1. Run `npm run install:all` to install new dependencies
2. Update any scripts referencing `auto-claude/` paths to `Apps/backend/`
3. Use npm scripts instead of direct python calls where possible
4. Refer to updated `CLAUDE.md` for complete usage instructions

## Files Changed

### Structural Changes
- **1,054 files changed** with strategic reorganization
- **+1,892 insertions, -23,271 deletions** (net simplification)
- Major directories restructured following Apps/ pattern

### Key Files Added/Modified
- `package.json` - Root-level dependency management
- `scripts/bump-version.js` - Automated version management
- `CLAUDE.md` - Updated comprehensive documentation
- `README.md` - Simplified getting started guide
- `.husky/` - Enhanced pre-commit hooks
- CI/CD workflows updated for Apps/ structure

## Conclusion

This refactoring transforms Auto Claude into a more professional, maintainable, and developer-friendly project while preserving all existing functionality. By applying SOLID, DRY, and KISS principles, we've created a codebase that's:

- **Simpler to understand** for new contributors
- **Easier to maintain** for the core team  
- **Faster to set up** for end users
- **More scalable** for future development

The changes position Auto Claude for sustainable growth while improving the experience for everyone involved in the project ecosystem.

title: fix: resolve Python environment race condition
body:
## Problem

Auto-Claude UI was experiencing two critical issues with Python environment initialization:

1. **Race Condition**: When multiple operations triggered initialization simultaneously (e.g., app startup + worktree merge), users would receive "Python environment not ready: Already initializing" error
2. **Path Handling**: Python paths containing spaces (like `/Users/.../Application Support/...`) caused spawn ENOENT errors

## Solution

### 1. Promise Queue Pattern
Replaced the simple boolean `isInitializing` flag with a promise-based queuing system:
- Concurrent requests now wait for the existing initialization promise instead of failing immediately
- Split `initialize()` into public method and private `_doInitialize()` to support promise sharing
- Returns cached status when already initialized with same source path

### 2. Path Handling with Spaces
Enhanced `parsePythonCommand()` to handle file paths correctly:
- Added `existsSync()` check before splitting on whitespace
- Preserves file paths with spaces as single command
- Still supports space-separated commands like "py -3"

## Technical Changes

**apps/frontend/src/main/python-env-manager.ts**:
- Added `initializationPromise: Promise<PythonEnvStatus> | null` field
- Modified `initialize()` to check for existing promise and wait
- Created private `_doInitialize()` with original initialization logic
- Enhanced JSDoc comments

**apps/frontend/src/main/python-detector.ts**:
- Imported `existsSync` from 'fs'
- Added file existence check in `parsePythonCommand()` before splitting

## Testing

Verified fixes with:
- Concurrent initialization from app startup + merge operation
- Python path with spaces: `/Users/jorisslagter/Library/Application Support/auto-claude-ui/python-venv/bin/python`
- Pre-commit hooks (ESLint, TypeScript check) passing

## Related Issues

Fixes the "Already initializing" error reported during worktree merge operations when Python environment was still initializing from app startup.

body: ### Bug Description Bug Analysis: Task Runner Crash Loop (File Not Found) Severity: High (Blocker) Component: Task Runner / Backend Process Management 1. Issue Summary The user is unable to run tasks in the auto-claude tool. When attempting to "Start" or "Recover" a task, the application briefly enters a "Running" state before crashing and reverting to a "Stuck / Needs Recovery" state. The UI correctly identifies that the background process has terminated unexpectedly, creating a loop where recovery is impossible without manual intervention. 2. Evidence & Observations The Error Log: The logs provide the definitive root cause. The application is attempting to execute a specific python script that does not exist at the expected path: [ERROR] Spec runner not found at: /Users/jorisslagter/Developer/Tools/auto-claude/auto-claude/runners/spec_runner.py The UI State Loop: Initial State: The task sits in "Pending" waiting for user input. Running State: Upon clicking Start/Recover, the UI briefly shows "Running" with an "Idle" progress bar. This indicates the frontend successfully sent the command to spawn the process. Crash State: The process immediately fails (due to the missing file), causing the UI to detect that "no active process was found". Stuck State: The card reverts to "Interrupted" and "Needs Recovery". 3. Root Cause Analysis The application runner is configured to launch spec_runner.py, but the file is missing from the filesystem at the specified absolute path. Potential Reasons: File Renaming/Deletion: The spec_runner.py file may have been refactored, renamed, or deleted in a recent update. Incorrect Path Configuration: The path in the configuration might be hardcoded or malformed (note the double auto-claude/auto-claude in the path: /Users/jorisslagter/Developer/Tools/auto-claude/auto-claude/runners/spec_runner.py). This suggests a potential issue with how the base directory is being appended to the relative path. Environment Mismatch: The application might be running in an environment where the file structure differs from what the config expects. 4. Recommended Fixes Immediate Workaround: Verify if spec_runner.py exists anywhere in the project. If it exists in a different location, update the configuration to point to the correct path. Code Fixes: Validate Path Generation: Check the code responsible for constructing the runner path. Look for logic that might be duplicating the project folder name (e.g., auto-claude/auto-claude). Add Pre-flight Check: Implement a file existence check (os.path.exists) before attempting to spawn the subprocess. If the file is missing, the app should fail gracefully with a clear "Configuration Error" rather than a generic "Stuck" state. Error Handling: Ensure the "Recover" function checks for the validity of the executable before retrying, preventing the infinite start/crash loop. ### Expected Behavior When the user clicks "Start" or "Recover": Process Initialization: The system should correctly resolve the absolute path to the runner script (removing the duplicate auto-claude/auto-claude segment if present) and successfully locate spec_runner.py. State Transition: The task status should switch to "Running" and remain in that state while the process is active. Execution: The background process should launch without immediate termination, executing the logic defined in spec_runner.py. Error Handling: If the runner file is missing, the application should surface a clear configuration error message in the UI (e.g., "Runner script not found") rather than crashing the process and reverting to a generic "Stuck" state. ### Steps to Reproduce Steps to Reproduce - Open the auto-claude application. - Navigate to a task card that is currently in a "Pending" state (e.g., "Fix roadmap generation stuck state"). - Click the "Start" button on the task card. - Observe: The card status briefly changes to "Running" with a blue badge. - Observe: After a few seconds, the task status reverts to "Stuck" and "Needs Recovery", showing an "Interrupted" progress bar. - Click the "Recover" (or "Recover & Restart Task") button. - Observe: The application enters a loop where it briefly shows "Running" before crashing back to the "Stuck" state. - Verify Logs: Check the console/application logs to confirm the error: [ERROR] Spec runner not found at: .../auto-claude/auto-claude/runners/spec_runner.py. ### Error Messages / Logs ```shell [ERROR] Spec runner not found at: /Users/jorisslagter/Developer/Tools/auto-claude/auto-claude/runners/spec_runner.py[ERROR] Spec runner not found at: /Users/jorisslagter/Developer/Tools/auto-claude/auto-claude/runners/spec_runner.py[ERROR] Spec runner not found at: /Users/jorisslagter/Developer/Tools/auto-claude/auto-claude/runners/spec_runner.py ``` ### Screenshots ### Component Both ### Auto Claude Version _No response_ ### Operating System macOS ### Python Version 3.12 ### Node.js Version (for UI issues) _No response_ ### Additional Context _No response_

title: fix: remove legacy path from auto-claude source detection
body:
## Problem

Auto-Claude UI was displaying error:
```
[ERROR] Spec runner not found at: /Users/jorisslagter/Developer/Tools/auto-claude/auto-claude/runners/spec_runner.py
```

The spec_runner.py actually exists at the correct location in the new monorepo structure:
```
/Users/jorisslagter/Developer/Tools/auto-claude/apps/backend/runners/spec_runner.py
```

## Root Cause

The `detectAutoBuildSourcePath()` function in `agent-process.ts` was checking multiple possible paths and selecting the first one that had `requirements.txt`. The issue was that the **legacy** `auto-claude/` path (from before the monorepo restructure in v2.7.2) was being selected instead of the new `apps/backend/` path.

```typescript
const possiblePaths = [
  path.resolve(__dirname, '..', '..', '..', 'backend'),
  path.resolve(app.getAppPath(), '..', 'backend'),
  path.resolve(process.cwd(), 'apps', 'backend'),
  path.resolve(process.cwd(), 'auto-claude')  // ← This was being selected!
];
```

## Solution

Removed the legacy path from the array completely. Since the project has fully migrated to the new monorepo structure, backwards compatibility with the old structure is not needed.

**Change in `apps/frontend/src/main/agent/agent-process.ts`:**
- Removed line 68: `path.resolve(process.cwd(), 'auto-claude')`
- Removed associated comment

## Impact

After this fix:
- ✅ Path detection correctly identifies: `/path/to/apps/backend/`
- ✅ Spec runner is found at: `/path/to/apps/backend/runners/spec_runner.py`
- ✅ No more "[ERROR] Spec runner not found" messages
- ✅ Forces migration to new monorepo structure
- ✅ Cleaner code - removes dead legacy path

## Testing

title: Config to separate the WHAT from HOW in workflow
body:
### Problem Statement

When working in a corporate environment, and not vibe coding, we want to separate the WHAT and the HOW workflow sometimes. In the current workflow the prompt for the task is interpreted by the AI  

### Proposed Solution

Like BMAD I would like to have the possibility to separate the WHAT and the HOW. In the what I want a detailed spec of what we are trying to do. In a dream situation this would include personas, user stories, user flows, requirements, non-functional requirements and out of scope definitions.
This is then reviewed and accepted. 

I want this step to verify that the task is understood by the developer. So for instance, a "large" issue is raised on the project. The developer or project manager takes the issue and generate a PRD on that issue since it's complex. It then review the prd and maybe also have to verify it with the stakeholder for the project (does it align with the project path, do we have the funding etc)
Maybe it need to have high level about the HOW as well (the refinement)

After the PRD and Refinement is accepted, we then create one or many task to this. We could separate the tasks by domain etc, holding the context to be minimal. One problem here is that the task will probably be dependent on each other, or at least have steps before that sets the entities etc, so that the database task creates the entity with different fields that the UI does.

Maybe this can be a separate board/menu choice that is optional before the tasks? Like insights or something. 

The sweet spot would be an AI interaction, where the AI help the user define the PRD and ask questions that is not clear in the prompt. Again, referencing the BMAD method, where it can add typical PM questions to define the feature in detail.
 

Things to consider
The person doing the PRD isn't the developer in a company. So the prd must be created by one person and then picked up and split into task(s) by another

The acceptance of the PRD from a third party could take time in a large scale project. There is a risk that the refinement and/or prd is slightly out of date. But since the PRD should only answer the WHAT question, and the implementation plan is created when the PRD is creating the task(s), I think it will be ok?

No

Both

title: Fix: Handle paths with spaces in parsePythonCommand
body:
## Problem

The `parsePythonCommand` function in `python-detector.ts` was splitting all Python paths by space:

```typescript
const parts = pythonPath.split(' ');
```

This breaks paths containing spaces, like macOS's default Electron userData path:
```
/Users/name/Library/Application Support/auto-claude-ui/python-venv/bin/python3
```

The path gets split into:
- command: `/Users/name/Library/Application`
- args: `['Support/auto-claude-ui/python-venv/bin/python3']`

This causes `ENOENT` errors when spawning Python processes.

## Solution

Only split by space for simple command names (like `py -3` on Windows). For absolute paths (starting with `/` or a drive letter), preserve the full path.

## Testing

Tested on macOS with the default `~/Library/Application Support/` path - the bug is now fixed.

title: fix: task persistence across app restarts
body:
## Description
Fixes critical task persistence bug that causes API credit waste by restarting completed tasks.

## Related Issues
Fixes #133, partially fixes #117

## Root Cause
**Critical Issue**: Task loading only scanned main project `.auto-claude/specs/`, NOT `.worktrees/{spec-id}/.auto-claude/specs/`

**Impact:**
- User completes 8 tasks → All in human_review (worktrees contain final code)
- App restarts
- getTasks() finds NO tasks (they're all in worktrees)
- UI shows empty task list
- User clicks "resolve" → recovery sees "no progress" → restarts from scratch
- **Massive API credits wasted, duplicate work**

## Changes Made

### 1. Scan Worktrees for Tasks
- Modified `getTasks()` in project-store.ts to scan both main and worktrees
- Created `loadTasksFromSpecsDir()` helper method for reusable task loading
- Added worktree scanning loop: `.worktrees/*/`.auto-claude/specs/

### 2. Task Deduplication
- Deduplicate tasks by ID (same task can exist in both locations)
- Prefer worktree version when duplicate (more recent state)
- Added location tracking for debugging

### 3. Fix Recovery Logic
- Check if all subtasks are completed before resetting
- Don't restart completed tasks waiting for merge
- Only reset truly stuck subtasks (in_progress/failed)
- Prevent API credit waste from unnecessary re-execution

### 4. Add Location Metadata
- Added `location` field to Task interface ('main' | 'worktree')
- Added `specsPath` field for full path to specs directory
- Enables better debugging and future features

## Testing

### Manual Testing Performed
- [x] Created 3 tasks in human_review (all subtasks complete)
- [x] Restarted app
- [x] Verified all 3 tasks still visible in UI
- [x] Task status preserved correctly
- [x] Recovery recognizes completed tasks
- [x] No duplicate work/API credit usage

### Code Coverage
- project-store.ts: Task loading logic
- task.ts: Type definitions
- execution-handlers.ts: Recovery logic

## Before/After

**Before:**
- Tasks in worktrees disappear after restart
- Empty task list after restart
- Clicking "resolve" restarts task from scratch
- **User loses massive API credits**

**After:**
- Tasks load from both main and worktrees
- All tasks visible after restart
- Recovery detects completed tasks
- **No API credit waste**

## Breaking Changes
None - fully backward compatible

## Performance Impact
- Minimal - adds one directory scan per restart
- Deduplication is O(n) where n = number of tasks

## Security Considerations
- No security impact
- Only reads from local filesystem

## Related PRs
- This is part 1 of 4 PRs to fix issues #87, #89, #109, #117, #132, #133

title: fix: settings persistence for Python and auto-build paths
body:
## Description
Fixes settings persistence bugs causing Python path and auto-build path to not persist correctly after app restart.

## Related Issues
Fixes #87, #132

## Root Causes

### Issue #87: Auto-build Source Path Not Configured
- `getEffectiveSourcePath()` validates if path exists on disk
- If configured path doesn't exist anymore, returns null
- Users see error even when settings.json has a value

### Issue #132: Python Path Does Not Save/Load
- Some handlers read settings.json directly with validation
- If path moved/deleted, validation fails and falls back to default
- Python path appears to save but reverts after restart

## Changes Made

### 1. Use AgentManager Instead of Direct File Reads
- `agentManager` is already configured from settings.json at startup
- Changed to use `agentManager.getPythonPath()` instead of re-reading file
- Eliminates redundant file reads and path validation issues

### 2. Add Python Command Parsing
- Use `parsePythonCommand()` to handle various formats
- Supports: `python3`, `py -3`, `/path/to/venv/bin/python`
- Properly splits command and arguments

### 3. Improve Error Handling
- Add stdout/stderr capture for Python analyzer
- Log detailed error messages to console
- Include Python output in error messages
- Better debugging for path resolution issues

### 4. Add Comprehensive Logging
- Log which Python path is being used
- Warn when falling back to defaults
- Show analyzer output for debugging

## Testing

### Manual Testing Performed
- [x] Configure Python path in settings
- [x] Restart app - path persists correctly
- [x] Load project context - uses configured path
- [x] Invalid path - shows clear error with fallback

- Integration with agentManager
- Python command parsing

**Before:**
- Python path read directly from settings.json
- Path validation fails if file moved
- Silent fallback to `python` (doesn't exist on macOS)
- No error details in logs

**After:**
- Python path from agentManager (already loaded)
- Uses configured path reliably
- Falls back to `python3` on macOS
- Detailed error logging with Python output

## Breaking Changes
None - fully backward compatible

## Performance Impact
- Slight improvement - eliminates redundant settings.json reads
- AgentManager already has paths in memory

- Uses existing agentManager security model
