title: fix: handle HTTP 300 errors in update checking (#89)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #89

This PR adds proper handling for HTTP 300 errors that occur when GitHub has both a branch and tag with the same name during update checks.

## Root Cause

- GitHub API returns HTTP 300 "Multiple Choices" when branch and tag have same name
- http-client.ts didn't handle HTTP 300 responses
- Both branch and tag (e.g., v2.6.5) existed simultaneously

## Changes Made

### 1. HTTP Client Updates (`http-client.ts`)
- Add HTTP 300 detection and handling in both `fetchJson()` and `downloadFile()`
- Provide clear error messages indicating branch/tag name collision
- Include issue reporting link for users

### 2. Update Installer (`update-installer.ts`)
- Detect HTTP 300 errors in catch block
- Provide user-friendly error message with manual download link
- Include direct link to GitHub releases page

### 3. Release Validation (`validate-release.js`)
- New script to validate releases before creation
- Check for existing tags with same version name
- Check for local branches with conflicting names
- Check for remote branches with conflicting names
- Exit with error code 1 if conflicts found

### 4. Version Bump Integration (`bump-version.js`)
- Call validate-release.js before creating git commit
- Prevent releases with conflicting branch/tag names
- Add validation step to release workflow

## Testing

- Normal updates continue to work
- HTTP 300 errors show clear message with manual download link
- Validation script prevents future branch/tag conflicts
- Release workflow validates before creating tags

## Impact

- ✅ Zero HTTP 300 errors on updates
- ✅ Clear error messaging directing users to manual download
- ✅ Release workflow prevents future conflicts
- ✅ Better user experience during update failures

title: Docker installation guide for "Ubuntu/Debian" only works on Ubuntu - Debian commands missing
body:
### Bug Description

The Docker installation section labeled "Installing Docker Desktop - Linux (Ubuntu/Debian)" contains Ubuntu-specific commands that will fail on Debian systems.

  ---
  Current Behavior:

  The guide uses hardcoded Ubuntu repository URLs:
  curl -fsSL https://download.docker.com/linux/ubuntu/gpg | sudo gpg --dearmor -o /etc/apt/keyrings/docker.gpg
  echo "deb [arch=$(dpkg --print-architecture) signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/docker.gpg] https://download.docker.com/linux/ubuntu \
    $(. /etc/os-release && echo "$VERSION_CODENAME") stable" | \
    sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/docker.list > /dev/null

  On Debian, this results in a 404 error because the Debian codename (e.g., bookworm) doesn't exist in Docker's Ubuntu repository.



### Expected Behavior

The guide should either:
  1. Provide separate command blocks for Ubuntu and Debian, or
  2. Use a dynamic approach that detects the distro

### Steps to Reproduce

  1. Use a Debian system (e.g., Debian 12 bookworm or Debian 13 trixie)
  2. Follow the "Installing Docker Desktop - Linux (Ubuntu/Debian)" section in guides/DOCKER-SETUP.md
  3. Run the repository setup command:
  echo \
    "deb [arch=$(dpkg --print-architecture) signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/docker.gpg] https://download.docker.com/linux/ubuntu \
    $(. /etc/os-release && echo "$VERSION_CODENAME") stable" | \
    sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/docker.list > /dev/null
  4. Run sudo apt-get update
  5. Observe 404 error because https://download.docker.com/linux/ubuntu/dists/bookworm/ does not exist (Debian codenames are not in the Ubuntu repo)


### Error Messages / Logs

```shell

```

### Screenshots

Not sure

_No response_

Linux

### Python Version

_No response_

_No response_

### Additional Context

Suggested Fix:

  Replace the current commands with distro-aware versions:

  # Detect distro (ubuntu or debian)
  . /etc/os-release
  DISTRO=$ID

  curl -fsSL https://download.docker.com/linux/${DISTRO}/gpg | sudo gpg --dearmor -o /etc/apt/keyrings/docker.gpg
  sudo chmod a+r /etc/apt/keyrings/docker.gpg
  echo \
    "deb [arch=$(dpkg --print-architecture) signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/docker.gpg] https://download.docker.com/linux/${DISTRO} \

title: Error: Auto Claude requires Python 3.10 or higher. You are running Python 3.9.6
body:
### Bug Description

## Issue

Released Binary uses hardcoded /usr/bin/python3 instead of PATH, breaks on macOS

## Description
Auto-Claude fails to launch on macOS even when Python 3.10+ is installed and available in PATH.

## Error Message
```
Error: Auto Claude requires Python 3.10 or higher.
You are running Python 3.9.6
```

## Environment
- **OS:** macOS (Apple Silicon)
- **Python in PATH:** 3.10.9 (Anaconda) / 3.12.12 (Homebrew)
- **System Python:** `/usr/bin/python3` → 3.9.6

## Problem
The binary appears to check `/usr/bin/python3` directly instead of using the system PATH or `#!/usr/bin/env python3`. 

On macOS, `/usr/bin/python3` is controlled by Apple and protected by System Integrity Protection (SIP) - users cannot modify or upgrade it.


### Expected Behavior

## Expected Behavior
Auto-Claude should detect Python using the user's PATH environment, not a hardcoded system path.

## Suggested Fix
Use `#!/usr/bin/env python3` or check `python3` from PATH rather than `/usr/bin/python3`.

## Workaround
Currently the only workaround is to run from source instead of using the pre-built release.

### Steps to Reproduce

**Steps to Reproduce:**

```markdown
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Use an Apple Silicon Mac (M1/M2/M3) running macOS
2. Have Python 3.10+ installed via Homebrew or Anaconda:
   ```bash
   python3 --version  # Shows 3.10+ 
   which python3      # Shows /opt/homebrew/bin/python3 or anaconda path
   ```
3. Download the latest release binary from GitHub Releases
4. Run the Auto-Claude binary
5. Error appears despite having Python 3.10+ installed:
   ```
   Error: Auto Claude requires Python 3.10 or higher.
   You are running Python 3.9.6
   ```

## Root Cause
macOS system Python at `/usr/bin/python3` is locked at 3.9.6 and protected by SIP (System Integrity Protection). The binary checks this path instead of the user's PATH.

```bash
/usr/bin/python3 --version   # 3.9.6 (cannot be changed)

```

title: Auto-Claude bundled Python is 3.9, but requirements need claude-agent-sdk>=0.1.16 (Python 3.10+), so PythonEnvManager never becomes ready on macOS
body:
### Bug Description

On macOS (Apple Silicon), the embedded Python environment that Auto-Claude creates is using Python 3.9.6, but the current  `requirements.txt ` requires  `claude-agent-sdk>=0.1.16`, which only supports **Python 3.10+**. As a result, dependency installation fails and the PythonEnvManager never becomes  `ready` , which then prevents tasks from running and isolated workspaces from being created.
I tried to install it manually from the venv and i got:

```
(python-venv) $ pip install "claude-agent-sdk>=0.1.16"
ERROR: Ignored the following versions that require a different python version: 0.0.23 Requires-Python >=3.10; 0.1.0 Requires-Python >=3.10; 0.1.1 Requires-Python >=3.10; 0.1.10 Requires-Python >=3.10; 0.1.11 Requires-Python >=3.10; 0.1.12 Requires-Python >=3.10; 0.1.13 Requires-Python >=3.10; 0.1.14 Requires-Python >=3.10; 0.1.15 Requires-Python >=3.10; 0.1.16 Requires-Python >=3.10; 0.1.17 Requires-Python >=3.10; 0.1.18 Requires-Python >=3.10; 0.1.2 Requires-Python >=3.10; 0.1.3 Requires-Python >=3.10; 0.1.4 Requires-Python >=3.10; 0.1.5 Requires-Python >=3.10; 0.1.6 Requires-Python >=3.10; 0.1.7 Requires-Python >=3.10; 0.1.8 Requires-Python >=3.10; 0.1.9 Requires-Python >=3.10
ERROR: Could not find a version that satisfies the requirement claude-agent-sdk>=0.1.16 (from versions: none)
ERROR: No matching distribution found for claude-agent-sdk>=0.1.16

(python-venv) $ which python
/Users/<user>/Library/Application Support/auto-claude-ui/python-venv/bin/python

(python-venv) $ python --version
Python 3.9.6
```


This means the app’s own Python (3.9.6) is incompatible with the minimum Python version required by `claude-agent-sdk` (>=3.10), so the install will never succeed in the current bundle.


## Actual behavior

- Auto-Claude creates a venv using Python 3.9.6 under:
  - `/Users/<user>/Library/Application Support/auto-claude-ui/python-venv`
- Installing dependencies fails with “No matching distribution found for claude-agent-sdk>=0.1.16”.
- `depsInstalled` remains `false`, `ready` remains `false`.
- Attempting to run the first task leads to failures like “No isolated workspace” because the agent runtime never initializes.

## Environment

- Auto-Claude: latest release at time of filing (2.7.x)
- OS: macOS (Apple Silicon)
- Auto-Claude embedded Python:
  - `Python 3.9.6` at `/Users/<user>/Library/Application Support/auto-claude-ui/python-venv/bin/python`
- GitHub CLI: installed and working from normal terminals (not directly related to this specific bug)

## Suggested fix

- Rebuild the macOS release so that the bundled Python is **3.10+** (ideally 3.11), consistent with `claude-agent-sdk`’s `Requires-Python` on PyPI.
- Optionally provide a setting to let advanced users point Auto-Claude at an external Python 3.10+ installation instead of the bundled one, to avoid this class of mismatch in the future.



### Expected Behavior

- The embedded Python runtime that Auto-Claude ships with on macOS should be **>= 3.10**, matching the requirements of `claude-agent-sdk>=0.1.16`.
- Alternatively, Auto-Claude should allow configuring an external Python 3.10+ interpreter instead of the bundled 3.9.x one.
- After Python and deps are compatible:
  - `[PythonEnvManager] depsInstalled` should become `true`.
  - The Python environment should be `ready: true`.
  - Tasks should run and isolated workspaces / worktrees should be created correctly.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. On macOS (Apple Silicon), download and install the latest Auto-Claude release (2.7.x at the time of filing).
2. Launch Auto-Claude and let it bootstrap its Python environment.
3. Either:
   - Let Auto-Claude install dependencies automatically (it fails), or
   - Manually activate the venv and run:
     ```
     source "/Users/<user>/Library/Application Support/auto-claude-ui/python-venv/bin/activate"
     pip install "claude-agent-sdk>=0.1.16"
     python --version  # shows 3.9.6
     ```
4. Observe the pip error about all versions of `claude-agent-sdk` requiring Python >= 3.10 and “No matching distribution found”.
5. Back in Auto-Claude, try to run a task; note that the Python environment is not ready and isolated workspace creation fails.


### Screenshots

_No response_

### Component

Python Backend (auto-claude/)

### Auto Claude Version

v2.7.1

### Operating System

macOS

title: fix: Add Python 3.10+ version validation and GitHub Actions Python setup (#180 #167)
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes critical bug #180 and #167 where macOS users with default Python 3.9.6 couldn't use Auto-Claude because `claude-agent-sdk` requires Python 3.10+.

## Root Cause Analysis

The investigation revealed that Auto-Claude:
- **Does NOT bundle Python** - relies entirely on system Python
- Had **no version validation** - accepted any Python 3.x
- **macOS default**: Ships with Python 3.9.6 (incompatible with claude-agent-sdk >=0.1.16)
- **GitHub Actions**: Build workflows didn't explicitly set Python version

This caused the following error chain:
```
System has Python 3.9.6
→ PythonEnvManager creates venv with 3.9.6
→ Tries to install claude-agent-sdk>=0.1.16
→ Fails: "No matching distribution found" (requires Python 3.10+)
→ depsInstalled = false, ready = false
→ Tasks can't run, workspaces can't be created
→ ModuleNotFoundError: dotenv (can't install any dependencies)
```

## Changes

### 1. `apps/frontend/src/main/python-detector.ts`

Added version validation functions:
- `getPythonVersion()` - Extracts version from `python --version` output
- `validatePythonVersion()` - Checks if Python >= 3.10.0
- Updated `findPythonCommand()` to validate versions and skip Python < 3.10 with clear error messages

**Before**: Accepted any Python 3.x
```typescript
if (version.includes('Python 3')) {
  return cmd;
}
```

**After**: Validates minimum version requirement
```typescript
const validation = validatePythonVersion(cmd);
if (validation.valid) {
  console.log(`[Python] Found valid Python: ${cmd} (${validation.version})`);
  return cmd;
} else {
  console.warn(`[Python] ${cmd} version too old: ${validation.message}`);
  continue;
}
```

### 2. `apps/frontend/src/main/python-env-manager.ts`

- Imported and used `findPythonCommand()` (which now has built-in version validation)
- Simplified `findSystemPython()` to use shared validation logic (removed 50+ lines of duplicate code)
- Updated error message from "Python 3.9+" to "Python 3.10+" with download link

**Before**:
```typescript
this.emit('error', 'Python 3 not found. Please install Python 3.9+');
```

**After**:
```typescript
this.emit(
  'error',
  'Python 3.10+ not found. Please install Python 3.10 or higher (required by claude-agent-sdk).\n\n' +
  'Download: https://www.python.org/downloads/'
);
```

### 3. `.github/workflows/release.yml`

Added Python 3.11 setup to **all 4 build jobs**:
- `build-macos-intel`
- `build-macos-arm64`
- `build-windows`
- `build-linux`

```yaml
- name: Setup Python
  uses: actions/setup-python@v5
  with:
    python-version: '3.11'
```

This ensures consistent Python version across all platforms during CI/CD builds.

## Impact

✅ **macOS users with Python 3.9**: Now see clear error message with download link
✅ **macOS users with Python 3.10+**: Work normally  
✅ **CI/CD builds**: Use consistent Python 3.11 across all platforms
✅ **Error prevention**: Stops "ModuleNotFoundError: dotenv" and dependency install failures at the source

## Testing

- [x] Code review - all changes match implementation plan
- [x] TypeScript syntax validated
- [x] Version comparison logic tested (3.9 < 3.10, 3.10 >= 3.10, 3.11 >= 3.10)
- [x] Error messages include clear download link
- [x] All 4 GitHub Actions jobs updated consistently

## Files Changed

- `.github/workflows/release.yml` - Added Python 3.11 setup to all build jobs
- `apps/frontend/src/main/python-detector.ts` - Added version validation functions
- `apps/frontend/src/main/python-env-manager.ts` - Use validated Python, improved error message

## Closes

Fixes #180  
Fixes #167

title: fix(core): add global spec numbering lock to prevent collisions

Implements distributed file-based locking for spec number coordination across main project and all worktrees. Previously, parallel spec creation could assign the same number to different specs (e.g., 042-bmad-task and 042-gitlab-integration both using number 042).

The fix adds SpecNumberLock class that:
- Acquires exclusive lock before calculating spec numbers
- Scans ALL locations (main project + worktrees) for global maximum
- Creates spec directories atomically within the lock
- Handles stale locks via PID-based detection with 30s timeout

Applied to both Python backend (spec_runner.py flow) and TypeScript frontend (ideation conversion, GitHub/GitLab issue import).

title: feat: created autoclaude container
body: ## Summary This PR introduces an **enterprise-grade Docker deployment** of Auto-Claude, transforming the single-user Electron desktop app into a containerized **multi-tenant web platform** with JWT authentication, real-time collaboration, and advanced credential management. This is a **complete architectural reimagining** (not a wrapper) that shares only the core Auto-Claude CLI (`auto-claude/`) for task execution while providing: - Multi-user web access via FastAPI + React - PostgreSQL-backed persistence - 3-tier credential hierarchy (Global → User → Project) - Enterprise SSO/OIDC support - Real-time WebSocket communication - Secure terminal sessions via PTY - Multi-provider Graphiti memory with FalkorDB ## Type of Change - [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [X] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change) - [X] Documentation update - [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes) - [ ] Tests (adding or updating tests) ## Related Issues Part of broader effort to enable team collaboration on Auto-Claude projects. ## Changes Made ### Docker Deployment (`docker/`) **Backend (FastAPI + Python 3.11)** - 17 route modules (~9,500 lines) for REST API + WebSocket - JWT authentication with access/refresh tokens (30min/30day expiry) - Async SQLAlchemy ORM with PostgreSQL 16 - Build runner with subprocess management - Fernet credential encryption at rest - WebSocket event broadcasting for real-time updates - 14 service modules (auth, projects, specs, builds, credentials, etc.) **Frontend (React 19 + Vite)** - 342+ components ported from Electron app - Zustand state management - Tailwind CSS 4 + shadcn/ui components - xterm.js terminal emulation - WebSocket integration for live logs/status - Same UI/UX as desktop app (Kanban, terminals, file explorer) **Database (PostgreSQL 16 + FalkorDB)** - 5 Alembic migrations - 8 database tables (users, projects, credentials, settings, tokens) - User accounts with role-based access (admin/user) - Encrypted credential storage (3-tier hierarchy) - Project management with user scoping - Refresh token revocation system **Infrastructure** - Multi-stage Dockerfile (Node.js builder → Python runtime) - Docker Compose stack (web, postgres, falkordb, graphiti-mcp) - Health checks for all services - Entrypoint script with Claude CLI setup automation - Production-ready with reverse proxy examples (Nginx, Traefik, Caddy) - Security: non-root user, bubblewrap terminal sandboxing, SYS_ADMIN capability ### Key Features **Multi-User Authentication** - JWT-based with bcrypt password hashing (work factor 12+) - Invitation-only registration system - Admin can create invite codes - Token lifecycle: 30min access tokens, 30day refresh tokens - Logout with immediate token revocation **3-Tier Credential Hierarchy** Global (SystemSettings) → Admin sets company-wide credentials ↓ (if not locked) User (UserCredentials) → User's default API keys ↓ Project (ProjectCredentials) → Per-project overrides - All credentials encrypted at rest with Fernet - Admin can lock credentials to prevent user overrides - Supports: Claude OAuth, Anthropic API, OpenAI, GitHub, Linear, Voyage AI, Google AI, Azure OpenAI **Enterprise Features** - **SSO/OIDC**: Full OpenID Connect support (Okta, Auth0, Azure AD, Google Workspace, Keycloak) - **SMTP Integration**: Automated invitation emails - **Debug Endpoints**: Credential flow verification for troubleshooting - **Admin Console**: User management, invitation system, global settings **Multi-Provider Graphiti Memory** - OpenAI (default) - Anthropic + Voyage AI (highest quality) - Google AI (Gemini) - Azure OpenAI (enterprise) - Ollama (fully offline/local) **Per-Project Agent Profiles** - Customize models per agent phase (planner, coder, QA) - Thinking level (standard vs extended) - Complexity settings (simple/standard/complex) - Memory backend (file-based, Graphiti, or both) - Git settings (auto-commit, auto-push) - Parallel subtasks control (1-10) - QA strict mode - Recovery attempts **Real-Time Features** - WebSocket build log streaming - Task status broadcasts (planning → coding → QA) - Multi-client support (all users see updates) - Interactive PTY terminal sessions via WebSocket ### Documentation **Comprehensive README.md** (1,698 lines) - Architecture diagrams with component breakdown - Quick start guide (5-minute setup) - Complete environment variable reference (50+ variables) - Deployment scenarios: - Local development - Team deployment (internal network) - Production (with Nginx/Traefik/Caddy examples) - Cloud deployment (AWS EC2, DigitalOcean, GCE) - API reference with HTTP examples - Security model (4-layer defense) - Troubleshooting guide (7 common issues) - Migration guide from desktop app **Environment Template** - `.env.example` with all 50+ variables documented - Examples for each Graphiti provider - Security key generation commands - Production vs development configurations **Security** - `.gitignore` configured to exclude `.env`, logs, databases - No secrets in commits (verified) - All API keys in `.env.example` are placeholders only ## Screenshots ### Invite System ### User Registration ### Admin Users Projects ### Test Users Projects - Showing Project seperation from Admin ### Login Page ### Test User - Project View ### SMTP Test Will add more screenshots soon. ## Work-in-Progress / Known Limitations ### ⚠️ Transparency Note This PR represents a **functional but incomplete** implementation. I'm submitting early to: 1. Get the work on the radar (repo evolves rapidly with many PRs) 2. Gather feedback on architecture/approach before investing more time 3. Collaborate on remaining items with maintainers ### 🔧 Known Items Needing Work - [ ] **Theme Integration**: Adopt built-in themes from base app (currently uses default styling) - [ ] **End-to-End Testing**: Need comprehensive integration test suite - [ ] **Feature Parity Validation**: Ensure all Electron features work in web context - [ ] **Performance Testing**: Load testing for concurrent users - [ ] **Migration Script**: Automated migration tool from desktop app data - [ ] **CI/CD Integration**: GitHub Actions workflow for Docker image builds - [ ] **Pre-commit Hooks**: Manual cleanup done, full pre-commit suite not run yet ### ✅ What's Tested & Working - [X] Docker Compose stack starts successfully - [X] PostgreSQL migrations run without errors - [X] JWT authentication flow (login, token refresh, logout) - [X] User registration with invite codes - [X] Admin user management and invitation system - 1,698-line comprehensive README.md with architecture, deployment, API docs - [X] My code follows the project's code style - **Status**: Follows FastAPI + React best practices, manual formatting applied ## Testing ### Manual Testing Performed ```bash # Local deployment test cd docker cp .env.example .env # Added test OAuth token from: claude setup-token # Generated secrets with: openssl rand -base64 32 / openssl rand -hex 32 docker compose up -d docker compose ps # All services healthy ``` # Feature testing: ✅ First-time setup (admin account creation on first access) ✅ User registration with invite codes (invite-only system) ✅ Admin dashboard (user CRUD, invitation management, global credentials) ✅ Project cloning (tested public GitHub repo) ✅ Project cloning with private repo (using GitHub token in credentials) ✅ Task creation from project view ✅ Autonomous build execution (spec creation → coding → QA) ✅ Real-time log streaming (WebSocket updates as build runs) ✅ Terminal sessions (interactive PTY via xterm.js) ✅ Credential hierarchy (set global, user, and project-level credentials) ✅ Multi-provider Graphiti (tested OpenAI and Ollama configurations) ✅ JWT token refresh (30min access, 30day refresh) ✅ Logout with token revocation ✅ Database persistence across container restarts ✅ Health endpoint (/health returns 200 OK) # Tested browsers: ✅ Chrome/Chromium ✅ Firefox ✅ Safari (WebSocket works correctly) # Tested deployment scenarios: ✅ Local (http://localhost:8080) ✅ Reverse proxy (Nginx with HTTPS) Automated Testing Needed - Backend API tests (pytest with FastAPI TestClient) - Frontend component tests (Vitest) - E2E workflow tests - Load testing for concurrent users (Locust/k6) - Security penetration testing # Additional Notes Architecture Decisions Why FastAPI over Electron IPC? - Enables true multi-user access (not possible with Electron) - RESTful API allows future mobile/CLI clients - WebSocket for real-time without Electron's overhead - Easier to deploy and scale horizontally Why PostgreSQL over JSON files? - ACID compliance for user data integrity - Concurrent access support (multiple users simultaneously) - Proper user/role isolation with database-level security - Alembic migrations for schema evolution Why separate from desktop app? - Different use case: team collaboration vs. individual use - Allows both to evolve independently - Shares core CLI (auto-claude/) for consistency - Desktop users unaffected by multi-user complexity Target Deployment Scenarios This deployment addresses use cases not served by the desktop app: - title: Python subprocess hangs on import when spawned from Electron (macOS)
body:
# Python Subprocess Hangs on Import When Spawned from Electron (macOS)

## Summary
Python subprocess spawned by Electron hangs indefinitely during module imports, causing 60-second timeout and task failures with "Task Incomplete - Process likely crashed during spec creation (0/0 subtasks)".

## Environment
- **OS**: macOS (Darwin 24.3.0)
- **Auto-Claude Version**: 2.7.1
- **Python Version**: 3.9.6 (system), 3.12.12 (venv)
- **Node/Electron**: Electron 39.2.7
- **Affected Component**: spec_runner.py execution via agent-process.ts and agent-queue.ts

## Symptoms
1. Task starts but produces **no output for 60 seconds**
2. Timeout triggers: `[TIMEOUT] Python subprocess hung (no output for 60s), killing process`
3. UI shows: "Task Incomplete - This task has a spec and implementation plan but never completed any subtasks (0/0)"
4. Error state: "No Workspace Found - No isolated workspace was found for this task"

## Root Cause
**`sys.stdout.isatty()` and `sys.stdin.isatty()` block indefinitely** when:
- Python is spawned as subprocess from Electron
- stdout/stderr are pipes (not TTY)
- UI modules (`ui/capabilities.py`) execute capability checks at module import time

### Technical Details
When Electron spawns Python subprocess with:
```typescript
spawn(pythonCommand, [...args], {
  env: { PYTHONUNBUFFERED: '1', ... }
})
```

The Python process imports `runners/spec_runner.py` → `ui` module → `ui/capabilities.py`, which executes at module level:
```python
# Lines 117-121 in ui/capabilities.py
FANCY_UI = _is_fancy_ui_enabled()
UNICODE = supports_unicode()
COLOR = supports_color()  # Calls sys.stdout.isatty()
INTERACTIVE = supports_interactive()  # Calls sys.stdin.isatty()
```

On macOS, `isatty()` on piped file descriptors can **block in subprocess context** instead of returning False.

## Reproduction Steps
1. Create new task in Auto-Claude UI
2. Click "Start Task" or "Resume Task"
3. Observe logs: Process spawns but produces no output
4. After 60 seconds: timeout error appears
5. Task status changes to "human_review" with 0/0 subtasks

## Workaround/Fix
Add environment variable to disable fancy UI features when spawning Python:

**File: `src/main/agent/agent-process.ts` (line 188)**
```typescript
env: {
  ...process.env,
  ...extraEnv,
  ...profileEnv,
  PYTHONUNBUFFERED: '1',
  PYTHONIOENCODING: 'utf-8',
  PYTHONUTF8: '1',
  ENABLE_FANCY_UI: 'false'  // ← ADD THIS
}
```

**File: `src/main/agent/agent-queue.ts` (lines 229, 476 - 2 locations)**
```typescript
const finalEnv = {
  ...process.env,
  ...combinedEnv,
  ...profileEnv,
  PYTHONPATH: autoBuildSource || '',
  PYTHONUNBUFFERED: '1',
  PYTHONIOENCODING: 'utf-8',
  PYTHONUTF8: '1',
  ENABLE_FANCY_UI: 'false'  // ← ADD THIS
};
```

**Additional Safety: `auto-claude/ui/capabilities.py` (lines 85-95, 107-114)**
Wrap `isatty()` calls in try-except:
```python
def supports_color() -> bool:
    """Check if terminal supports ANSI colors."""
    if not _is_fancy_ui_enabled():
        return False
    # ... existing checks ...
    try:
        if not hasattr(sys.stdout, "isatty"):
            return False
        is_tty = sys.stdout.isatty()
        if not is_tty:
            return False
    except (AttributeError, OSError, ValueError):
        # isatty() can block in subprocess context
        return False
    # ... rest of function
```

## Python Version Compatibility Issue
**File: `runners/spec_runner.py` (line 39)**

Current code requires Python 3.10+:
```python
if sys.version_info < (3, 10):
    sys.exit("Error: Auto Claude requires Python 3.10 or higher...")
```

Should be lowered to 3.9 (or document the 3.10+ requirement in README).

## Related Issues
- #214 - "Python environment not ready: Already initializing" (may be related)
- #132 - Python path configuration issues
- #130 - Windows 11 stuck in "thinking..."

## Impact
- **Critical**: Blocks all task execution on affected systems
- **Scope**: macOS systems with Python 3.9, possibly other platforms
- **User Experience**: Tasks appear to hang with no feedback

## Suggested Long-term Fix
1. Use lazy imports for UI modules in spec_runner.py
2. Avoid module-level code execution in ui/__init__.py
3. Implement timeout wrapper for subprocess.isatty() calls
4. Add pre-flight check: test Python subprocess import before spawning tasks

## Testing
After applying workaround, verify:
```bash
ENABLE_FANCY_UI=false python3 -c "from ui import capabilities; print('OK')"
```
Should complete instantly without hanging.

title: Security profile created after agent starts in worktrees, blocking npm/jest commands
body:
## Bug Description

Security profile (`.auto-claude-security.json`) is created **after** the agent session starts in worktrees, causing commands like `npm` and `jest` to be blocked during the initial phase of execution.

## Environment

- **Auto-Claude Version**: 2.7.1
- **OS**: Linux (Debian 13)
- **Project Type**: TypeScript/JavaScript (npm-based)
- **Git Worktrees**: Yes

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have a TypeScript/JavaScript project with `package.json` and `package-lock.json` in the main branch
2. Create a new Auto-Claude spec
3. Auto-Claude creates a git worktree and starts an agent session
4. Agent attempts to run `npm test` or `jest` commands within the first ~20-25 minutes
5. Commands are blocked with error: `Command 'npm' is not in the allowed commands for this project`

## Expected Behavior

- Security profile should be created **before** the agent session starts
- All package manager commands detected from the project (npm, npx) should be available immediately
- Worktrees should inherit or receive the security profile from the main project

## Actual Behavior

**Timeline from actual logs:**
```
20:25:27 UTC - Worktree session starts
20:25:53 UTC - npm command blocked: "Command 'npm' is not in the allowed commands"
20:26:06 UTC - jest command blocked: "Command 'jest' is not in the allowed commands"
20:48:25 UTC - Security profile finally created (23 minutes later!)
```

The agent session begins before the security profile is analyzed and created, causing legitimate commands to be blocked.

## Root Cause Analysis

1. When a worktree is created via `git worktree add`, only **tracked files** are checked out
2. `.auto-claude-security.json` is typically **not tracked** (ignored via `.gitignore`)
3. Auto-Claude's `get_or_create_profile()` is called during agent initialization, but this happens:
   - Asynchronously
   - After the agent has already started executing
   - Can take 20+ minutes depending on project size
4. During this gap, commands fall back to a minimal allowlist that doesn't include detected package managers

## Impact

- **High**: Breaks automated testing and build verification in specs
- Agents cannot run verification commands specified in `implementation_plan.json`
- Forces manual workarounds (using `npx` instead of direct commands, or waiting 20+ minutes)
- Reduces autonomous capability of the system

## Workaround

**User-side workaround:**
```bash
# Track the security profile in git
git add -f .auto-claude-security.json
git commit -m "chore: track Auto-Claude security profile for worktrees"
```

This ensures worktrees get the security profile immediately.

**Alternative workaround:**
Add commonly-blocked commands to `custom_commands` in the security profile:
```json
"custom_commands": ["jest", "vitest", "mocha", "ava"]
```

## Proposed Fix

**Option 1: Pre-create security profile during worktree setup** (Recommended)

In `core/worktree.py`, after creating the worktree (line ~330), immediately analyze and create the security profile:

```python
def create_worktree(self, spec_name: str) -> WorktreeInfo:
    # ... existing worktree creation code ...
    
    # Immediately create security profile for worktree
    from project_analyzer import get_or_create_profile
    get_or_create_profile(worktree_path)
    
    return WorktreeInfo(...)
```

**Option 2: Block agent start until profile is ready**

Ensure `get_or_create_profile()` completes synchronously before starting the agent session.

**Option 3: Copy security profile from main project**

If the main project has a security profile, copy it to the worktree:
```python
main_profile = project_dir / '.auto-claude-security.json'
worktree_profile = worktree_path / '.auto-claude-security.json'
if main_profile.exists() and not worktree_profile.exists():
    shutil.copy(main_profile, worktree_profile)
```

## Additional Context

The security profile correctly detects npm/npx when it's finally created - the issue is purely timing-related. The detection logic works fine; it just needs to run **before** the agent starts executing commands.

**Logged errors from task_logs.json:**
- Line 636: `"detail": "Command 'npm' is not in the allowed commands for this project"`
- Line 696: `"detail": "Command 'jest' is not in the allowed commands for this project"`

## Related Files

- `core/worktree.py` - Worktree creation
- `project/analyzer.py` - Security profile creation
- `agents/session.py` - Agent session initialization
- `security/hooks.py` - Command validation

## Labels Suggestion

`bug`, `priority/high`, `area/security`, `area/worktrees`

title: Python venv creation fails with Python 3.9 - claude-agent-sdk requires Python 3.10+
body:
## Description

When starting the Auto Claude UI for the first time, the Python environment initialization fails with the error:

```
Failed to run merge: spawn /Users/.../auto-claude/.venv/bin/python ENOENT
```

This occurs because the `claude-agent-sdk` package requires Python 3.10+, but the system may have Python 3.9 as the default, causing the virtual environment setup to fail.

## Root Cause

1. The `requirements.txt` specifies `claude-agent-sdk>=0.1.16`
2. This package requires Python 3.10 or higher
3. If the system's default `python3` is version 3.9.x, the venv creation succeeds but dependency installation fails
4. The Electron UI then tries to use a non-existent or incomplete Python environment

## Impact

- First-time setup fails silently
- Users see cryptic `ENOENT` errors when trying to use features like merge, QA, or autonomous builds
- The UI appears to work but backend operations fail

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have Python 3.9.x as your system's default `python3`
2. Clone the Auto-Claude repository
3. Launch the Electron UI (`npm start` in `auto-claude-ui/`)
4. The UI starts but any backend operation fails with `ENOENT` error
5. Checking the venv reveals missing packages:
   ```bash
   cd auto-claude
   .venv/bin/pip list | grep claude-agent-sdk
   # Returns nothing - installation failed
   ```

## Proposed Solutions

### Option 1: Check Python Version in Setup Script (Recommended)

Add a Python version check in `auto-claude-ui/src/main/python-env-manager.ts`:

```typescript
private async validatePythonVersion(pythonCommand: string): Promise<boolean> {
  try {
    const result = await execAsync(\`\${pythonCommand} --version\`);
    const match = result.stdout.match(/Python (\d+)\.(\d+)/);
    if (match) {
      const major = parseInt(match[1]);
      const minor = parseInt(match[2]);
      return major === 3 && minor >= 10;
    }
  } catch (error) {
    return false;
  }
  return false;
}
```

Then use this before creating the venv and show a clear error message to users if their Python is too old.

### Option 2: Auto-detect Higher Python Version

Modify the Python detection logic to prefer Python 3.10+ when available:

```typescript
// In python-detector.ts or python-env-manager.ts
const pythonVersions = ['python3.13', 'python3.12', 'python3.11', 'python3.10', 'python3'];
for (const cmd of pythonVersions) {
  if (await isPythonAvailable(cmd)) {
    const version = await getPythonVersion(cmd);
    if (version >= 3.10) {
      return cmd;
    }
  }
}
```

### Option 3: Better Error Messages

At minimum, improve error handling to show:
- Which Python version was used
- Which package installation failed
- Clear instructions to install Python 3.10+

## Environment

- **OS**: macOS 14+ (also affects Linux/Windows with Python 3.9)
- **Default Python**: 3.9.6
- **Available Python**: 3.12.12 (installed via Homebrew)
- **Auto Claude UI**: v2.6.0

## Workaround for Users

If you encounter this issue:

1. Check if you have Python 3.10+ installed:
   ```bash
   python3.12 --version  # or python3.11, python3.10
   ```

2. If yes, manually create the venv with the correct Python version:
   ```bash
   cd auto-claude
   rm -rf .venv  # Remove failed venv
   python3.12 -m venv .venv  # Use Python 3.12
   .venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt
   ```

3. If no, install Python 3.10+:
   - **macOS (Homebrew)**: `brew install python@3.12`
   - **Ubuntu/Debian**: `sudo apt install python3.12 python3.12-venv`
   - **Windows**: Download from [python.org](https://www.python.org/downloads/)

## Additional Context

The `requirements.txt` also includes optional packages that require Python 3.12+:
- `real_ladybug>=0.13.0; python_version >= "3.12"`
- `graphiti-core>=0.5.0; python_version >= "3.12"`

Using Python 3.12 enables all features. Consider documenting this as the recommended version.

## Documentation Update Needed

The `README.md` currently states:
> Prerequisites: Python 3.8+

This should be updated to:
> Prerequisites: Python 3.10+ (Python 3.12+ recommended for all features)

title: "I've Installed It" button in GitHub CLI modal does nothing - modal keeps reloading

body:
## Description

When generating ideas in the Ideation view for one project, switching to another project tab does not close or hide the "Generating Ideas" panel. The panel remains visible and active even though the user has switched to a different project context.

This behavior is inconsistent with other views like Kanban Board and Agent Terminals, which properly handle tab switching.

## Current Behavior

1. Open Project A (e.g., "redwoodsdk-template-private-tob-as")
2. Navigate to **Ideation** view (sidebar)
3. Click "Generate Ideas" or similar action
4. See "Generating Ideas - 0/3 complete" panel with progress
5. Switch to Project B tab (e.g., "tob-caps")
6. **Expected**: Panel closes or switches context to Project B
7. **Actual**: "Generating Ideas" panel for Project A remains visible in Project B's view

## Expected Behavior

When switching between project tabs, the Ideation generation panel should:

**Option 1 (Recommended)**: Hide/close and show a notification that idea generation is still running in the background for Project A

**Option 2**: Switch context to show Project B's ideation status (if applicable)

**Option 3**: Prevent tab switching while generation is in progress (show warning)

## Comparison with Other Views

Other views handle tab switching correctly:

- **Kanban Board**: Switches to the new project's kanban immediately
- **Agent Terminals**: Shows the new project's terminals
- **Insights**: Switches to new project context
- **Roadmap**: Updates to show new project's roadmap

Only **Ideation** view has this issue where the active operation panel persists across projects.

## Impact

- **Confusing UX**: Users see Project A's generation panel while viewing Project B
- **Potential Data Corruption**: User might think ideas are being generated for Project B when they're actually for Project A
- **Cannot access Project B's Ideation**: The persistent panel blocks access to Project B's ideation features
- **Inconsistent Behavior**: Breaks user expectations set by other views

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Add two projects to Auto Claude (Project A and Project B)
2. Open Project A tab
3. Navigate to **Ideation** in the sidebar
4. Click to generate ideas (starts the generation process)
5. Immediately switch to Project B tab (click the tab at the top)
6. Observe that "Generating Ideas" panel from Project A is still visible
7. Try accessing Ideation features for Project B - they're blocked by Project A's panel

## Environment

- **Auto Claude UI**: v2.6.0
- **OS**: macOS (likely affects all platforms)
- **Projects**: Multiple projects added to the workspace

## Technical Details

The issue appears to be in the Ideation component's state management. Possible causes:

1. **Global State**: Ideation panel state is stored globally rather than per-project
2. **Missing Cleanup**: No cleanup/unmount logic when switching tabs
3. **Event Listeners**: Component doesn't listen to tab switch events
4. **React State**: Component state persists across different project contexts

## Suggested Solutions

### Option 1: Project-Scoped State (Recommended)

Store ideation generation state per project:

```typescript
// In ideation state management
interface IdeationState {
  [projectId: string]: {
    isGenerating: boolean;
    progress: number;
    ideas: Idea[];
  };
}

// When switching tabs
const currentProjectIdeation = ideationState[activeProjectId];
```

### Option 2: Cleanup on Tab Switch

Add cleanup logic when project tab changes:

```typescript
useEffect(() => {
  return () => {
    // Cleanup when component unmounts or project changes
    if (isGenerating) {
      // Option A: Cancel generation
      cancelIdeaGeneration();
      
      // Option B: Move to background with notification
      moveToBackgroundGeneration(projectId);
    }
  };
}, [activeProjectId]);
```

### Option 3: Background Operations Manager

Create a global background operations manager:

```typescript
// Show persistent notification for background operations
<BackgroundOperations>
  {backgroundTasks.map(task => (
    <TaskNotification 
      key={task.id}
      task={task}
      onView={() => switchToProject(task.projectId)}
      onCancel={() => cancelTask(task.id)}
    />
  ))}
</BackgroundOperations>
```

### Option 4: Modal Approach

Make the generation process a modal dialog that:
- Stays visible across tab switches (clearly labeled with project name)
- Can be minimized to a corner notification
- Allows cancellation

## Proposed Fix Locations

Based on the codebase structure:

- `auto-claude-ui/src/renderer/src/components/Ideation/` - Main component
- `auto-claude-ui/src/renderer/src/stores/` - State management
- `auto-claude-ui/src/renderer/src/layouts/ProjectLayout.tsx` - Tab switching logic

## Workaround

Currently, users must:
1. Wait for idea generation to complete before switching tabs
2. Or click "Stop" to cancel generation, then switch tabs
3. Refresh the app to clear the stuck panel (loses progress)

## Related Issues

This might be related to other background operation handling, such as:
- Running autonomous tasks in Kanban
- Agent terminal sessions
- QA review processes

Consider implementing a unified background operations system for all async operations.

## Additional Context

See attached screenshots showing:
1. Project A with "Generating Ideas" panel active
2. Switched to Project B tab - panel still visible
3. Expected behavior: panel should be hidden or contextualized

title: Task status 'In Progress' not persisting after page refresh during spec creation/planning
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched existing issues and this hasn't been reported

### Area

Frontend

### Operating System

Linux (also affects Windows/macOS)

### Version

2.7.1

### What happened?

When a task starts (spec creation or planning phase), the UI initially shows it as "In Progress". However, after refreshing the page (Ctrl+R), the task reverts to showing the "Start" button, even though the task is still actively running in the background.

**Root Cause:**

The `determineTaskStatusAndReason()` function in `auto-claude-ui/src/main/project-store.ts` (lines 498-503) has overly strict validation logic. It rejects `status: "in_progress"` from `implementation_plan.json` when there are no subtasks created yet, which is common during spec creation/planning phases.

The validation checks:
```typescript
const isStoredStatusValid =
  (storedStatus === calculatedStatus) ||  // ← Fails: 'in_progress' != 'backlog'
  (storedStatus === 'human_review' && calculatedStatus === 'ai_review') ||
  (storedStatus === 'human_review' && isPlanReviewStage) ||
  (isActiveProcessStatus && storedStatus === 'in_progress'); // ← Only works for "planning"/"coding" planStatus
```

Since `calculatedStatus` is `'backlog'` (no subtasks yet), validation fails and the UI falls back to showing "backlog" status with a "Start" button.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create and start a new task (click "Start" button)
2. Task begins spec creation phase (status shows "In Progress" in UI)
3. Refresh the browser window (Ctrl+R or F5)
4. **Bug:** Task now shows "Start" button again (incorrect - task is still running)
5. Verify `implementation_plan.json` shows `"status": "in_progress"` (correct)
6. Verify Python backend process is still running (correct)

### Expected behavior

Task should continue showing "In Progress" status after page refresh when the task is actively running, regardless of whether subtasks have been created yet.

The explicit `status` field in `implementation_plan.json` should be trusted during early task phases (spec creation, planning) before subtasks are generated.

### Proposed Fix

Add one additional validation case in `project-store.ts` at line 502-503:

```typescript
const isStoredStatusValid =
  (storedStatus === calculatedStatus) ||
  (storedStatus === 'human_review' && calculatedStatus === 'ai_review') ||
  (storedStatus === 'human_review' && isPlanReviewStage) ||
  (isActiveProcessStatus && storedStatus === 'in_progress') ||
  (storedStatus === 'in_progress' && (plan.status as string) === 'in_progress'); // Trust explicit in_progress status from plan file
```

**Testing:**
- All existing tests pass (477 tests green)
- TypeScript type checking passes
- Manual testing confirms task status persists across refresh

### Logs / Screenshots

**implementation_plan.json (on disk - correct):**
```json
{
  "status": "in_progress",
  "planStatus": "in_progress",
  "updated_at": "2025-12-24T13:28:24.221Z",
  "phases": []
}
```

**UI behavior:**
- Before refresh: Shows "In Progress" ✓
- After refresh: Shows "Start" button ✗ (reads from disk but rejects the status)

**Process verification:**
```bash
$ ps aux | grep spec_runner
python /path/to/auto-claude/runners/spec_runner.py --task ... # ← Still running
```

### Related Issues

This appears related to the broader status persistence issues:
- #243 - Task status Done not persisting (always back to Human Review)
- #133, #214, #216, #226 - Other status-related issues

The difference is this bug occurs during **task startup** (spec/planning phase), while #243 occurs during **task completion** (merge phase).

Bumps [jsdom](https://github.com/jsdom/jsdom) from 26.1.0 to 27.3.0.
Release notes

Sourced from jsdom's releases.

Version 27.3.0

  • Improved CSS parsing and CSSOM object APIs via updates to @acemir/cssom. (acemir)

Version 27.2.0

  • Added CSSGroupingRule, CSSNestedDeclarations, CSSConditionRule, CSSContainerRule, CSSScopeRule, CSSSupportsRule, CSSLayerBlockRule, and CSSLayerStatementRule to jsdom Windows. (acemir)
  • Improved CSS parsing and CSSOM object APIs via updates to @acemir/cssom. (acemir)
  • Fixed @import-ed stylesheets to be properly exposed to CSSOM, and not to overwrite the sheet created from the <link> or <style> element. (acemir)

Version 27.1.0

  • Improved CSS parsing by switching to @acemir/cssom, including support for nested selectors, nested declarations, layer statements, and improved at-rule validation. (acemir)
  • Fixed some selector cache invalidation issues where changes to attributes were not being picked up. (asamuzaK)
  • Fixed package.json "engines" field to reflect the new minimum Node.js versions needed to run jsdom, as noted in the changelog for v27.0.1.

Version 27.0.1

This release inadvertently raised the minimum Node.js version from v20.0.0 to v20.19.0+, v22.12.0+, v24.0.0+. (This happened via a dependency update.) This probably should have been a breaking (major) change, instead of happening in a patch version, since it prevents using earlier Node.js versions.

After further testing, we found that most of our development dependencies also require these versions, and so it's not feasible for the jsdom project to support earlier Node.js versions. (For example, our testing frameworks will not run on them.) If you need to use such earlier versions, or otherwise are working in an environment which gives related errors such as ERR_REQUIRE_ESM, then please stick with the v26.1.0 release of jsdom. (Noting, of course, that such versions are unsupported, and we will not respond to bug reports opened against them.)

Subsequent jsdom releases will explicitly require these minimum Node.js versions, and will have CI testing to ensure that the minimum version is not accidentally raised again.

Normal changelog:

  • Fixed some regressions in CSS selectors. Most such regression fixes were done in a minor update of a dependency, and thus available for all fresh installs of v27.0.0. However, one related to class="" attribute changes is only possible with a new version of jsdom. (asamuzaK)

Version 27.0.0

Changes since 26.1.0

  • Node.js v20 is now the minimum supported version.
  • Added a variety of event constructors, even though we do not implement their associated specifications or ever fire them: BeforeUnloadEvent, BlobEvent, DeviceMotionEvent (omitting requestPermission()), DeviceOrientationEvent (omitting requestPermission()), PointerEvent, PromiseRejectionEvent, and TransitionEvent.
  • Added movementX and movementY to MouseEvent. (These are from the Pointer Lock specification, the rest of which is not implemented.)
  • Added customElements.getName(). (mash-graz)
  • Updated the virtual console:
    • "jsdomError" events are now documented, with specific type properties and other properties that depend on the type.
    • sendTo() was renamed to forwardTo().
    • The jsdomErrors option to forwardTo() can be used to control which errors are sent to the Node.js console. This replaces the previous omitJSDOMErrors boolean option.
    • "jsdomError"s for failed XMLHttpRequest fetches are no longer emitted.
    • The values that are printed when forwarding "jsdomError"s to the Node.js console are streamlined.
  • Switched our CSS selector engine from nwsapi to @asamuzakjp/dom-selector, closing over 20 selector-related bugs.
  • Upgraded tough-cookie, which now considers URLs like http://localhost/ to be secure contexts (per the spec), and thus will return Secure-flagged cookies for such URLs. (colincasey)
  • Upgraded cssstyle, which brings along many improvements and fixes to the CSSStyleDeclaration object and its properties.
  • Updated the user agent stylesheet to be derived from the HTML Standard, instead of from an old revision of Chromium.
  • Changed element.click() to fire a PointerEvent instead of a MouseEvent.
  • Changed certain events to be passive by default.
  • Changed the <input> element's pattern="" attribute to use the v regular expression flag, instead of u.
  • Fixed many specification conformance issues with the Window object, including named properties and changing various data properties to accessor properties.
  • Fixed document.createEvent() to accept a more correct set of event names.
  • Fixed the ElementInternals accessibility getters and setters. (They were introduced in v23.1.0, but due to inadequate test coverage never actually worked.)
  • Fixed using Object.defineProperty() on certain objects, such as HTMLSelectElement instances.
  • Fixed jsdom.reconfigure({ url }) not updating document.baseURI or properties derived from it. (This regressed in v26.1.0.)
  • Fixed CSS system colors, as well as the initial, inherit, and unset keywords, to resolve correctly. (asamuzaK)

... (truncated)

title: feat: Add screenshot capture to task creation modal
body:
## Summary

Adds a built-in screenshot capture feature to the task creation modal, allowing users to capture screens or windows directly without leaving the app.

## What This Does

This PR adds a screenshot capture system integrated into the **Reference Images** section of the new task modal. Users can now capture screenshots of their entire screen or individual windows and add them as reference images for their tasks.

## Changes Made

### 1. Screenshot Capture Modal (`ScreenshotCapture.tsx`)
- New modal component that displays all available screenshot sources (screens and windows)
- Grid layout showing thumbnail previews of each source
- Visual selection with hover effects and checkmarks
- High-resolution capture support (handles retina displays)
- Loading states and error handling
- Refresh button to reload available sources

### 2. Electron IPC Layer
- **IPC Handlers** (`screenshot-handlers.ts`): Uses Electron's `desktopCapturer` API
  - `SCREENSHOT_GET_SOURCES`: Returns list of available screens/windows with thumbnails
  - `SCREENSHOT_CAPTURE`: Captures full-resolution screenshot from selected source
- **Preload API** (`screenshot-api.ts`): Exposes screenshot functionality to renderer
- **Constants** (`ipc.ts`): Added new IPC channel definitions

### 3. Task Creation Modal Integration (`TaskCreationWizard.tsx`)
- Added collapsible "Reference Images (optional)" section (matching edit modal pattern)
- "Capture" button in Reference Images section opens screenshot modal
- Auto-expands section when images are added via paste/drop/capture
- Uses `ImageUpload` component for consistent UI
- Shows image count badge when images are present
- Automatically generates timestamped filenames (e.g., `screenshot-1234567890.png`)
- Creates thumbnails and stores as base64 in task metadata

## User Flow

1. Open task creation modal
2. Click **"Reference Images (optional)"** to expand section
3. Click **"Capture"** button
4. Screenshot modal opens showing all available screens/windows
5. Select desired screen or window from grid
6. Click **"Capture"** to add screenshot to task
7. Screenshot appears in image attachments with other images

## Technical Details

- **Electron API**: Uses `desktopCapturer.getSources()` for screenshot capture
- **Image Processing**: Converts to base64, creates thumbnails, handles MIME types
- **Storage**: Screenshots stored as ImageAttachment objects in task metadata
- **File Naming**: Auto-generates unique timestamped filenames
- **Resolution**: Captures at 2x native resolution for retina display support
- **Compatibility**: Works with multiple monitors and window arrangements

## Why This Feature?

Previously, users had to:
1. Take a screenshot with OS tools
2. Save to file
3. Drag & drop or paste into the modal

Now they can capture directly from the app in one click, streamlining the workflow for adding visual references to tasks.

## Testing

Tested on macOS with:
- ✅ Multiple monitors
- ✅ Individual application windows
- ✅ High-resolution (retina) displays
- ✅ Image limit enforcement (max 10 images per task)
- ✅ Thumbnail generation
- ✅ Integration with existing drag & drop and paste functionality

## Screenshots

The feature adds a "Capture" button in the Reference Images section that opens a source selection modal showing all available screens and windows.

## Files Changed

- `apps/frontend/src/main/ipc-handlers/screenshot-handlers.ts` (new)
- `apps/frontend/src/main/ipc-handlers/index.ts` (register handlers)
- `apps/frontend/src/preload/api/screenshot-api.ts` (new)
- `apps/frontend/src/preload/api/index.ts` (integrate API)
- `apps/frontend/src/renderer/components/ScreenshotCapture.tsx` (new)
- `apps/frontend/src/renderer/components/TaskCreationWizard.tsx` (integration)
- `apps/frontend/src/shared/constants/ipc.ts` (IPC channels)

title: fix(ci): use correct electron-builder arch flags
body:
## Summary
- Fixes Mac Intel and ARM64 builds failing with "Unknown argument: arch"
- Changes deprecated `--arch=x64` to `--x64` and `--arch=arm64` to `--arm64` in both workflow files

## Root Cause
When the project switched from pnpm to npm, the argument passing behavior changed:
- **pnpm**: `pnpm run script -- --arg` adds a `--` separator, so electron-builder ignores `--arch`
- **npm**: `npm run script -- --arg` passes it directly, causing electron-builder to reject the deprecated `--arch` flag

title: fix: resolve spawn python ENOENT on macOS and Linux
body:
# Merry Christmas Team.

## Fix: Resolve spawn python ENOENT on macOS and Linux

Fixes #215

### Problem

Auto-Claude fails with "spawn python ENOENT" error when using "Analyze context" or "Generate context" features on:
- macOS (Homebrew Python installations)
- Ubuntu/Linux (system Python)

The error occurs even though:
1. Python is correctly installed
2. The Python detector (`findPythonCommand()`) successfully finds the Python executable

### Root Cause

The analyzer subprocess spawn in `project-context-handlers.ts` uses `process.env` which doesn't include Homebrew paths (`/opt/homebrew/bin`) or Linux system paths (`/usr/bin`) when the Electron app is launched from the GUI.

**Why**: GUI-launched apps don't inherit the full shell PATH that terminal sessions have.

### Solution

**1. Use `getAugmentedEnv()` for subprocess environment** (line 191)

Changed from:
```typescript
env: { ...process.env }
```

To:
```typescript
env: getAugmentedEnv()
```

This utility already exists in the codebase (used for GitHub CLI detection) and adds platform-specific binary paths.

**2. Enhanced Linux paths in `env-utils.ts`** (lines 29, 32)

Added missing system paths:
```typescript
linux: [
  '/usr/local/bin',
  '/usr/bin',               // ← Added: System binaries (Python, etc.)
  '/snap/bin',
  '~/.local/bin',
  '/usr/sbin',              // ← Added: System admin binaries
],
```

### Testing

✅ **Verified on Ubuntu 24.04**:
- Built and packaged AppImage with fixes
- "Analyze context" works correctly
- Python analyzer executes without ENOENT errors
- Project index loads successfully

✅ **Quality gates**:
- All Python tests pass (1162 passed, 1 xfailed, 1 xpassed)
- Frontend linting passes (0 errors, 151 warnings)
- TypeScript type checking passes

**Expected macOS behavior**: Should also fix the issue as the macOS paths (`/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`) were already in `getAugmentedEnv()`, they just weren't being used.

### Relationship to PR #136

This PR supersedes #136 with a more complete solution:
- PR #136 focuses on Python detection (which already works via `findPythonCommand()`)
- This PR fixes the **environment** passed to `spawn()` (the actual root cause)
- This PR also enhances Linux paths that were incomplete

### Commits

- `208c9d0` - fix: use augmented env for Python analyzer spawn to fix macOS PATH issue
- `25c10d8` - fix: add /usr/bin and /usr/sbin to Linux augmented PATH
- `8934416` - docs: add fix summary and update package-lock

### Checklist

- [x] Branched from `develop`
- [x] All tests pass
- [x] Frontend linting passes
- [x] TypeScript type checking passes
- [x] Tested on Ubuntu 24.04
- [x] References issue #215
- [x] Follows commit message format

title: Potential fix for code scanning alert no. 224: Uncontrolled command line
body:
Potential fix for [https://github.com/AndyMik90/Auto-Claude/security/code-scanning/224](https://github.com/AndyMik90/Auto-Claude/security/code-scanning/224)

To fix the problem, avoid building a shell command with string interpolation that embeds `zipPath` and `destDir`. Instead, invoke PowerShell with `execFileSync` (which does not use a shell) and pass each argument as a separate array element. This removes shell parsing from the equation and prevents any characters in `zipPath` or `destDir` from being interpreted as additional commands or flags.

Concretely, within `apps/frontend/scripts/download-prebuilds.cjs`, in the `extractZip(zipPath, destDir)` function around lines 136–142, replace the single-string `execSync` call:

```js
execSync(`powershell -Command "Expand-Archive -Path '${zipPath}' -DestinationPath '${destDir}' -Force"`, {
  stdio: 'inherit',
});
```

with a call to `execFileSync` that explicitly supplies the PowerShell executable and its arguments as an array, for example:

```js
execFileSync('powershell', [
  '-NoProfile',
  '-NonInteractive',
  '-Command',
  'Expand-Archive',
  '-Path', zipPath,
  '-DestinationPath', destDir,
  '-Force',
], { stdio: 'inherit' });
```

You can continue to use the existing `execSync` import by adding a local `execFileSync` import within the function via destructuring from `require('child_process')`, or you can change that local destructuring to get both `execSync` and `execFileSync` if needed. No changes are required elsewhere in the file; `extractZip`’s behavior (extracting the archive to `destDir` and inheriting stdio) will be preserved, but it will no longer be vulnerable to command injection via crafted paths.

title: fix(updater): proper semver comparison for pre-release versions
body:
## Summary

Fixes the beta auto-update bug where the app was offering downgrades (e.g., showing v2.7.1 as "new version available" when on v2.7.2-beta.6).

## Problem

The version comparison logic had two issues:
1. `compareVersions()` in `version-manager.ts` was splitting versions by `.` and parsing to numbers, which breaks for pre-release versions like `2.7.2-beta.6` (because `Number("2-beta")` returns `NaN`)
2. `app-updater.ts` was using simple `!==` instead of proper semver comparison to detect updates

## Solution

### version-manager.ts
- New `parseVersion()` function that separates base version from pre-release suffix
- Updated `compareVersions()` to handle pre-release versions correctly:
  - alpha < beta < rc < stable (no prerelease)
  - 2.7.2-beta.1 < 2.7.2-beta.2 < 2.7.2 (stable)
  - 2.7.1 < 2.7.2-beta.1 < 2.7.2

### app-updater.ts
- Import and use `compareVersions()` for proper version comparison
- Added debug logging for version comparisons

### Tests
- Added comprehensive unit tests covering:
  - Basic version comparison
  - Pre-release handling
  - The specific bug scenario (2.7.1 vs 2.7.2-beta.6)

## Testing

```bash
cd apps/frontend && pnpm test -- --run src/main/__tests__/version-manager.test.ts
```

## Verification

With this fix:
- ✅ v2.7.1 will NOT be offered as update when on v2.7.2-beta.6
- ✅ v2.7.2-beta.7 WILL be offered as update when on v2.7.2-beta.6
- ✅ v2.7.2 (stable) WILL be offered as update when on v2.7.2-beta.7

title: [Bug] Roadmap generation fails with ENOENT on macOS - path with spaces not handled
body:
## Environment
- Auto-Claude version: 2.7.1
- macOS: Sequoia (Darwin 24.6.0)
- Python: 3.12.9

## Error
When generating a roadmap, the app fails with:
```
[Roadmap] Process error: spawn /Users/av/Library/Application ENOENT
```

## Cause
The path `/Users/av/Library/Application Support/auto-claude-ui/python-venv/bin/python` is being split at the space. PRs #135 and #155 fixed this for some code paths but not for the Roadmap feature.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Install Auto-Claude 2.7.1 on macOS
2. Add a project
3. Try to generate a roadmap
4. Observe ENOENT error

## Workarounds Attempted (all failed)
- ✅ Set custom Python path in Settings → Paths → Python Path to `/opt/anaconda3/bin/python` or `/usr/local/bin/python`
- ✅ Moved app data directory to path without spaces (`~/.auto-claude-data`) with symlink from original location
- ✅ Set `ENABLE_FANCY_UI=false` in project .env
- ✅ Rebuilt Python venv with correct Python 3.12

None of these workarounds help because the Roadmap code constructs the path string before spawning, doesn't resolve symlinks, and doesn't properly quote/escape the path containing spaces.

## Expected Behavior
Roadmap generation should work on macOS where the default app data path contains spaces (`~/Library/Application Support/`).

## Suggested Fix
The spawn call in the Roadmap feature needs to properly handle paths with spaces, similar to the fixes in PRs #135 and #155. Either:
1. Quote the path when passing to spawn
2. Use an array format for spawn arguments
3. Resolve symlinks before constructing the path

title: Bug: Stage Changes button stages to main instead of worktree branch
body:
## Description
When using the 'Stage Changes' button on a task that is in a worktree, the changes are being staged directly to `main` instead of to the worktree's branch. This causes merge conflicts when trying to merge the task.

## Reported By
CyberClash (Discord #feedback-and-bugs)

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Create a task with a worktree
2. Make changes in the worktree
3. Click 'Stage Changes' or mark as Done
4. Attempt to merge from the worktree to main
5. Observe conflicts due to changes being staged on main

## Expected Behavior
Changes should be staged within the worktree branch, not on main.

## Actual Behavior
Changes are staged directly to main, causing the worktree branch and main to have conflicting staged changes.

## User Report
> 'Found the issue! Main has staged changes that shouldn't be there (looks like the 11.3 changes got staged directly on main instead of merged from the branch).'
> 'The Stage Changes button in Auto-Claude had staged files directly on main instead of in the worktree branches, causing conflicts.'

## Possible Location
Likely in `apps/frontend/src/main/ipc-handlers/task/worktree-handlers.ts` - the staging logic may be using the wrong git context.

## Environment
- Windows 11
- Beta build 2.7.x

title: Bug: Memory status always checks for OPENAI_API_KEY regardless of configured embedding provider
body:
## Description

The Graph Memory Status card on the Memories page always shows "OPENAI_API_KEY not set (required for Graphiti embeddings)" even when a different embedding provider (like Ollama) is properly configured.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure Ollama as the embedding provider in `.env`:
   ```
   GRAPHITI_ENABLED=true
   GRAPHITI_LLM_PROVIDER=ollama
   GRAPHITI_EMBEDDER_PROVIDER=ollama
   OLLAMA_LLM_MODEL=llama2-uncensored:latest
   OLLAMA_EMBEDDING_MODEL=mxbai-embed-large:latest
   OLLAMA_EMBEDDING_DIM=1024
   ```
2. Start the Electron app
3. Navigate to the Memories tab
4. Observe the "Graph Memory Status" card still shows "OPENAI_API_KEY not set"

## Expected Behavior

The status card should recognize that Ollama is configured and show "Available" since the Ollama settings are properly set.

## Actual Behavior

The status card shows "Not Available" with the message "OPENAI_API_KEY not set (required for Graphiti embeddings)" regardless of the configured provider.

## Root Cause

In `apps/frontend/src/main/ipc-handlers/context/memory-status-handlers.ts`, the `buildMemoryStatus()` function hardcodes an OpenAI API key check:

```typescript
const hasOpenAI = hasOpenAIKey(projectEnvVars, globalSettings);
// ...
if (!hasOpenAI) {
  return {
    enabled: true,
    available: false,
    reason: 'OPENAI_API_KEY not set (required for Graphiti embeddings)'
  };
}
```

This ignores the `GRAPHITI_EMBEDDER_PROVIDER` setting entirely.

## Proposed Fix

1. Add a `hasEmbeddingsConfigured()` function in `utils.ts` that checks the correct credentials based on the configured provider:
   - `ollama`: Check for `OLLAMA_EMBEDDING_MODEL` and `OLLAMA_EMBEDDING_DIM`
   - `openai`: Check for `OPENAI_API_KEY`
   - `voyage`: Check for `VOYAGE_API_KEY`
   - `google`: Check for `GOOGLE_API_KEY`
   - `azure_openai`: Check for `AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY`
   - `openrouter`: Check for `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`

2. Update `buildMemoryStatus()` to use the provider-aware check instead of hardcoded OpenAI check.

## Affected Versions

- v2.7.2-beta.9 (and likely earlier versions)

## Labels

bug, frontend, memory

- **Make handleProcessExit async** - Converted to async function to support async operations within the handler
- **Async commit message reading** - Replaced `readFileSync` with `fsPromises.readFile` for non-blocking file reads
- **Parallel plan updates** - Refactored plan persistence to use `Promise.all()` for concurrent updates to both main project and worktree plans
- **Fire-and-forget pattern** - Plan updates now run in the background without blocking the IPC response to the renderer process
- **Enhanced error handling** - Separated error handling logic for main vs worktree plans with appropriate logging levels

## Impact

These changes eliminate blocking I/O operations that could freeze the Electron UI during merge operations, particularly when:
- Reading suggested commit messages
- Updating implementation plans across multiple locations

The async refactor ensures the main thread remains responsive while file operations complete in the background.

## Technical Details

**Before:** Sequential synchronous file operations blocked the event loop
```typescript
const suggestedCommitMessage = readFileSync(commitMsgPath, 'utf-8').trim();
for (const planPath of planPaths) {
  const planContent = readFileSync(planPath, 'utf-8');
  writeFileSync(planPath, JSON.stringify(plan, null, 2));
}
```

**After:** Async operations with parallel execution
```typescript
const suggestedCommitMessage = (await fsPromises.readFile(commitMsgPath, 'utf-8')).trim();
const updates = planPaths.map(async ({ path: planPath }) => {
  const planContent = await fsPromises.readFile(planPath, 'utf-8');
  await fsPromises.writeFile(planPath, JSON.stringify(plan, null, 2));
});
await Promise.all(updates); // Executed in background
```

- [ ] Confirm suggested commit messages are read correctly
- [ ] Validate implementation plan updates persist to both main and worktree locations
- [ ] Test error handling for missing or inaccessible plan files

title: feat: add terminal dropdown with inbuilt and external options in task review
body:
## Summary

Adds a dropdown menu to the task review modal's terminal button, allowing users to choose between opening an inbuilt terminal tab or launching the system's default external terminal app. When selecting the inbuilt option, the modal automatically closes and switches to the Agent Terminals view where the terminal is created.

## Motivation

Previously, the task review modal only had a single terminal button that opened the system's default terminal. Users wanted the ability to:
- Open a terminal within the app (inbuilt terminal tab in Agent Terminals view)
- Still have the option to use their external terminal app
- Have the UI automatically navigate to where the terminal was created for better UX

## Changes

### Backend/IPC Layer
- **New IPC Channel**: Added `SHELL_OPEN_TERMINAL` for cross-platform external terminal opening
- **Cross-platform Support**: Implemented handlers for macOS, Windows, and Linux
  - macOS: Uses `open -a Terminal`
  - Windows: Uses `start cmd`
  - Linux: Tries gnome-terminal, konsole, xfce4-terminal, xterm with fallback logic

### Frontend Components

#### New Component: `TerminalDropdown`
- Dropdown menu with two options:
  - "Open in Inbuilt Terminal" - Creates terminal tab in Agent Terminals view
  - "Open in External Terminal" - Opens system terminal at worktree path
- Supports disabled state and custom styling
- Used in two locations:
  - Main terminal button in workspace status header
  - Terminal button in uncommitted changes warning

#### Updated Components
- **`WorkspaceStatus`**: Replaced single Terminal button with TerminalDropdown
- **`TaskReview`**: Passes callbacks through to WorkspaceStatus
- **`TaskDetailModal`**: Threads callbacks from App.tsx down to TaskReview
- **`App.tsx`**: Implements `handleOpenInbuiltTerminal` that orchestrates the full flow

### Terminal Creation Flow

The inbuilt terminal option now properly:
1. Switches active view to Agent Terminals (`setActiveView('terminals')`)
2. Closes the task detail modal (`setSelectedTask(null)`)
3. Waits for TerminalGrid component to mount (100ms delay)
4. Adds terminal to frontend store (`useTerminalStore.getState().addTerminal()`)
5. Terminal component mounts and creates backend PTY via `usePtyProcess` hook

This ensures the terminal appears in the UI by following the correct lifecycle:
- Frontend store update → Component mount → Backend PTY creation

### Hook Extension: `useTerminalHandler`
- Extended to support both terminal types:
  - `openTerminal(id, cwd)` - Creates inbuilt terminal tab
  - `openExternalTerminal(cwd)` - Opens system terminal app
- Unified error handling and loading states for both types

### API Extension
- **`shell-api.ts`**: Added `openTerminal(dirPath)` method
- **Preload API**: Exposed new IPC channel to renderer process

## Technical Details

### Component Prop Threading
The `onOpenInbuiltTerminal` callback is threaded through the component hierarchy:
```
App.tsx
  → TaskDetailModal
    → TaskReview
      → WorkspaceStatus
        → TerminalDropdown
```

This architecture allows the parent component (`App.tsx`) to orchestrate:
- Modal state management
- View switching
- Terminal store updates

Without this, the WorkspaceStatus component would unmount when the modal closed, preventing terminal creation.

### Race Condition Fix
The initial implementation had a race condition where:
1. Terminal was created in backend
2. Modal closed, unmounting WorkspaceStatus
3. Terminal creation handler never completed

**Solution**: Move terminal creation to parent level (`App.tsx`) where modal and view state are managed, ensuring proper lifecycle control.

### Store Integration Fix
The second iteration had another issue:
- Backend PTY was created successfully
- But no Terminal object existed in frontend store
- TerminalGrid had nothing to render

**Solution**: Use `addTerminal()` to create frontend Terminal object first, then let the normal component lifecycle create the backend PTY via `usePtyProcess`.

## Testing

Verified the following scenarios work correctly:

### Inbuilt Terminal
- [x] Click dropdown → "Open in Inbuilt Terminal"
- [x] Modal closes automatically
- [x] View switches to Agent Terminals
- [x] Terminal appears in TerminalGrid
- [x] Terminal opens at correct worktree path
- [x] Works from main workspace status header
- [x] Works from uncommitted changes warning section

### External Terminal
- [x] Click dropdown → "Open in External Terminal"
- [x] System terminal opens
- [x] Terminal opens at correct worktree path
- [x] Works on macOS (tested)
- [x] Cross-platform code implemented for Windows and Linux

### Edge Cases
- [x] Dropdown disabled while terminal is opening
- [x] Error handling for failed terminal creation
- [x] Max terminals limit respected
- [x] Project path correctly passed to terminal store
- [x] Works with both worktree path and main project path (uncommitted changes)

## Screenshots

### Dropdown Menu
The new dropdown appears when clicking the terminal button:
- Terminal icon with chevron-down indicator
- Two menu options with distinct icons

### Flow
1. User clicks terminal dropdown in task review modal
2. Selects "Open in Inbuilt Terminal"
3. Modal closes
4. View switches to Agent Terminals
5. New terminal appears with correct working directory

## Breaking Changes

None. This is a pure feature addition with backwards-compatible changes.

## Commits

- `c3b4d00` - feat: add dropdown to select inbuilt or external terminal in task review
- `33d913d` - fix: correct import paths in TerminalDropdown component
- `16a3b46` - feat: add modal close and view switch for inbuilt terminal option
- `960e4d5` - fix: pass terminal creation callback to parent to prevent unmount race condition
- `648f234` - fix: add terminal to frontend store to display in UI

## Related Issues

Resolves user request for inbuilt terminal option in task review workflow.

title: Fix: Update phase logs when task is stopped
body:
## Summary

Fixes a bug where the logs tab continued to show phases as "Running" even after a task was stopped and moved to the planning board.

## Problem

When a user stopped a task in progress:
- ✅ Task status changed to 'backlog' 
- ✅ Execution progress reset to 'idle'
- ✅ Task moved to planning board in UI
- ❌ **But** the logs tab still showed "Running" badge for active phases

### Root Cause

The phase logs are stored in `task_logs.json` files (separate from task status). When a task was stopped:
1. The main task status was updated to 'backlog'
2. The execution progress was reset to 'idle'
3. **But the `task_logs.json` files were not updated**
4. Phases with `status: 'active'` in the log files continued to display as "Running"

## Solution

### Backend Changes

**`task-log-service.ts`**
- Added `markActivePhasesStopped()` method to update phase status in log files
- Updates both main and worktree `task_logs.json` files
- Marks all `active` phases as `stopped` when task is interrupted
- Emits `logs-changed` event to update UI immediately

**`execution-handlers.ts`** 
- Updated `TASK_STOP` handler to call `markActivePhasesStopped()`
- Wrapped in try-catch to ensure task stopping works even if log update fails
- Prevents any errors in log updates from breaking core stop functionality

### Type System Changes

**`task.ts`**
- Extended `TaskLogPhaseStatus` to include `'stopped'` as a valid status
- More semantically correct than using `'failed'` for user-initiated stops

### UI Changes

**`TaskLogs.tsx`**
- Added "Stopped" badge with muted gray styling
- Shows alert triangle icon to indicate interruption
- Distinct from "Failed" (red/error) and "Running" (blue/active)
- Added phase section styling for `stopped` status

## Testing

Tested the following scenarios:
1. ✅ Starting a task and immediately stopping it
2. ✅ Stopping a task during different phases (planning, coding, validation)
3. ✅ Verifying logs tab updates immediately when task is stopped
4. ✅ Ensuring stop button works even if log files are missing/corrupted
5. ✅ Checking both main and worktree log files are updated

## Files Changed

- `apps/frontend/src/main/task-log-service.ts` - Added phase status update methods
- `apps/frontend/src/main/ipc-handlers/task/execution-handlers.ts` - Call markActivePhasesStopped on task stop
- `apps/frontend/src/shared/types/task.ts` - Extended TaskLogPhaseStatus type
- `apps/frontend/src/renderer/components/task-detail/TaskLogs.tsx` - Added Stopped badge and styling

## Screenshots

**Before:** Logs tab showed "Running" even after task was stopped
**After:** Logs tab correctly shows "Stopped" when task is stopped

## Breaking Changes

None - this is purely a bug fix. The new `'stopped'` status is backward compatible.

## Related Issues

Fixes issue where logs tab displays incorrect running status after stopping a task.
