title: [Bug] "Start Claude Code" causes infinite freeze on macOS
body:
```
## Problem
Clicking "Start Claude Code" in Agent Terminals causes macOS beachball (infinite freeze).

## Root Cause
`@lydell/node-pty@1.1.0` is based on `node-pty@1.1.0-beta14`, which is missing a critical fix for macOS PTY writes.

The fix ([microsoft/node-pty#831](https://github.com/microsoft/node-pty/pull/831)) wasn't included until `beta42` - 28 versions later.

When writing to the PTY on macOS:
- macOS kernel buffer is only ~1KB
- If buffer fills, libuv deadlocks due to mismatched blocking mode
- Event loop starves indefinitely

## Why @lydell/node-pty?
Commit e1aee6a switched to @lydell because microsoft/node-pty failed to compile on Windows (MSBuild errors). The prebuilt binaries avoid requiring Visual Studio Build Tools.

## Options

### Option A: Switch back to microsoft/node-pty
- ✅ Has the fix
- ❌ May reintroduce Windows build issues
- ❌ Requires build tools (node-gyp, Python, C++)

### Option B: Request @lydell update their fork
- ✅ Keep prebuilt binaries
- ❌ Depends on third-party maintainer timeline

### Option C: Fork @lydell/node-pty ourselves
- ✅ Full control
- ❌ Maintenance burden

### Option D: Implement workaround
- Chunk PTY writes with `setImmediate()` between them
- ✅ No package changes
- ❌ May not fully fix the issue

## References
- [microsoft/node-pty#831](https://github.com/microsoft/node-pty/pull/831) - The fix
- [microsoft/vscode#246204](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/246204) - VS Code had same issue
- [@lydell/node-pty](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@lydell/node-pty) - Based on beta14
```

title: Fix #609: Windows coding phase not starting after spec/planning
body:
Fixes #609

## Problem
On Windows, `os.execv()` breaks the connection with the Electron parent process when `spec_runner.py` transitions to `run.py` for the coding phase. This causes:
- Coding phase never starts after planning completes
- UI shows "encountered unknown error"
- Task cannot be resumed

## Root Cause
`os.execv()` on Windows spawns a new process and exits the current one, severing the IPC connection with the Electron main process.

## Solution
- Use `subprocess.run()` on Windows to maintain the parent-child process connection
- Keep `os.execv()` on Unix/macOS for efficiency (replaces the current process)
- Added `import subprocess` to support the new approach

## Testing
✅ Tested on Windows 10:
- Planning phase completes successfully
- Coding phase now starts immediately after planning
- Full workflow executes without errors

✅ Unix/macOS compatibility:
- No changes to Unix/macOS behavior (continues using `os.execv()`)
- Platform-specific handling via `sys.platform` check

## Changes
- `apps/backend/runners/spec_runner.py`:
  - Added `import subprocess`
  - Added platform-specific execution logic (lines 344-351)
  - Added comments referencing issue #609

title: Fix Windows UTF-8 encoding errors in spec file reading
body:
## Problem

On Windows, Python's  defaults to  encoding instead of UTF-8, causing  crashes when spec files contain non-ASCII characters (smart quotes, em dashes, Unicode symbols, etc.).

**Error encountered:**
```
UnicodeDecodeError: 'charmap' codec can't decode byte 0x8f in position 2895
```

This error occurs in the spec validation phase, preventing tasks from being created or completed.

## Solution

Added explicit `encoding='utf-8'` parameter to all `read_text()` calls in the spec pipeline:

### Files changed (4):
1. **spec_document_validator.py** - Reading spec.md during validation
2. **compaction.py** - Reading phase output files for summarization  
3. **validation_strategy.py** - Reading requirements.txt and pyproject.toml
4. **agent_runner.py** - Reading prompt template files

### Changes:
```diff
- content = spec_file.read_text()
+ content = spec_file.read_text(encoding='utf-8')
```

## Impact

✅ **Fixes:** Spec generation crashes on Windows with Unicode content  
✅ **Tested:** Windows 10 with Auto-Claude v2.7.3  
✅ **Safe:** No impact on Unix/Mac (already default to UTF-8)  
✅ **Minimal:** Only 5 lines changed across 4 files

## Testing

Verified that:
- Spec files with Unicode characters can be read without errors
- Spec validation completes successfully on Windows
- No regression on Unix/Mac systems (UTF-8 is already the default)

## Related Issues

This fix prevents the "spec validation failed" errors on Windows that block task creation in the Roadmap tool and spec runner.

title: feat: Consolidate security config files into single .auto-claude-security.json
body:
## Summary

Currently, security configuration is split across two files:
- `.auto-claude-allowlist` - manual command allowlist (one command per line)
- `.auto-claude-security.json` - auto-generated security profile (detected stack, base commands)

This proposal consolidates them into a single `.auto-claude-security.json` file.

## Current State

**`.auto-claude-allowlist`** (manual):
```
# Custom commands
bazel
terraform
```

**`.auto-claude-security.json`** (auto-generated):
```json
{
  "base_commands": ["ls", "cat", "grep"],
  "stack_commands": ["cargo", "rustc"],
  "detected_stack": {
    "languages": ["rust"],
    "package_managers": ["cargo"]
  },
  "project_hash": "abc123",
  "created_at": "2024-01-15T10:30:00"
}
```

## Proposed Format

Single `.auto-claude-security.json`:
```json
{
  "version": 2,
  "base_commands": ["ls", "cat", "grep"],
  "stack_commands": ["cargo", "rustc"],
  "custom_commands": ["bazel", "terraform"],
  "detected_stack": {
    "languages": ["rust"],
    "package_managers": ["cargo"]
  },
  "project_hash": "abc123",
  "created_at": "2024-01-15T10:30:00"
}
```

## Benefits

- **Single source of truth** - one file to manage
- **Easier to understand** - all security config in one place
- **JSON format** - structured, validatable, IDE-friendly
- **Version field** - enables future migrations

## Migration Strategy

1. On startup, if `.auto-claude-allowlist` exists:
   - Read commands from it
   - Merge into `custom_commands` array in `.auto-claude-security.json`
   - Optionally: rename old file to `.auto-claude-allowlist.migrated`
2. Backward compatible - old files still work during transition

## Implementation

Files to modify:
- `apps/backend/security/profile.py` - merge allowlist loading into profile
- `apps/backend/security/constants.py` - update constants
- `apps/backend/project/stack_detector.py` - output new format
- `shared_docs/SECURITY_COMMANDS.md` - update documentation

## Related

- #580 - Broader config centralization effort (env vars, .env loading)
- #646 - Recent fix for security profile in worktree mode

---

Happy to implement this if there's interest!

title: fix(memory): save PR review patterns and gotchas as separate episodes
body:
## Summary
- Fixes memory learning issue where PR review patterns and gotchas were not searchable
- Patterns and gotchas extracted from PR reviews are now saved as separate episodes with correct types

## Problem
The backend's `get_patterns_and_gotchas()` in `integrations/graphiti/queries_pkg/search.py` searches for episodes with `type='pattern'` or `type='gotcha'`. However, `savePRReviewToMemory()` in the frontend was embedding patterns and gotchas as JSON fields within `'pr_review'` episodes.

This meant:
- ✅ Patterns/gotchas were extracted and stored
- ❌ But they were unsearchable by the backend retrieval functions
- ❌ The memory system was "storing but not learning"

## Solution
After saving the main `pr_review` episode, also save each extracted pattern and gotcha as **separate episodes** with the correct type (`'pattern'` or `'gotcha'`).

The patterns and gotchas are still embedded in the `pr_review` episode for backwards compatibility - this change only adds the separate episodes to enable searchability.

body:
### Checklist

### Area

Frontend

Windows

### Version

2.7.2

### What happened?

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/34a26245-362a-426d-9417-f9b271960b22

# 🐞 [Kanban] Project Files excluded from `@` reference search after first miss

---

## Environment
- **Application**: auto-claude
- **OS**: Windows 11 25H2

---

## Description
When creating a new Kanban task in **auto-claude**, Project Files can be referenced from the task **Description** using the `@` tag.  
However, there is a state-related bug in the `@` reference search.

If a Project File does **not appear in the search results on the first attempt**, that file is **excluded from all subsequent searches** within the same task creation flow.

Even after refining the query (for example, by typing the full file name), the file never appears again.

This is not a simple search miss, but a case where the **search state becomes fixed after the initial failure**.

---

## Impact
This issue does not completely block Kanban-based workflows, but it introduces **clear usage constraints and misleading behavior**:

- Users may incorrectly assume that:
  - the file does not exist, or
  - the file is not part of Project Files
- This is especially problematic for:
  - users unfamiliar with the repository structure
  - new contributors
  - large repositories with many Project Files
- Users are forced to:
  - manually search for files one by one
  - distrust the `@` reference search
- This results in:
  - slower task creation
  - increased cognitive load
  - reduced trust in the UI

In short, the feature exists but is **unreliable in normal usage**.

---

## Actual Behavior
- If a file is missing from the initial search results:
  - it is excluded from later searches
  - changes to the query do not refresh the candidate set
- The search behaves as if the result set is locked after the first miss

---

## Suspected Cause
Possible causes include:
- caching the initial result set and filtering it incrementally
- maintaining a negative cache for non-matching files
- not resetting the candidate list when the query changes

---

## Workaround
A workaround exists, but it bypasses the intended search workflow:

1. Open **Project Files View**
2. Manually locate the file
3. **Drag and drop** the file onto the Kanban task to create the reference

This works, but requires prior knowledge of the file’s location and does not scale well for large projects.


### Steps to reproduce

1. Launch auto-claude
2. Open a Kanban board
3. Create a new task (`+ Add item`)
4. Focus the **Description** field
5. Type `@` to trigger reference search
6. Enter a Project File name (or a partial name)
7. The file does **not** appear in the search results
8. Modify the query:
   - type a more specific name, or
   - enter the full file name
9. ❌ The file still does not appear

### Expected behavior

- The `@` reference search should re-evaluate **all Project Files** whenever the input changes
- A file should appear as soon as the query matches, regardless of earlier search attempts

```

title: Ollama model pull fails silently when Ollama version is too old
body:
Ollama model pull fails silently when Ollama version is too old

## Labels
bug

## Description

When attempting to pull newer embedding models (like `qwen3-embedding:8b`) via the Auto-Claude settings UI, the download appears to fail silently. The UI shows no error message, and the model is not downloaded.

## Root Cause

The issue is in `apps/backend/ollama_model_detector.py` in the `cmd_pull_model()` function. When Ollama's API returns an error via the streaming response (e.g., `{"error": "requires newer version"}`), the code doesn't handle it:

```python
for line in response:
    try:
        progress = json.loads(line.decode("utf-8"))
        # BUG: Only handles "completed"/"total" and "success" status
        # Missing: check for "error" key in progress
        if "completed" in progress and "total" in progress:
            # ... emit progress
        elif progress.get("status") == "success":
            pass
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        continue
```

The Ollama API returns this when the version is too old:
```json
{"status":"pulling manifest"}
{"error":"pull model manifest: 412: \n\nThe model you are attempting to pull requires a newer version of Ollama.\n\nPlease download the latest version at:\n\n\thttps://ollama.com/download\n\n"}
```

## Environment
- Auto-Claude: 2.7.2
- Ollama: 0.9.6 (too old for qwen3-embedding models)
- macOS Sequoia (Apple Silicon)
- Model attempted: `qwen3-embedding:8b`

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Have an older Ollama version installed (e.g., 0.9.6)
2. Open Auto-Claude Settings → Memory
3. Enable Memory with Ollama provider
4. Try to download `qwen3-embedding:8b` or similar newer model
5. The download starts but fails silently - no error is shown

## Expected Behavior
The UI should display the actual error message from Ollama, informing the user that they need to upgrade Ollama.

## Proposed Fix

1. **Check for error in streaming response** in `ollama_model_detector.py`:
```python
elif "error" in progress:
    output_error(f"Ollama error: {progress['error']}")
    return
```

2. **Add Ollama version check** that warns users when their version may be too old for certain models

3. **Better error display in UI** - surface the actual Ollama error message to users

## Workaround
Upgrade Ollama manually:
```bash
# macOS with Homebrew
brew upgrade ollama
brew services restart ollama

# Or download from https://ollama.com/download
```

## Related Issues
- #712 - Ollama mac command (install script issue)
- #665 - Memory initialization fails with Ollama provider

title: fix: improve cross-platform and multi-provider compatibility
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes several issues that cause Auto Claude to fail on non-default configurations (macOS, Google AI instead of OpenAI).

### Fixes Included

#### 1. Quote-aware security parser
Commands like `python -c 'x; y'` were incorrectly split on inner semicolons, causing false positives in security validation.
- Replaced regex-based `extract_commands` with `shlex`-based implementation
- Rewrote `split_command_segments` with state-machine approach
- Added handling for redirection operators (`>&`, `2>&1`)

#### 2. Google AI provider without OpenAI dependency
Graphiti defaulted to OpenAI's reranker even when using Google AI as both LLM and embedder.
- Added `NoOpCrossEncoder` to avoid OpenAI dependency
- Fixed `GoogleLLMClient` and `GoogleEmbedder` base class inheritance

Frontend only set `GRAPHITI_EMBEDDER_PROVIDER` but not `GRAPHITI_LLM_PROVIDER`, causing "OPENAI_API_KEY required" errors even with Google AI configured.
- Read `graphitiLlmProvider` from settings and set `GRAPHITI_LLM_PROVIDER`
- Default LLM provider to same as embedder if not explicitly set

#### 4. Platform-appropriate Python command fallback
On macOS, the bare `python` command doesn't exist (only `python3`), causing "command not found" errors.
- Added `getPlatformPythonFallback()` returning `python3` on macOS/Linux
- Updated fallback locations to use platform-appropriate command

title: Memory Leak: Claude Agent SDK leaves orphaned processes after agent sessions (upstream bug)
body:
## Problem Description

Auto Claude builds are experiencing significant memory leaks due to a bug in the `claude-agent-sdk` Python package. After each agent session completes, the Claude Code subprocess spawned by the SDK is not being properly cleaned up, causing processes to accumulate in the background.

### What Happens

1. Auto Claude creates a client using `create_client()` from `core/client.py`
2. The client is used with `async with client:` context manager
3. After the session completes, the SDK's `__aexit__` method is called
4. The SDK's `Query.close()` method **hangs indefinitely** due to missing timeout
5. The Claude Code subprocess stays alive in the background
6. Memory continues accumulating with each session
7. Eventually the system runs out of memory (OOM killer)

### Root Cause

This is caused by **two critical bugs in the `claude-agent-sdk` package** (external dependency):

#### Issue #378: `Query.close()` Hangs Indefinitely
- **Link**: https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/issues/378
- The `Query.close()` method can hang indefinitely if tasks don't properly respond to cancellation
- Causes anyio's `_deliver_cancellation()` to spin at 100% CPU
- **Root cause**: Missing timeout on `await self._tg.__aexit__(None, None, None)`
- Affects all code using `async with client:` pattern

#### Issue #434: Large Memory Spike / OOM
- **Link**: https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/issues/434  
- Since SDK 0.1.18, memory spikes when spawning helper processes
- Processes get killed with exit code -9 (OOM killer)
- After first OOM, subsequent calls fail with "Cannot write to terminated process"

### Affected Code Paths

This affects any code in Auto Claude that uses the Claude Agent SDK client:
- `apps/backend/agents/coder.py` - Main autonomous agent loop
- `apps/backend/agents/session.py` - Session management
- `apps/backend/qa/reviewer.py` - QA reviewer agent
- `apps/backend/qa/fixer.py` - QA fixer agent
- `apps/backend/analysis/insight_extractor.py` - Insight extraction
- `apps/backend/spec/pipeline/agent_runner.py` - Spec creation agents
- And several other files using `async with client:` pattern

### Operating System

This issue appears to be **more pronounced on Linux** (tested on Fedora), but may affect other platforms as well due to:
- How anyio handles task cancellation on different platforms
- Python subprocess cleanup behavior differences
- The Claude Code CLI's memory management

### Impact

title: fix(roadmap): normalize feature status values for Kanban display [ACS-115]
body: ## Summary Fixes **ACS-115** - roadmap features were not appearing in Kanban columns after generation. ## Problem After roadmap generation completed, the Kanban board showed "25 features" in the header but all 4 columns displayed "No features - Drag features here". ## Root Cause The Python backend generates features with `status: "idea"`, but the Kanban columns expect: - `under_review` - `planned` - `in_progress` - `done` The existing code used a type cast that passed invalid values through unchanged: ```typescript status: (raw.status as RoadmapFeature['status']) || 'under_review' ``` Since `"idea"` is truthy, it passed through and didn't match any column ID. ## Solution Added `normalizeFeatureStatus()` helper that: 1. Passes through valid status values unchanged 2. Maps known backend values to valid column IDs: - `idea`, `backlog`, `proposed` → `under_review` - `approved`, `scheduled` → `planned` - `active`, `building` → `in_progress` - `complete`, `completed`, `shipped` → `done` 3. Falls back to `under_review` for any unknown values ## Additional Fix Added Python environment readiness check in `agent-queue.ts` to prevent race conditions where roadmap process could spawn before dependencies are installed. ## Verification All 25 features now appear correctly in the "Under Review" column: ## Files Changed - `apps/frontend/src/main/ipc-handlers/roadmap/transformers.ts` - Added status normalization - `apps/frontend/src/main/agent/agent-queue.ts` - Python env readiness guard ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * More reliable Python environment initialization to avoid spawn-time failures * macOS Ollama install now uses Homebrew; Linux uses the official install script * Improved normalization of roadmap feature statuses to reduce mismatches * **Performance** * Kanban roadmap view now remounts on updates to ensure correct rendering and state refresh ✏️ Tip: You can customize this high-level summary in your review settings.

title: fix(insights): await async sendMessage to prevent race condition (#613)
body:
## Summary

Fixes the Insights feature failing with "Process exited with code 1" on Windows and macOS, while Claude Code and Ideation work correctly.

Fixes #613

## Root Cause

The IPC handler for `INSIGHTS_SEND_MESSAGE` was declared `async` but never awaited the `sendMessage()` call. This caused:

1. **Race condition**: The handler returned immediately while async environment setup was still running
2. **Silent failures**: On Windows (slower environment setup), the Python process would spawn before environment variables were ready
3. **Unhandled errors**: Any errors in the async chain were swallowed

The `sendMessage()` chain includes `getProcessEnv()` which calls `await getAPIProfileEnv()` - this async operation must complete before spawning the Python process.

## Solution

Added `await` to the `insightsService.sendMessage()` call and wrapped it in try/catch:

```typescript
try {
  await insightsService.sendMessage(projectId, project.path, message, modelConfig);
} catch (error) {
  console.error('[Insights IPC] Error in sendMessage:', error);
}
```

This ensures all async operations complete before the handler returns, fixing the race condition.

## Changes

- `apps/frontend/src/main/ipc-handlers/insights-handlers.ts`: Added `await` and try/catch wrapper

## Testing

- [x] TypeScript type check passes
- [x] ESLint passes
- [ ] Tested on macOS
- [ ] Tested on Windows
- [ ] Tested on Linux

## Cross-Platform Compatibility

This fix ensures the same behavior across all platforms by properly awaiting async operations:
- **Windows**: Primary fix target - environment setup is slower, making the race condition more likely to manifest
- **macOS**: Also affected (confirmed in issue comments by edwinmol)
- **Linux**: Same code path applies

title: fix(python-bundling): verify critical packages exist, not just marker file (#416)
body:
## Summary

Fix for tasks immediately failing on Linux AppImage and Windows builds with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'claude_agent_sdk'` or `python-dotenv`.

Fixes #416

## Root Cause

The bundled Python setup validation only checked:
1. Python binary exists
2. `.bundled` marker file exists

It did **not** verify that packages were actually installed. This meant corrupted CI caches or partial installs with missing packages would incorrectly pass validation, causing import errors at runtime.

## Solution

### Build-time fix (`download-python.cjs`)
After verifying the `.bundled` marker exists, also check that `claude_agent_sdk` and `dotenv` directories are present. If packages are missing, remove site-packages to force reinstall.

### Runtime fix (`python-env-manager.ts`)
Changed the fallback package detection from OR logic (`existsSync(claudeSdk) || existsSync(dotenv)`) to AND logic (`existsSync(claudeSdk) && existsSync(dotenv)`) - both packages must exist. Added diagnostic logging to help identify which packages are missing when detection fails.

## Changes

- **`apps/frontend/scripts/download-python.cjs`** (+19 lines)
  - Added verification of critical packages when `.bundled` marker exists
  - If packages missing, removes site-packages to force reinstall
  
- **`apps/frontend/src/main/python-env-manager.ts`** (+21/-12 lines)
  - Changed package detection from OR to AND (both must exist)
  - Added diagnostic logging for missing packages
  - Reordered logic to check packages first, marker second

## Testing

- [x] TypeScript type check passes
- [x] ESLint passes
- [ ] Tested on macOS
- [ ] Tested on Windows
- [ ] Tested on Linux AppImage

## Cross-Platform Compatibility

The fix uses `path.join()` and `fs.existsSync()` which are cross-platform compatible. No platform-specific code was added.

## How to verify

1. Build the app: `npm run package:linux` (or `:win`/`:mac`)
2. Run the packaged app
3. Create and start a task

title: fix(multi-project): filter task IPC events by project to prevent cross-project interference (#723)
body:
## Summary

Fixes a bug where starting a task in Project B caused an already-running task in Project A to appear "idle" unexpectedly. Tasks in different projects should run independently without affecting each other.

Fixes #723

## Root Cause

Task execution progress IPC events were broadcast globally without project context. When switching between projects:

1. User opens Project A, starts Task A (process runs)
2. User switches to Project B → task store replaces with Project B's tasks
3. Task A's process still emits `execution-progress` events
4. These events try to update by `taskId` in the store (now containing Project B tasks)
5. Task store lookup fails to find matching taskId, causing state corruption
6. Task appears in default `{phase: 'idle'}` state

The roadmap IPC events had proper project filtering, but task events did not (asymmetric implementation).

## Solution

Added `projectId` to all task-related IPC events and filter them in the renderer based on the currently selected project. This mirrors the existing pattern used for roadmap events.

## Changes

**Main Process (`agent-events-handlers.ts`)**
- Added project lookup for task events to include `projectId`
- Modified `execution-progress` event to include `projectId`
- Modified `TASK_STATUS_CHANGE` events (exit handler and execution-progress) to include `projectId`
- Modified file watcher `progress` event to include `projectId`

**Preload API (`task-api.ts`)**
- Updated type signatures for `onTaskProgress`, `onTaskStatusChange`, `onTaskExecutionProgress` to accept optional `projectId` parameter
- Updated IPC handlers to pass `projectId` through to callbacks

**Renderer Hooks (`useIpc.ts`)**
- Added `useProjectStore` import
- Added `isTaskForCurrentProject()` helper function
- Applied filter to `onTaskProgress`, `onTaskStatusChange`, and `onTaskExecutionProgress` handlers

## Testing

- [x] TypeScript type checking passes
- [x] ESLint passes (pre-existing warnings unrelated to this fix)
- [x] Pre-commit hooks pass
- [ ] Tested on macOS
- [ ] Tested on Windows
- [ ] Tested on Linux

## Backward Compatibility

The `projectId` parameter is optional throughout the chain. Events from older code without `projectId` will continue to work:
- If no `projectId` provided → event is accepted (backward compatibility)
- If no project selected → event is accepted
- Otherwise → only accept if `projectId` matches `selectedProjectId`

title: fix(permissions): grant worktree access to original project directories (#385)
body:
## Summary

Fixes permission errors when Claude agents run in a worktree and need to access files in the original project's `.auto-claude/` or `.worktrees/` directories.

Fixes #385

## Root Cause

When the Claude Agent SDK runs in a worktree (either `.auto-claude/worktrees/tasks/` or legacy `.worktrees/`), the filesystem permissions were restricted to:
1. The worktree directory (`project_dir`)
2. The spec directory (`spec_dir`)

However, agents sometimes need to access the **original project's** `.auto-claude/` directory (for spec files) or legacy `.worktrees/` directory. These paths are **outside** the worktree's restricted filesystem, causing permission errors like:

```
Claude requested permissions to write to /Users/XXX/dev/XXX/.worktrees/001-xxx/.auto-claude/specs/001-xxx/implementation_plan.json, but you haven't granted it yet.
```

## Solution

Added worktree detection logic in `create_client()` that:
1. Detects if `project_dir` is inside a worktree (new or legacy location)
2. Extracts the original project directory path
3. Adds Read/Write/Edit/Glob/Grep permissions for:
   - Original project's `.auto-claude/` directory (if it exists)
   - Original project's `.worktrees/` directory (legacy support, if it exists)

## Changes

**`apps/backend/core/client.py`** (+58 lines):
- Added worktree path detection using markers for both new (`.auto-claude/worktrees/tasks/`) and legacy (`.worktrees/`) locations
- Cross-platform path handling (handles both Unix `/` and Windows `\` separators)
- Added informative log message when worktree permissions are granted

## Testing

- [x] Python syntax check passed
- [x] All 170 security-related tests passed
- [x] Unit test of worktree detection logic validated
- [x] Tested on macOS
- [ ] Tested on Windows (logic includes Windows path support)
- [ ] Tested on Linux (should work same as macOS)

## Cross-Platform Compatibility

- The fix handles both Unix (`/`) and Windows (`\`) path separators
- Uses `str.replace("\\", "/")` for consistent path comparison
- Path markers include both Unix and Windows variants

## Note on Other Reported Errors

The issue also mentions Context7 MCP and WebFetch errors. Investigation shows:
- These tools are already correctly included in the permission system (`WebFetch(*)` and Context7 tools)
- The errors are likely related to MCP server availability/network issues or agent phase configuration (e.g., `spec_gatherer` has no MCP servers by design)
- The main fix needed was for the **filesystem permission** issue, which this PR addresses

title: fix: add PYTHONPATH to subprocess environment for bundled packages (#139)
body:
## Summary

Fixes the "Process exited with code 1" errors occurring across multiple features (GitHub PR review, autofix, triage, GitLab MR review) on all platforms (macOS, Windows, Linux) in packaged Electron apps.

Fixes #139

## Root Cause

The `subprocess-runner.ts` explicitly excluded PYTHONPATH from the environment passed to Python subprocesses. The comment said "Don't set PYTHONPATH - let runner.py manage its own import paths", but this was incorrect for packaged Electron apps where bundled site-packages require explicit PYTHONPATH.

Without PYTHONPATH, Python processes failed with:
```
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'dotenv'
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'claude_agent_sdk'
```

## Solution

1. **`runner-env.ts`**: Added `pythonEnvManager.getPythonEnv()` to the environment returned by `getRunnerEnv()`, which includes PYTHONPATH for bundled packages
2. **`subprocess-runner.ts`**: Changed to use the caller-provided environment directly when `options.env` is set (from `getRunnerEnv()`) instead of filtering it
3. **`mr-review-handlers.ts` (GitLab)**: Added `getRunnerEnv()` call to pass environment to subprocess (GitHub handlers already did this)

## Changes

| File | Change |

| `apps/frontend/src/main/ipc-handlers/github/utils/runner-env.ts` | Added `pythonEnvManager.getPythonEnv()` to include PYTHONPATH |

| `apps/frontend/src/main/ipc-handlers/github/utils/__tests__/runner-env.test.ts` | Updated tests to verify PYTHONPATH is included |

title: Fix frontend performance and type safety issues

## Problem

During PR #782 CodeRabbit review, two frontend issues were identified as out-of-scope:

1. **Unnecessary Cache Clearing:** Code unconditionally clears Electron session cache on every Windows startup, impacting startup performance with unnecessary I/O
2. **Unsafe Terminal Type Cast:** `settings?.preferredTerminal as SupportedTerminal` bypasses type validation, allowing unrecognized values from settings file to pass through

- Prevents runtime errors from invalid shell values in settings file

**Impact:** Type safety, clear error messages, graceful fallback for invalid preferences

Replace `'en-US'` with `undefined` to use the system's default locale:

```typescript
// Before
new Date(dateString).toLocaleDateString('en-US', { ... })

// After  
new Date(dateString).toLocaleDateString(undefined, { ... })
```

## Additional Context

The backend already uses ISO 8601 format correctly. This issue only affects the frontend display layer.

title: Add pre-commit hook for UTF-8 encoding enforcement
body:
## Problem

PR #782 fixed 251 instances of missing UTF-8 encoding across the backend. Without enforcement, these issues will recur as developers add new file operations without knowing about Windows encoding requirements.

## Solution

Add pre-commit hook that automatically checks for missing `encoding="utf-8"` parameters in file operations.

### 1. Encoding Check Script (`scripts/check_encoding.py`)
- Validates all `open()` calls have encoding parameter
- Validates `Path.read_text()` and `Path.write_text()` calls
- Checks `json.load/dump` with `open()`
- Allows binary mode without encoding (correct behavior)
- Windows-compatible with UTF-8 console reconfiguration

### 2. Pre-commit Configuration
- Runs automatically on every commit
- Scoped to `apps/backend/` to avoid false positives
- Integrates with existing pre-commit infrastructure
- Fast regex-based checking

### 3. Comprehensive Tests
- 10 tests covering all validation scenarios
- Tests detection, allowlisting, and edge cases
- All tests passing ✅

## Real-World Validation

The hook already caught **6 real encoding issues** in `apps/backend/core/progress.py` that were missed by PR #782 or added since then:
- Lines 45, 83, 184, 304, 378, 418

## Benefits

1. **Prevents Regressions:** Automatically catches missing encoding in new code
2. **Developer Education:** Fast feedback teaches encoding best practices
3. **CI Ready:** Can be integrated into GitHub Actions
4. **Low Overhead:** Simple regex matching, runs in milliseconds

## Testing

- ✅ All 10 unit tests passing
- ✅ Tested on backend files with/without encoding
- ✅ Verified binary files are allowed
- ✅ Confirmed scoping works (only checks apps/backend/)

## No Migration Needed

PR #782 already fixed most files. Developers only need to:
1. Ensure pre-commit is installed: `pip install pre-commit`
2. Install hooks: `pre-commit install`

The hook runs automatically on commit after installation.

## Related

- PR #782: Fix Windows UTF-8 encoding errors (fixed existing issues)
- This PR: Prevent future issues through automation
- Session Doc: `.claude/session-docs/session-encoding-precommit-hooks.md`

## Summary

Fixes a bug where the staging UI was shown again after app restart even when a task had already been staged. The persisted `stagedInMainProject` flag was being ignored because the condition order in the UI prioritized worktree existence over staged state.

## Problem

1. The `stagedInMainProject` and `stagedAt` flags were correctly saved to `implementation_plan.json`
2. After app restart, these flags were correctly loaded
3. **BUT** the UI showed the staging interface again because `worktreeStatus?.exists` was checked before `task.stagedInMainProject`

## Solution

3. **Added "Review Again" button** - clears staged state and returns to staging UI if user needs to re-stage

title: Fix/merge commit verification
body:
## Base Branch

- [x] This PR targets the `develop` branch (required for all feature/fix PRs)
- [ ] This PR targets `main` (hotfix only - maintainers)

## Description

Fixes a critical bug where clicking "Merge to main" deletes the worktree but doesn't actually commit changes to git. This PR adds verification that the merge commit is created before cleanup, preventing data loss.  If verification fails, the worktree is preserved for manual investigation.

## Related Issue

Closes #797

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix
- [ ] ✨ New feature
- [ ] 📚 Documentation
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor
- [ ] 🧪 Test

## Area

- [ ] Frontend
- [ ] Backend
- [x] Fullstack

## Commit Message Format

Follow conventional commits:  `<type>: <subject>`

**Types:** feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, test, chore

**Example:** `fix: verify merge commit creation before worktree cleanup`

## Changes Made

### Backend (`apps/backend/core/worktree.py`)
- Added merge commit verification after `git merge` command
- Verify commit message matches expected format:  `"auto-claude:  Merge {branch}"`
- Check if branch is already merged (acceptable edge case)
- Only report success if merge is confirmed
- Added detailed logging for debugging merge issues

### Frontend (`apps/frontend/src/main/ipc-handlers/task/worktree-handlers.ts`)
- Added pre-delete verification using `git branch --merged`
- Verify task branch is fully merged before deleting worktree
- If verification fails, preserve worktree and set status to `human_review`
- Provide clear error messages guiding users to check `git log`
- Safe-by-default:  keep worktree on any verification error

## Root Cause Analysis

The original code deleted the worktree immediately after `git merge` returned exit code 0. However, git can return success even when no merge commit is created: 
- Branch already merged (fast-forward)
- No changes to merge (empty diff)
- Certain git configurations

This caused commits to disappear from `git log`, leading users to believe their work was lost.

## Checklist

- [x] I've synced with `develop` branch

title: Fix pydantic_core missing module error during packaging
body:
Fixes #684

## Problem

Users reported `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pydantic_core._pydantic_core'` when running the packaged macOS app.

### Root Cause Analysis

The error occurred because:

1. **pydantic-core** includes a compiled C extension (`_pydantic_core.so`)
2. During packaging, pip could attempt to build from source if no compatible binary wheel was found
3. Source builds could fail silently without a C compiler or due to build issues
4. The package would be marked as "installed" but missing the critical compiled extension
5. **pydantic_core was not in the critical packages verification list**, so the broken installation went undetected

## Solution

This PR implements a two-part fix following systematic debugging methodology:

### 1. Force Binary Wheels for Pydantic Packages

**File:** `apps/frontend/scripts/download-python.cjs` (line 619)

Added `--only-binary pydantic,pydantic-core` to the pip install arguments. This:
- Prevents pip from attempting to build from source
- Ensures compiled extensions are properly included from pre-built wheels
- Makes the build fail fast if a compatible wheel isn't available (better than silent failure)

### 2. Add pydantic_core to Critical Packages Verification

**Files updated:**
- `apps/frontend/scripts/download-python.cjs` (lines 712, 815)
- `apps/frontend/src/main/python-env-manager.ts` (line 129)

Added `pydantic_core` to the critical packages list in all three locations where verification occurs. This ensures:
- **Build-time verification**: Package installation fails fast if pydantic_core is missing
- **Runtime verification**: App startup checks verify pydantic_core is present
- **Cache validation**: Existing cached installations are re-validated

## Testing Recommendations

To verify this fix:

1. **Clean build test**: Remove cached Python runtime and rebuild
   ```bash
   rm -rf apps/frontend/python-runtime
   npm run package:mac  # or package:win, package:linux
   ```

2. **Verify pydantic_core exists**: Check the bundled site-packages contains pydantic_core with the compiled extension

3. **Runtime test**: Run the packaged app and execute a task that uses the backend (which imports pydantic)

## Impact

This fix ensures that:
- ✅ Packaging will fail if pydantic binary wheels aren't available (fail fast)
- ✅ Both build-time and runtime verification check for pydantic_core
- ✅ Users won't receive a broken package with missing dependencies
- ✅ The issue is caught during packaging, not after distribution

## Related Issues

Closes #684

title: [Windows] Claude Agent SDK fails to import - pywin32 not initialized in bundled Python
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched existing issues and this hasn't been reported

### Area

Backend

### Operating System

Windows

### Version

2.5.5 (Windows Installer)

### What happened?

The **Insights** and **Ideation** features fail immediately with "Process exited with code 1" on Windows.

**Root Cause**: The Claude Agent SDK cannot be imported because `pywin32` is not properly initialized in the bundled Python environment.

The bundled `python-site-packages` directory contains pywin32, but:
1. `pywin32_bootstrap.py` is missing from site-packages
2. `pywin32_system32/__init__.py` is missing (directory not a proper package)
3. The `win32` and `win32/lib` directories aren't added to `sys.path`

This causes the import chain to fail:
```
claude_agent_sdk → mcp → mcp.os.win32.utilities → pywintypes
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pywintypes'
```

The backend then falls back to calling the `claude` CLI via subprocess, which also fails on Windows with:
```
ERROR Raw mode is not supported on the current process.stdin
```

**Related Issues**: #609, PR #752, PR #768

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install Auto-Claude using the Windows installer (v2.5.5)
2. Open Auto-Claude and select any project
3. Navigate to **Insights** tab and try to send any chat message
4. OR navigate to **Ideation** and click "Generate Ideas"
5. Observe: "Process exited with code 1" error

**Verification steps (confirming root cause)**:
```powershell
# Test SDK import with bundled Python
$env:PYTHONPATH = "C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Programs\auto-claude-ui\resources\python-site-packages"
& 'C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Programs\auto-claude-ui\resources\python\python.exe' -c "from claude_agent_sdk import ClaudeSDKClient"
# Result: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pywintypes'
```

### Expected behavior

The Claude Agent SDK should import successfully and Insights/Ideation features should work on Windows.

**Suggested Fix** (tested and working):

Add these files to the Windows build:

1. **`python-site-packages/pywin32_bootstrap.py`**:
```python
import os
import sys

_site_packages = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
_win32_dir = os.path.join(_site_packages, "win32")
_win32_lib = os.path.join(_site_packages, "win32", "lib")

for _p in [_win32_dir, _win32_lib]:
    if _p not in sys.path:
        sys.path.insert(0, _p)

_pywin32_system32 = os.path.join(_site_packages, "pywin32_system32")
if os.path.isdir(_pywin32_system32):
    os.environ["PATH"] = _pywin32_system32 + os.pathsep + os.environ.get("PATH", "")
    if hasattr(os, "add_dll_directory"):
        try:
            os.add_dll_directory(_pywin32_system32)
        except OSError:
            pass
```

2. **`python-site-packages/pywin32_system32/__init__.py`**:
```python
import os
__path__ = [os.path.dirname(__file__)]
```

After adding these files, the SDK imports successfully.

### Logs / Screenshots

```shell
**Ideation Log Output** (`%APPDATA%\auto-claude-ui\logs\main.log`):

◐ Running Performance Optimizations agent...
Security settings: D:\Projects\ColorPaletteDNA\.claude_settings.json
- Extended thinking: 16,384 tokens
- MCP servers: context7, graphiti-memory
⚠ Running recovery agent (attempt 1)...

◐ Running Code Quality & Refactoring agent...
⚠ Running recovery agent (attempt 1)...

✗ Generation failed: 0 of 2 ideas generated


**Environment**:
- Windows 11 Pro
- Auto-Claude v2.5.5 (Windows Installer)
- Bundled Python 3.12.8
- Claude Code CLI v2.0.76
```

title: fix: Increase Claude SDK JSON buffer size to prevent spec creation failures
body:
### Bug Description

Spec creation fails with error: `CLIJSONDecodeError: Failed to decode JSON: JSON message exceeded maximum buffer size of 1048576 bytes`

This occurs when the agent's tool results (e.g., large file reads, Glob searches) exceed the Claude Agent SDK's default 1MB JSON buffer limit during spec creation phases.

### Expected Behavior

Spec creation should complete successfully even when reading large files or performing extensive codebase searches during the discovery/research phases.

### Actual Behavior

Spec creation crashes with a JSON decode error when tool results exceed 1MB.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a spec for a feature that requires extensive context gathering (e.g., test suite overhaul, ESLint migration)
2. During discovery or research phase, agent reads multiple files or performs broad Glob searches
3. Error occurs when combined tool results exceed 1MB

### Environment

- **OS**: Linux
- **Python Version**: 3.12+
- **Auto Claude Version**: Latest develop branch
- **Claude Agent SDK**: >=0.1.16

### Root Cause

The `ClaudeAgentOptions` in `apps/backend/core/client.py` was not configured with `max_buffer_size`, leaving it at the default 1MB limit.

### Proposed Fix

Add `max_buffer_size` parameter to `ClaudeAgentOptions` in `create_client()`:

```python
options_kwargs = {
    # ... existing options ...
    "max_buffer_size": 10 * 1024 * 1024,  # 10MB buffer (default: 1MB) - fixes large tool results
}
```

This increases the buffer to 10MB, which should handle large tool results while still protecting against memory issues.

### Related Issues

- References: https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/issues/98

### Component

- [x] Backend (Python)

title: 🐛 Bug: Test command output (pnpm test:coverage) exceeds context window, causing API failures
body:
### Bug Description

When the coder agent runs test commands like `pnpm test:coverage`, the output size exceeds the Claude API's context window limit, causing the API call to fail with:

```
API Error: The model has reached its context window limit
```

The test command runs once and produces large output (Jest coverage reports can be 50KB+). The agent then retries, but since the same test command produces the same large output, it fails again in a loop.

### Expected Behavior

Test output should be truncated or handled in a way that doesn't flood the context window, allowing the task to complete.

### Actual Behavior

- `session.py` captures up to 50KB of Bash output
- For test commands, this is still too much
- Agent can't complete the subtask due to repeated context limit errors

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a spec involving test coverage verification
2. Agent runs `pnpm test:coverage`
3. Test output exceeds context window
4. API fails, agent retries, same failure repeats

### Environment

- **OS**: Linux (affects all)
- **Auto Claude Version**: 2.7.2

### Root Cause

`apps/backend/agents/session.py` (lines 505-510) stores Bash tool output up to 50KB. Test coverage output commonly exceeds this, and there's no special handling for known high-output commands.

### Suggested Approaches

1. **Command-specific output limits**: Detect test commands (`pnpm test`, `pytest`, `jest`, etc.) and truncate more aggressively (2-5KB max)

2. **Output to file redirect**: Add environment variable to redirect test output to a file instead of including in context

3. **Expose max iterations limit**: The `max_iterations` parameter exists but isn't configurable via `.env` - adding this would prevent infinite loops

4. **Combination**: Command-specific limits + configurable max iterations

### Component

- [x] Backend (Python)

title: 🐛 Bug: Jest worker processes orphaned after test commands complete
body:
### Bug Description

After running test commands like `pnpm test:coverage`, Jest worker processes (`processChild.js`) remain running even after the test completes and the session ends. These orphaned workers consume 90%+ CPU each and accumulate over time, requiring manual cleanup (`pkill -9 -f jest-worker`).

### Expected Behavior

All child processes spawned by Bash commands should be terminated when the command completes or the session ends.

### Actual Behavior

- Jest workers continue running after `pnpm test:coverage` completes
- Multiple workers accumulate across sessions
- No automatic cleanup mechanism exists

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run any spec that executes test commands
2. Wait for tests to complete
3. Check running processes: `ps aux | grep jest-worker`
4. Workers are still running at high CPU

### Environment

- **OS**: Linux Fedora 43
- **Auto Claude Version**: 2.7.2

### Root Cause

The Claude Agent SDK's Bash tool spawns processes without process group management. When Jest spawns worker processes, they outlive the parent bash process because there's no tracking mechanism to terminate the entire process tree.

### Suggested Mitigations

1. **Post-command cleanup hook**: Track and terminate child process groups after Bash commands complete

2. **Session cleanup**: On session end, scan for and terminate orphaned processes from that session

3. **Test command wrapper**: Special handling for known test runners (jest, pytest, vitest) with explicit cleanup

4. **Configurable cleanup**: Add `.env` option for cleanup timeout/strategy

title: Feature Request: Sparse Checkout Support for Large Repos (Unity/Game Dev)
body:
## Problem

Worktree creation fails or takes extremely long on large game projects (Unity, Unreal, Godot).

**My test case:** Unity project with 85,000+ files / 22GB
- Worktree checkout times out or fails with `fatal: Could not reset index file to revision 'HEAD'` on Windows
- Even when it works, checking out 33,000+ files takes several minutes per worktree
- Windows Defender and file locking exacerbate the issue

## Proposed Solution

Support **git sparse-checkout** when creating worktrees. For code-focused tasks, only checkout source code directories, not binary assets.

### How it works

```bash
git worktree add --no-checkout ../worktree-name branch
cd ../worktree-name
git sparse-checkout init --cone
git sparse-checkout set Assets/Scripts Assets/ScriptableObjects ProjectSettings Packages
git checkout
```

### Results from my testing (GalacticGlitch Unity project)

| Metric | Full Checkout | Sparse Checkout | Improvement |
|--------|---------------|-----------------|-------------|
| **Files** | 85,404 | 4,622 | **95% fewer** |
| **Disk Space** | 22 GB | 26 MB | **99.9% smaller** |
| **Checkout Time** | Minutes (often fails) | Seconds | **~100x faster** |

All code files needed for development tasks are present in the sparse checkout.

## Suggested UX

**Option A - Auto-detection:**
- Detect large repos (>10K files or >1GB)
- Automatically offer/enable sparse checkout with sensible defaults

**Option B - Project configuration:**
- Allow users to configure sparse-checkout patterns in project settings
- Provide presets for common project types (Unity, Unreal, Godot, etc.)

**Option C - Per-task configuration:**
- Let users specify which directories are needed for a specific task
- AI could potentially infer required directories from the task description

## Unity-specific defaults

```
Assets/Scripts
Assets/ScriptableObjects
Assets/Editor
ProjectSettings
Packages
```

This would make Auto-Claude viable for game development projects, which are often the largest and most complex codebases.

## Environment
- Windows 11
- Git 2.x
- Auto-Claude v2.7.2

title: fix: improve Claude CLI detection on Windows with space-containing paths
body:
## Description

This PR fixes Claude CLI detection issues on Windows when the installation path contains spaces (e.g., \).

## Problem

Users with Claude CLI installed via nvm-windows or in paths containing spaces experienced two issues:

1. **Detection failure**: Claude CLI in non-standard paths (like nvm-windows) was not detected
2. **Execution failure**: Even when detected, paths with spaces failed with error: 
## Solution

This PR implements a two-layer solution:

### Layer 1: Detection (Commits 1-2)
- **Commit 1**: Add \ as 4th fallback detection step
  - Searches all PATH directories + registry entries
  - Works regardless of installation location
- **Commit 2**: Prefer .cmd/.exe extensions when multiple paths found
  - Improves accuracy when \ returns multiple results

### Layer 2: Execution (Commit 3)
- **Root cause**: Node.js \ cannot handle space-containing paths in .cmd/.bat files, even with - **Fix**: Use \ with quoted paths for .cmd/.bat files, \ for .exe files
- **Implementation**:
  - Add \ utility to detect .cmd/.bat files
  - Add \ utility for spawn calls
  - Use \ + quoted paths for validation
  - Add 15 comprehensive unit tests

## Technical Details

| Method | .cmd/.bat | .exe | Spaces in Path |
|--------|-----------|------|----------------|
| execFileSync + shell:false | ❌ | ✅ | ❌ |
| execFileSync + shell:true | ❌ | ✅ | ❌ |
| execSync + quoted path | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |

title: Merge fails explicitly due to git hooks returning non-zero exit codes during checkout
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched existing issues and this hasn't been reported

### Area

Backend

### Operating System

Windows

### Version

2.7.2

### What happened?

When running `--merge` (or "Stage with AI Merge" in the UI), the merge fails with:

```
Error: Could not checkout base branch: Already on 'main'
<hook-name> script failed (code 1)
```

The merge is aborted even though there are no actual conflicts.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Have a project with git hooks that run on `post-checkout` (e.g., husky, lefthook, or custom hooks)
2. The hook returns a non-zero exit code for any reason (validation, setup script, etc.)
3. Be already on the base branch (e.g., `main` or `develop`)
4. Attempt to merge a completed spec/worktree

### Expected behavior

The merge should succeed because:
1. The checkout is unnecessary (already on the target branch)
2. Even if checkout runs, hook failures shouldn't block git operations that succeeded

---

### Root cause

In `apps/backend/core/worktree.py`, `merge_worktree()`:
- Always runs `git checkout <base-branch>` without checking if already on that branch
- Treats any non-zero exit code as a checkout failure, including exit codes from post-checkout hooks

---

### Suggested fix

1. Check current branch before checkout; skip if already on target
2. Consider disabling hooks during internal git operations (e.g., `HUSKY=0`, `LEFTHOOK=0`, or `--no-verify` where applicable)
3. Optionally: provide a frontend toggle or CLI flag like `--skip-hooks` for users with strict hook setups

title: fix(frontend) (ACS-175): Integrations page freezes when authenticating another account
body:
## Description

The Integrations settings page freezes/hangs when users try to authenticate another Claude account. Multiple users have reported this issue in Discord.

## Root Cause

**Primary:** Synchronous `alert()` calls blocking the entire Electron renderer process.

**File:** `apps/frontend/src/renderer/components/settings/IntegrationSettings.tsx`

### The Problem

There are **9 `alert()` calls** in the component that block the UI thread:

| Line | Context |
|------|---------|
| 87 | After successful OAuth - **most common trigger** |
| 138 | Profile init failure |
| 143 | Add profile failure |
| 206 | Auth start failure |
| 212 | Auth exception |
| 249 | Save token failure |
| 253 | Save token exception |
| 282 | Auto-switch update failure |
| 286 | Auto-switch exception |

### The Killer Combo (lines 82-88)

```typescript
const unsubscribe = window.electronAPI.onTerminalOAuthToken(async (info) => {
  if (info.success && info.profileId) {
    await loadClaudeProfiles();  // IPC round-trip ~200-500ms
    alert(`✅ Profile authenticated...`);  // ← BLOCKS ENTIRE UI
  }
});
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Settings → Integrations
2. Click "Authenticate" on an existing profile (or add a new one)
3. Complete OAuth flow in browser
4. **App appears frozen** - the `alert()` dialog may be hidden behind another window
5. User cannot interact with the app until they find and dismiss the alert

## Expected Behavior

Authentication should complete with a non-blocking toast notification, allowing the user to continue using the app immediately.

## Additional Issues Found

1. **Multiple components listen for same OAuth event** - `IntegrationSettings`, `ClaudeOAuthFlow`, `EnvConfigModal` all register listeners. If Settings is open during OAuth from another component, the blocking `alert()` fires.

2. **500ms hardcoded delay** in `apps/frontend/src/main/ipc-handlers/terminal-handlers.ts:355` - adds latency but not the main freeze cause.

3. **Missing useEffect dependencies** (lines 70-75) - `loadClaudeProfiles` and `loadAutoSwitchSettings` not in dependency array.

## Proposed Fix

Replace all `alert()` calls with non-blocking `toast()` notifications:

```typescript
// Before (blocking)
alert(`✅ Profile authenticated successfully!`);

// After (non-blocking)  
import { useToast } from '../../hooks/use-toast';

const { toast } = useToast();

toast({
  title: "Profile Authenticated",
  description: info.email ? `Connected as ${info.email}` : "Authentication complete.",
});
```

## Affected Files

- `apps/frontend/src/renderer/components/settings/IntegrationSettings.tsx` (primary)
- `apps/frontend/src/main/ipc-handlers/terminal-handlers.ts` (secondary - 500ms delay)

## Environment

- Version: 2.7.2+
- Platform: All (macOS, Windows, Linux)

body:
### Checklist

### Area

Backend

### Operating System

Windows

### Version

latest executable from GitHub

### What happened?

## Bug Description
Auto Claude fails to automatically detect Claude Code when the Windows username contains spaces.

## Environment
- **OS**: Windows 11 (or 10)
- **Username**: `OXFAM MONS` (contains a space)
- **Claude Code Version**: 2.1.1
- **Auto Claude Version**: [check in the repo, probably latest]

## Workaround Found
Manually specifying the path in `.env` with escaped spaces works:
```env
CLAUDE_PATH=C:\Users\OXFAM MONS\AppData\Roaming\npm\claude.cmd
```

## Root Cause (Suspected)
The automatic detection script likely doesn't properly escape spaces in Windows paths when executing the `claude` command.

## Suggested Fix
- Wrap the detected path in quotes when spawning the Claude Code process
- Or use proper path escaping for Windows paths with spaces

## Additional Context
This issue affects any Windows user whose username contains spaces, which is common in corporate environments (e.g., "John Smith", "Company Name", etc.)
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install Claude Code via npm on a Windows machine where the username contains spaces

3. Run Auto Claude with default configuration (empty `CLAUDE_PATH` in `.env`)
4. Try to create a new project
5. Error occurs: "Failed to initialize Claude: Command failed with exit code 1"

### Expected behavior

## Expected Behavior
Auto Claude should automatically detect Claude Code even when the path contains spaces.

## Actual Behavior

title: fix(windows): resolve Claude CLI detection race condition on GUI launch
body:
## Summary
- Fixes race condition where version check runs before settings load, causing Claude CLI to show "not found" initially
- Suppresses expected "node is not recognized" error on Windows with nvm-windows + GUI launch
- Claude CLI now detects correctly immediately on startup without requiring manual refresh

## Problem
When Auto Claude starts from Windows GUI (Start Menu, desktop shortcut) - not terminal:
1. **Race condition**: `CLAUDE_CODE_CHECK_VERSION` IPC called before user settings load, so `getToolInfo('claude')` did fresh detection ignoring user config
2. **npm.cmd failure**: With nvm-windows, `node` isn't in PATH when launched from GUI, causing `npm.cmd config get prefix` to fail with "node is not recognized"

## Solution
### Change 1: Make `getToolInfo()` respect user configuration
- Added `getUserConfiguredPath()` helper to extract user-configured paths
- Added `validateToolByType()` helper to validate paths by tool type
- Updated `getToolInfo()` to check user config FIRST before fresh detection

### Change 2: Suppress expected Windows error
- Added check in `getNpmGlobalPrefixAsync()` to detect expected "is not recognized" error on Windows
- Only logs error if it's NOT the expected nvm-windows issue

## Files Changed
| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `apps/frontend/src/main/cli-tool-manager.ts` | Added helpers, updated `getToolInfo()` |
| `apps/frontend/src/main/env-utils.ts` | Suppressed expected Windows error |

title: OAuth Login Command Migration
body: The Electron frontend app currently uses `claude setup-token` for OAuth authentication, which returns tokens with limited scopes (`user:inference` only). This prevents the app from accessing the `/usage` API endpoint required for monitoring per-account usage. This task migrates the OAuth flow to use the `/login` command within an interactive Claude CLI session, which provides the full OAuth scopes (`user:inference` + `user:profile`) necessary for usage tracking.

title: fix(frontend): quote Claude CLI paths containing spaces on Windows
body:
## Base Branch

- [x] This PR targets the `develop` branch (required for all feature/fix PRs)
- [ ] This PR targets `main` (hotfix only - maintainers)

## Description

Fixes ACS-176. On Windows, when the username or path contains spaces (e.g., `C:\Users\Jane Smith\AppData\Roaming\npm\claude.cmd`), Claude CLI detection and execution failed in multiple places. This PR also addresses several security vulnerabilities and PowerShell compatibility issues.

### Initial Fixes (Windows Path Quoting)

1. **CLI Tool Detection (`cli-tool-manager.ts`)**: Path wasn't quoted when executing with `shell: true` for `.cmd` files during validation
2. **Changelog Generation (`formatter.ts`)**: Generated Python scripts didn't use `shell=True` for `.cmd/.bat` files
3. **Version Analysis (`version-suggester.ts`)**: Same issue with generated Python scripts

This fix wraps commands in quotes when shell mode is enabled AND the path contains spaces, and ensures generated Python scripts use `subprocess.run(shell=True)` for Windows batch files.

### Code Refactoring

- **Extracted shared utilities** in `env-utils.ts`:
  - `preparePythonSubprocessCommand()`: For Python subprocess generation (formatter, version-suggester)
  - `prepareShellCommand()`: For Node.js child_process execution (cli-tool-manager)
  - Eliminated ~60 lines of duplicated code across 3 files

### Security Fixes

1. **Case-insensitive extension check** (`env-utils.ts`):
   - Windows file extensions are case-insensitive (`.CMD`, `.Bat`, `.BAT` etc.)
   - Both `preparePythonSubprocessCommand()` and `prepareShellCommand()` now use `toLowerCase()` before checking for `.cmd`/`.bat` extensions

2. **Shell injection vulnerability fix** (`formatter.ts`):
   - When `needsShell=true`, now uses `shlex.quote()` to safely escape the prompt
   - Prevents shell metacharacter injection via user input

3. **Shell injection vulnerability fix** (`version-suggester.ts`):
   - Uses base64 encoding for the prompt (avoids string escaping issues)
   - When `needsShell=true`, uses `shlex.quote()` to safely escape the prompt
   - Prevents cmd.exe metacharacter injection (`%`, `^`, `&`, `|`, `<`, `>`, etc.)

4. **Path validation for user-configured paths** (`formatter.ts`, `version-suggester.ts`, `env-utils.ts`):
   - Added `isSecurePath()` validation to prevent command injection via malicious Settings configuration
   - Validates paths don't contain dangerous characters (`; & | ${} [] <> ! " ^`, env vars, directory traversal, newlines)
   - Throws descriptive error if validation fails

### PowerShell Compatibility Fixes (#865, #866, #867)

PowerShell terminals use different command syntax than bash/cmd.exe, causing failures in Claude CLI operations:

1. **Shell Type Detection** (`pty-manager.ts`, `terminal-lifecycle.ts`):
   - Added `detectShellType()` to identify PowerShell, cmd.exe, bash, zsh, fish from shell path
   - Added `shellType` field to `TerminalProcess` interface
   - Shell type detected and stored on terminal creation

2. **Shell-Aware Command Utilities** (`shell-escape.ts`):
   - `buildPathAssignment()` - PATH syntax: `$env:PATH = '...'` (PowerShell) vs `PATH='...'` (bash) vs `set "PATH=..."` (cmd)
   - `buildEnvVarAssignment()` - ENV syntax: `$env:VAR = '...'` vs `VAR='...'` vs `set "VAR=..."`
   - `buildEnvVarReference()` - Variable reference: `$env:VAR` vs `$VAR` vs `%VAR%`
   - `buildCommandInvocation()` - Adds `&` call operator for .cmd/.bat files in PowerShell
   - `buildCdCommandForShell()` - Shell-specific cd syntax

3. **Updated Command Generation**:
   - **Claude CLI invocation** (`claude-integration-handler.ts`): Uses shell-type-aware PATH and command syntax
   - **Authentication handlers** (`terminal-handlers.ts`): Uses shell-type-aware environment variable syntax

4. **Bash Availability Check** (`claude-integration-handler.ts`):
   - Added `isBashAvailable()` to detect bash on Windows (Git Bash, MSYS2, Cygwin)
   - When bash unavailable, uses native PowerShell/cmd syntax for OAuth token authentication
   - Prevents silent failures for Windows users without bash

5. **File Permissions Fix** (`claude-integration-handler.ts`):
   - `mode: 0o600` is Unix-only - now only applied on non-Windows platforms

6. **Echo Command Fix** (`terminal-handlers.ts`):
   - Removed extra quotes that made echo command a string literal instead of executable

### Test Fixes

- **Added missing mocks** in `cli-tool-manager.test.ts`:
  - Added `prepareShellCommand` and `preparePythonSubprocessCommand` to the `env-utils` mock
  - These functions are now used by `cli-tool-manager.ts` after the refactoring
  - All 21 tests now pass

- **Fixed requestAnimationFrame mock** in `useXterm.test.ts`:
  - Removed duplicate mock causing TypeScript type errors
  - All 20 tests now pass

- **Removed unused import** (`useXterm.test.ts`):
  - Removed `renderHook` which was not being used

title: Bug: Subtasks list shows UUIDs instead of subtask titles
body:
In the task details view, the **Subtasks** tab is rendering each subtask row header as a raw **UUID** (e.g., `1cfaf362-adff-449f-bca7-69bb41e3ac08`) rather than the subtask’s human-readable **title**. This makes the subtasks list hard to scan and undermines the purpose of subtasks as a quick checklist. **Steps to reproduce:** 1. Open any task that has subtasks. 2. Click the **Subtasks** tab. 3. Observe the heading/title shown for each subtask row. **Actual result:**
Each subtask row displays a UUID as the title (appears to be an internal ID). **Expected result:**
Each subtask row displays the subtask **title** (same text as the actual subtask/task name), optionally alongside metadata (status, assignee, etc.). **Impact:** * Poor usability/readability: impossible to quickly understand subtasks at a glance. * Increases time to navigate and validate work items, especially on issues with many subtasks. **Notes / suspected cause:**
Likely binding the UI label to `id` / `uuid` instead of `title` / `name` from the subtask object (or the API response is missing the title field and the UI falls back to ID). **Acceptance criteria:** * Subtask list rows show the correct **subtask title** (not UUIDs) for all subtasks. * No regressions to subtask ordering, completion status, or click-through behavior. * If the title is missing, show a safe fallback like “Untitled subtask” (not the UUID), and optionally log/report the data issue.

fix(ui): display subtask titles instead of UUIDs (#844)
body:
## Summary

Fixes the Subtasks tab displaying raw UUIDs instead of human-readable subtask titles. The list was showing values like `1cfaf362-adff-449f-bca7-69bb41e3ac08` instead of the actual subtask descriptions, making it impossible to quickly understand subtasks at a glance.

Fixes #844

## Root Cause

In `TaskSubtasks.tsx`, line 72 was rendering `{subtask.id}` (the UUID) instead of `{subtask.title}` (the human-readable description). The data structure and upstream code were correct - only the display binding was wrong.

## Solution

- Changed the display from `subtask.id` to `subtask.title` 
- Added a fallback to `'Untitled subtask'` for edge cases where title might be missing
- Updated the tooltip to show the full title (useful when text is truncated)

This follows the same pattern already used in `PhaseProgressIndicator.tsx:245`: `${subtask.title || subtask.id}`

## Changes

- `apps/frontend/src/renderer/components/task-detail/TaskSubtasks.tsx` (lines 69-78)
  - Line 72: `{subtask.id}` → `{subtask.title || 'Untitled subtask'}`
  - Line 76: Updated tooltip to show title instead of UUID

## Testing

- [x] TypeScript type check passes
- [x] All 63 task-store tests pass
- [x] ESLint passes (pre-existing warnings only)
- [x] Pre-commit hooks pass

## Cross-Platform Compatibility

This is a pure React/TypeScript rendering fix with no platform-specific code. Works identically on Windows, macOS, and Linux.

title: MCP Tools Not Available to Agents: Context7 tool name mismatch & Custom server permissions missing
body:
## Summary

Two issues prevent MCP tools from working properly for agents:

1. **Context7 `query-docs` tool is permission-gated** - Tool name mismatch in code
2. **Custom MCP server tools not available** - Permissions not granted for custom servers

## Issue 1: Context7 Tool Name Mismatch

### Symptom
- `resolve-library-id` ✅ works
- `query-docs` ⚠️ permission-gated (asks for permission every time)

### Root Cause
`CONTEXT7_TOOLS` in `apps/backend/agents/tools_pkg/models.py` has the wrong tool name:

```python
# Current (wrong):
CONTEXT7_TOOLS = [
    "mcp__context7__resolve-library-id",
    "mcp__context7__get-library-docs",  # ❌ Wrong name
]

# Should be:
CONTEXT7_TOOLS = [
    "mcp__context7__resolve-library-id",
    "mcp__context7__query-docs",  # ✅ Actual tool name from Context7 MCP
]
```

### Fix
Simple one-line change in `apps/backend/agents/tools_pkg/models.py` line 49.

---

## Issue 2: Custom MCP Server Tools Not Available

### Symptom
- Custom MCP server (e.g., `docs-langchain`) is configured in UI
- Server shows as "added" to agent (e.g., Coder)
- Server health check passes (325ms response)
- **But agent cannot find or use the server's tools** (e.g., `SearchDocsByLangChain`)

### Root Cause
Custom MCP servers are started correctly, but **no permissions are granted for their tools**.

In `apps/backend/core/client.py` (lines 620-638), permissions are only granted for known tool lists:
- `CONTEXT7_TOOLS`
- `LINEAR_TOOLS`
- `GRAPHITI_MCP_TOOLS`
- `browser_tools_permissions`

**Custom server tools like `mcp__docs-langchain__SearchDocsByLangChain` are never permitted!**

### Proposed Fix

**1. Add permission grants for custom server tools in `client.py` (~line 638):**

```python
*[f"{tool}(*)" for tool in browser_tools_permissions],
# Grant permission for all tools from enabled custom servers
*[
    f"mcp__{custom.get('id')}__*(*)"
    for custom in mcp_config.get("CUSTOM_MCP_SERVERS", [])
    if custom.get("id") in required_servers
],
```

**2. Add custom server tools to allowed_tools list in `permissions.py` (~line 78):**

```python
# Add custom server tool patterns
custom_servers = mcp_config.get("CUSTOM_MCP_SERVERS", []) if mcp_config else []
for custom in custom_servers:
    server_id = custom.get("id")
    if server_id in required_servers:
        tools.append(f"mcp__{server_id}__*")
```

> **Note:** Need to verify Claude SDK supports wildcard patterns in permissions. If not, alternative is to query MCP server for tool list at startup.

---

## Files to Modify

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `apps/backend/agents/tools_pkg/models.py` | Fix Context7 tool name (line 49) |
| `apps/backend/core/client.py` | Add custom server permissions (~line 638) |
| `apps/backend/agents/tools_pkg/permissions.py` | Add custom server tools to allowed list (~line 78) |

## Environment
- Auto-Claude Desktop App (Electron)
- Linux
- Tested with Coder/Planner agents

title: Insights feature fails with "Process exited with code 1" on systems with Python 3.9
body:
## Description

The Insights feature fails silently with "Process exited with code 1" on macOS systems where the default `python3` is Python 3.9.x. No error message or stack trace is shown to the user, making debugging extremely difficult.

## Root Cause

The `core/auth.py` module uses Python 3.10+ union type syntax:

```python
def get_token_from_keychain() -> str | None:  # Line 35
```

The `|` operator for type hints was introduced in [PEP 604](https://peps.python.org/pep-0604/) and requires Python 3.10+. On Python 3.9, this causes:

```
TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for |: 'type' and 'NoneType'
```

Since this error occurs at import time in `insights_runner.py`, the process exits immediately with code 1.

## Environment

- **OS:** macOS (stock Python 3.9.6 at `/usr/bin/python3`)
- **Auto-Claude Version:** Latest (as of January 2026)
- **Python:** 3.9.6 (system default)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install Auto-Claude on a Mac with default system Python 3.9
2. Open any project
3. Click on Insights feature
4. Observe "Process exited with code 1" with no additional feedback

## Expected Behavior

Either:
- Insights works on Python 3.9+
- OR a clear error message indicates Python 3.10+ is required

## Suggested Fixes

**Option A (Recommended): Use backward-compatible type hints**

Replace all `X | None` syntax with `Optional[X]` from the `typing` module:

```python
from typing import Optional

def get_token_from_keychain() -> Optional[str]:
```

This maintains compatibility with Python 3.9+ while being semantically identical.

**Option B: Bundle Python runtime**

Ship Auto-Claude with its own Python 3.10+ runtime or virtual environment, independent of the system Python.

**Option C: Add Python version check**

Add a startup check that validates Python version and shows a clear error:

```python
import sys
if sys.version_info < (3, 10):
    print("Error: Auto-Claude requires Python 3.10+", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)
```

## Workaround

Users can work around this by:
1. Installing Python 3.12 via Homebrew: `brew install python@3.12`
2. Creating a venv in the backend directory with all requirements
3. Updating runner shebangs to use the venv Python

## Additional Context

The `claude-agent-sdk` dependency may also be missing from some installations, causing a secondary `ModuleNotFoundError`. Consider verifying all requirements are installed during app startup.

title: Coder Agent fails to run npm commands - not included in dynamic allowlist for Node.js projects
body:
## Description

The Coder Agent is unable to execute `npm install` and other npm commands, even when working on a Node.js/Next.js project. This causes automated workflows to fail repeatedly when tasks require npm operations (e.g., syncing `package-lock.json` after adding dependencies).

## Root Cause

The Dynamic Command Allowlist system does not automatically include `npm` commands for detected Node.js projects. The Coder Agent has Bash tool access (confirmed in `AGENT_CONFIGS`), but the security layer blocks npm execution.

## Environment

- **Project Type:** Next.js (Node.js)
- **Files Present:** `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `node_modules/`
- **Auto-Claude Version:** Latest (as of January 2026)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a Next.js project in Auto-Claude
2. Create a spec that requires adding a new npm dependency
3. Run the automated build
4. Observe Coder Agent successfully edits `package.json`
5. Observe Coder Agent fails to run `npm install` to sync `package-lock.json`
6. QA Agent rejects the work due to unsynchronized lock file
7. Loop continues indefinitely (7+ rejections observed)

## Expected Behavior

For Node.js projects (detected via `package.json`), the following commands should be auto-allowed:
- `npm`, `npm install`, `npm ci`, `npm run *`
- `npx`
- `yarn`, `pnpm` (if detected)

## Suggested Fixes

**Option A: Enhance stack detection for Node.js**

Update the security profile generator to detect Node.js projects and add npm commands:

```python
# In security profile generation
if Path("package.json").exists():
    allowed_commands.extend([
        "npm", "npm install", "npm ci", "npm run",
        "npx", "yarn", "pnpm"
    ])
```

**Option B: Document manual allowlist configuration**

Improve documentation for `.auto-claude-allowlist` file. Many users don't know this file exists or how to use it.

**Option C: Prompt user on first npm command**

When Coder Agent attempts an npm command that's not allowlisted, prompt the user: "Allow npm commands for this project? [Yes/No]"

**Option D: Project-level UI configuration + error surfacing**

1. Add a project-level settings panel in the Auto-Claude UI where users can configure additional allowed commands without manually editing files
2. Surface blocked command errors from log files to the UI, showing users exactly which command was blocked and why
3. Provide a one-click "Allow this command" action when a blocked command is detected

This would significantly improve UX by:
- Making the allowlist discoverable through the settings UI
- Showing clear feedback when commands are blocked (instead of silent failure)
- Allowing users to quickly unblock commands without leaving the app

## Workaround

Users can manually create `.auto-claude-allowlist` in their project root:

```
npm
npm install
npm run
npm ci
npx
yarn
pnpm
```

## Additional Context

The current security model mentions "Dynamic Command Allowlist - Only approved commands based on detected project stack" in the README, but the Node.js stack detection appears incomplete or not implemented for npm commands.

title: Parallel worktree workflow lacks merge ordering/rebase tooling - leads to conflict trainwrecks
body:
## Problem Summary

The system advertises parallel spec execution ("Run multiple builds simultaneously with up to 12 agent terminals") but provides no tooling to handle merging multiple divergent worktrees back to main. Users end up with cascading merge conflicts and lost code.

## The Contradiction

**What the system promises:**
- README: "Parallel Execution - Run multiple builds simultaneously with up to 12 agent terminals"
- `worktree.py`: "This allows multiple specs to be worked on simultaneously"
- Kanban-style UI implies queuing/parallel work

**What the system actually handles well:**
- Sequential: Feature A → merge → Feature B → merge → Feature C

**What breaks:**
```
Feature A ─┐
Feature B ─┼─→ merge all at once → conflict hell, lost code
Feature C ─┘
```

## What EXISTS vs What's MISSING

| Exists | Missing |
|--------|---------|
| Parallel worktrees | Merge queue/ordering system |
| Per-spec locking | Rebase automation |
| Concurrency limit (5 file merges) | Warnings about parallel merge conflicts |
| Priority field on merges (appears unused) | Sequential merge enforcement |
| Worktree count warnings (10+) | Guidance on safe merge order |

## User Impact

When a user creates multiple specs via the Kanban board and runs builds on them, they have no guidance or tooling for:
1. What order to merge them
2. Auto-rebasing later specs against merged changes
3. Preventing conflicts before they happen
4. Recovering when conflicts cascade

The user is left to manually figure out merge ordering and resolve potentially massive conflicts.

## Suggested Solutions (pick one or combine)

1. **Add guardrails** - Warn or prevent running a new spec while another is unmerged
2. **Add merge queue** - System tracks merge order, auto-rebases pending specs against main after each merge
3. **Add rebase tooling** - `--rebase` flag to update a spec's worktree against current main before merging
4. **Fix the messaging** - If parallel execution isn't fully supported, don't advertise it; document the sequential workflow clearly

## Reproduction

1. Create 3+ specs via the UI
2. Run builds on all of them (they complete on separate worktrees/branches)
3. Try to merge all 3 back to main
4. Experience conflict cascade, especially if specs touched overlapping files

## Environment

- Auto-Claude version: 2.7.3-beta.1
- Issue discovered through user workflow friction

title: `[UX] Settings auto-save renders "Save" redundant and "Cancel" dysfunctional`
