title: fix(insights): add Git Bash path detection for Windows
body: ## Base Branch - [x] This PR targets the `develop` branch (required for all feature/fix PRs) - [ ] This PR targets `main` (hotfix only - maintainers) ## Description ### What happened? When using the **Insights** feature on Windows, users encounter a fatal error: ``` Claude Code on Windows requires git-bash ProcessError: Command failed with exit code 1 ``` The Insights chat becomes completely unusable, displaying the error message instead of responding to user queries. ### Why did this happen? The Claude Code CLI on Windows requires `git-bash` (bash.exe) to execute shell commands. This is communicated via the `CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH` environment variable. The **root cause** is an inconsistency between two code paths: | Component | Location | Git Bash Detection | |-----------|----------|-------------------| | `AgentProcess` | `agent-process.ts` | ✅ Has detection logic | | `InsightsConfig` | `insights/config.ts` | ❌ **Missing detection** | When the Electron app spawns a Python subprocess for Insights, it uses `InsightsConfig.getProcessEnv()` to build the environment variables. This method was missing the `CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH` detection that `AgentProcess.setupProcessEnvironment()` already had. As a result, when the Python backend invokes Claude Code CLI, the CLI cannot find git-bash and fails with the error shown above. ### How did we fix it? 1. **Extract shared utility function** (DRY principle) - Moved `deriveGitBashPath()` from `agent-process.ts` to `env-utils.ts` - This function derives the `bash.exe` path from a given `git.exe` path - Handles various Git for Windows installation structures: - `Git/cmd/git.exe` → `Git/bin/bash.exe` - `Git/bin/git.exe` → `Git/bin/bash.exe` - `Git/mingw64/bin/git.exe` → `Git/bin/bash.exe` - `Git/mingw32/bin/git.exe` → `Git/bin/bash.exe` 2. **Add Git Bash detection to InsightsConfig** - Added the same detection logic to `InsightsConfig.getProcessEnv()` - Now sets `CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH` environment variable when Git is found 3. **Add comprehensive unit tests** - 10 new test cases covering all Git installation path variants - Tests for non-Windows platforms (should return null) - Tests for paths with spaces - Tests for fallback path logic 4. **Clean up stale mocks** - Removed incorrect `deriveGitBashPath` mock from `cli-tool-manager` in test files - Added correct mock location in `env-utils` mock ## Related Issue Related to upstream issue: anthropics/claude-code#11496 ## Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix - [ ] ✨ New feature - [ ] 📚 Documentation - [x] ♻️ Refactor - [x] 🧪 Test ## Area - [x] Frontend - [ ] Backend - [ ] Fullstack ## Commit Message Format `fix(insights): add Git Bash path detection for Windows` ## Checklist - [x] I've synced with `develop` branch - [x] I've tested my changes locally - [x] I've followed the code principles (SOLID, DRY, KISS) - [x] My PR is small and focused (< 400 lines ideally) ## Platform Testing Checklist **CRITICAL:** This project supports Windows, macOS, and Linux. Platform-specific bugs are a common source of breakage. - [x] **Windows tested** (tested locally, fix verified working) - [ ] **macOS tested** (CI will verify) - [ ] **Linux tested** (CI will verify) - [x] Used centralized `platform/` module instead of direct `process.platform` checks - [x] No hardcoded paths (used dynamic Git path detection) **If you only have access to one OS:** CI now tests on all platforms. Ensure all checks pass before submitting. ## CI/Testing Requirements - [ ] All CI checks pass on **all platforms** (Windows, macOS, Linux) - [x] All existing tests pass (1771 passed locally) - [x] New features include test coverage - [x] Bug fixes include regression tests ## Screenshots | Before | After | |--------|-------| | || ## Feature Toggle - [x] N/A - Feature is complete and ready for all users ## Breaking Changes **Breaking:** No ## Files Changed | File | Change | |------|--------| | `env-utils.ts` | Added shared `deriveGitBashPath()` function | | `agent-process.ts` | Removed duplicate function, now imports from `env-utils.ts` | | `insights/config.ts` | Added Git Bash detection in `getProcessEnv()` | | `env-utils.test.ts` | Added 10 unit tests for `deriveGitBashPath()` | | `agent-process.test.ts` | Fixed mock location | | `ipc-handlers.test.ts` | Removed stale mock | ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Detects Git Bash on Windows and injects its path into the process environment to improve CLI behavior. * **Integration** * Environment assembly now includes discovered Git Bash info via a dependency-injectable helper for more consistent Windows runtime setups. * **Tests** * Expanded tests covering Windows and non-Windows scenarios, multiple Git Bash layouts, path quoting, env-var precedence, and platform-specific behavior. ✏️ Tip: You can customize this high-level summary in your review settings.

title: gh CLI not found when creating PRs from GUI despite being installed
body:
Summary

The Electron GUI doesn't pass the detected gh CLI path to the Python backend via the GITHUB_CLI_PATH environment variable, causing subprocess calls to fail when the GUI is launched from Finder/Dock (not terminal). While gh_executable.py exists with proper fallback logic, some code paths use hardcoded "gh" strings instead of calling get_gh_executable().

Problem Description

Root Cause Chain:

1. Frontend detects gh correctly (cli-tool-manager.ts) but does NOT set GITHUB_CLI_PATH env var for Python subprocess
2. Backend expects GITHUB_CLI_PATH (gh_executable.py:107) but it's never set
3. Some files use hardcoded "gh" instead of calling get_gh_executable():

```
- runners/github/gh_client.py:132 - cmd = ["gh"] + args
- runners/github/bot_detection.py:157 - ["gh", "api", "user"]
```

4. When GUI launches from Finder/Dock, subprocess PATH doesn't include /opt/homebrew/bin

Why it works in terminal but not GUI:

title: "Require Human Review Before Coding" Feature Broken
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched existing issues and this hasn't been reported

### Area

Frontend

### Operating System

macOS

### Version

2.7.4



## Summary

When creating a task with "Require human review before coding" enabled, the workflow stops after planning completes with no way to approve/continue. Only a "Stop Task" button is available - no approval UI appears.

## Environment

- **Application**: Auto-Claude Kanban Board
- **Feature**: "Require human review before coding" checkbox in task creation
- **Context**: UI-based task creation and execution

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the Kanban board
2. Click "Create New Task"
3. Enter a task description
4. **Enable "Require human review before coding" checkbox**
5. Click "Create Task"
6. Wait for planning phase to complete

## Expected Behavior

After planning completes:
- Task should transition to `human_review` status with `reviewReason: 'plan_review'`
- UI should display approval controls (Approve Plan, Request Changes, etc.)
- User can review the spec/plan and approve before coding begins

## Actual Behavior

After planning completes:
- Task shows "In Progress" status with "Coding" badge at 0%
- Planning phase shows as "Complete" in logs
- Coding phase shows as "Pending"
- **Only "Stop Task" and "Close" buttons available - NO approval UI**
- Workflow is stuck with no way to continue

## Screenshots

See `/Users/user/Desktop/auto-claude/bug/` folder:
- `SCR-20260117-basq.png` - Task creation with "Require human review" checked
- `SCR-20260117-baky.png` - Kanban showing "Coding" badge at 0%
- `SCR-20260117-banw.png` - Logs showing Planning=Complete, Coding=Pending, only Stop button
- `SCR-20260117-baqq.png` - Files tab, still only Stop button

---

## Root Cause Analysis

### The Problem Chain

1. **UI creates task** with `requireReviewBeforeCoding: true` in metadata
2. **`agent-manager.ts:144`** does NOT pass `--auto-approve` flag to backend
3. **Backend `spec_runner.py`** runs with `auto_approve=False`
4. **Review checkpoint** tries to show interactive menu but **stdin is NOT a TTY** (subprocess context)
5. **`_fallback_menu()`** calls `input()` which raises `EOFError` immediately
6. **Review returns as NOT approved** → script exits with `sys.exit(1)`
7. **UI sees process exit** but task status remains `in_progress` instead of `human_review`
8. **Approval UI never renders** because `task.status !== 'human_review'`

### Code Path Trace

```
Frontend:
  TaskCreationWizard.tsx:350 → sets metadata.requireReviewBeforeCoding = true
  agent-manager.ts:144 → if (!metadata?.requireReviewBeforeCoding) args.push('--auto-approve')
                         // Does NOT push --auto-approve when review required

Backend:
  spec_runner.py:288-292 → orchestrator.run(auto_approve=args.auto_approve)  // False
  orchestrator.py:412 → self._run_review_checkpoint(auto_approve)  // False
  orchestrator.py:629-632 → run_review_checkpoint(spec_dir, auto_approve=False)

  reviewer.py:200-204 → if auto_approve: state.approve() ... return  // SKIPPED (auto_approve=False)
  reviewer.py:248-265 → while True: ... select_menu(...)  // ENTERS INTERACTIVE LOOP

  menu.py:108-110 → if not INTERACTIVE: return _fallback_menu(...)  // INTERACTIVE=False (no TTY)
  menu.py:234-237 → choice = input("Your choice: ")  // Raises EOFError (no stdin)
                   except (EOFError, KeyboardInterrupt): return None

  reviewer.py:267-268 → if choice is None: ... // User "quit" - review NOT approved
  reviewer.py returns → state.is_approved() = False

  spec_runner.py:309-327:
    if not review_state.is_approved():
        print_status("Build cannot start: spec not approved.", "error")
        sys.exit(1)  // ← EXITS WITH ERROR

Frontend (continued):
  Process exits with code 1
  Task stays in 'in_progress' status
  Execution phase badge shows "Coding" (incorrect)
  human_review status never set → approval UI never shown
```

### Key Files Involved

| File | Line(s) | Issue |
|------|---------|-------|
| `apps/frontend/src/main/agent/agent-manager.ts` | 144-147 | Passes/omits `--auto-approve` based on `requireReviewBeforeCoding` |
| `apps/backend/runners/spec_runner.py` | 305-327 | Exits with error if spec not approved (no non-interactive handling) |
| `apps/backend/review/reviewer.py` | 177-270 | Review checkpoint has no "pause and wait" mode for UI |
| `apps/backend/ui/menu.py` | 206-249 | `_fallback_menu` returns `None` on `EOFError` (interpreted as "quit") |
| `apps/frontend/src/main/project-store.ts` | 558-689 | Status determination logic - never receives `human_review` signal |

---

## Proposed Fix (High-Level)

The core issue is that the backend has no mechanism to **pause and signal "waiting for human review"** in a non-interactive context. The frontend needs to:
1. Receive this signal
2. Show the approval UI
3. Send approval back to continue execution

### Option A: Backend "Pause and Poll" Approach

1. **Backend changes**:
   - Add new mode to `run_review_checkpoint()`: `mode='ui'` (in addition to `interactive` and `auto`)
   - In UI mode: Write `plan.status = 'human_review'`, `planStatus = 'review'` to `implementation_plan.json`
   - Exit cleanly (code 0) instead of failing
   - Add new script `resume_after_approval.py` or enhance `run.py` to resume from review

2. **Frontend changes**:
   - Detect `human_review` + `plan_review` status during plan polling
   - Show approval UI (already exists in `TaskReview.tsx`)
   - On approval: Call new IPC to resume execution

### Option B: Frontend "Gate Before Coding" Approach

1. **Split execution into phases**:
   - Phase 1: Spec/planning only (no `--auto-approve` check)
   - Gate: Frontend checks `requireReviewBeforeCoding` and waits for user action
   - Phase 2: Coding (only starts after explicit user approval via UI)

2. **Implementation**:
   - Modify `agent-manager.ts` to add `--no-build` when `requireReviewBeforeCoding=true`
   - After spec creation, set task to `human_review` with `reviewReason: 'plan_review'`
   - Show approval UI
   - On approval, start `run.py` separately

### Recommended: Option B

Option B is cleaner because:
- No complex state synchronization between backend pause/resume
- Leverages existing `--no-build` flag
- Frontend already has `TaskReview` component for approval flow
- Simpler to implement and test

---

## Impact

- **Severity**: High - Feature is completely non-functional
- **Affected Users**: Anyone using "Require human review before coding" option
- **Workaround**: None - users must disable the option to use the system

## Additional Notes

- The `reviewReason: 'plan_review'` type already exists in `task.ts:15`
- The badge "Approve Plan" already exists in `TaskHeader.tsx:80`
- The infrastructure for plan approval exists but the **trigger path is broken**

title: fix(windows): resolve pywin32 DLL loading failure on Python 3.8+
body:
## Summary
- Fix pywin32 DLL loading failure on Windows for bundled Python packages
- Add PYTHONSTARTUP bootstrap script to call `os.add_dll_directory()` for Python 3.8+
- Add comprehensive tests for the pywin32 environment setup

## Technical Recap: pywin32 Windows Build Issue

### Investigation Summary

18 AI agents (6 agents × 3 rounds) investigated from different angles: GitHub issues, git history, build process, DLL discovery, path resolution, and environment variables. **All 18 agents converged on the same root cause.**

### Root Cause (Confirmed by All Agents)

The packaged `.exe` sets `PYTHONPATH` to the bundled `site-packages/` directory. However:

1. **Python doesn't process `.pth` files for PYTHONPATH directories** - only for proper site-packages
2. `pywin32.pth` never executes, so `win32/` and `win32/lib/` aren't added to `sys.path`
3. `pywin32_bootstrap.py` never runs, so `os.add_dll_directory()` isn't called for `pywin32_system32/`
4. **Result:** `win32api.pyd` not found (wrong path) and `pywintypes312.dll` not found (DLL search path not set)

The DLLs ARE bundled correctly - Python just can't find them at runtime.

### Where's The Fix?

Branch: `fix/windows-pywin32-dll-loading` (commits e7c3000e, ec2e484f, d64db09b)

### Why It Was Never Merged

- **Jan 13:** PR #1005 created with the runtime DLL loading fix (PYTHONSTARTUP approach)
- **Jan 16:** PR #1197 merged instead - this only ensured pywin32 is bundled, not that it loads
- **PR #1005 was left open/unmerged** - the assumption was "if bundled, it works"

## The Fix

### Build-time (`download-python.cjs`):

title: Project analyzer fails to detect monorepo with nested frontend structure (e.g., frontend/app/)
body:
## Problem

Projects with a nested frontend structure are incorrectly detected as `single` instead of `monorepo`, which breaks Puppeteer MCP integration for QA browser testing.

### Example Structure
```
project-root/
├── package.json          # Backend (NestJS)
├── backend/
│   └── api/
│       └── package.json
└── frontend/
    └── app/
        └── package.json  # Frontend (React + Vite)
```

### Expected Behavior
- `project_type: "monorepo"`
- `is_web_frontend: true`
- Puppeteer MCP enabled for QA agents

### Actual Behavior
- `project_type: "single"`
- `is_web_frontend: false`
- Puppeteer MCP **not** enabled, QA phase can't do browser testing

## Root Cause

In `analysis/analyzers/project_analyzer_module.py`:

1. `_detect_project_type()` only checks **1 level deep** for service root files
2. Does not find `frontend/app/package.json` (2 levels deep)
3. Project detected as `single` → `_find_and_analyze_services()` only analyzes root
4. Frontend service not discovered → `is_web_frontend=false`
5. Puppeteer not added to QA agent's MCP servers

## Proposed Fix

Add check for common nested patterns in `_detect_project_type()`:

```python
# Check for frontend/backend separation pattern
# Common pattern: root has package.json (backend) + frontend/ dir with nested package.json
frontend_dir = self.project_dir / "frontend"
if frontend_dir.exists() and frontend_dir.is_dir():
    # Check if frontend has package.json directly or in subdirectory (e.g., frontend/app/)
    has_frontend_service = any((frontend_dir / f).exists() for f in SERVICE_ROOT_FILES)
    if not has_frontend_service:
        # Check one level deep (frontend/app/, frontend/web/, etc.)
        for subdir in frontend_dir.iterdir():
            if subdir.is_dir() and not subdir.name.startswith(".") and subdir.name not in SKIP_DIRS:
                if any((subdir / f).exists() for f in SERVICE_ROOT_FILES):
                    has_frontend_service = True
                    break

    # If root has package.json and frontend has a service, it's a monorepo
    if has_frontend_service and any((self.project_dir / f).exists() for f in SERVICE_ROOT_FILES):
        self.index["project_type"] = "monorepo"
        return
```

Also add `frontend` and `backend` to `service_locations` in `_find_and_analyze_services()`.

## Impact

Without this fix:
- QA agents can't use Puppeteer for browser automation testing
- `PUPPETEER_MCP_ENABLED=true` in `.env` has no effect
- Manual workaround: edit `project_index.json` by hand

## Environment
- Auto Claude version: 2.7.x
- OS: macOS

## Bug Description

When using Claude Opus 4.5 (`claude-opus-4-5-20251101`), Auto-Claude requests `max_tokens: 65537` which exceeds the model's limit of 64000, causing all tasks to fail at the spec_writing phase.

## Error Message

```
API Error: 400 {"type":"error","error":{"type":"invalid_request_error","message":"max_tokens: 65537 > 64000, which is the maximum allowed number of output tokens for claude-opus-4-5-20251101"}}
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a new project in Auto-Claude
2. Set model to Opus
3. Create any task
4. Task fails at phase 6 (SPEC DOCUMENT CREATION) with the above error

## Environment

- Auto-Claude version: Latest from releases
- OS: macOS
- Model: claude-opus-4-5-20251101

## Investigation

- The value 65537 (2^16 + 1) appears to be hardcoded in `app.asar`
- Changing agent profile (auto/complex/etc.) does not change this value
- Adding `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS=64000` to `.env` does not override it
- The issue persists across multiple retry attempts

## Expected Behavior

Auto-Claude should:
1. Use max_tokens ≤ 64000 for Opus 4.5
2. Respect `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` env var if set
3. Ideally, auto-detect model limits and adjust accordingly

Currently, switching to Sonnet instead of Opus avoids this issue.

title: fix(windows): prevent zombie process accumulation on app close
body:
## Summary

Fixes Windows-specific issue where processes accumulate in Task Manager after closing Auto-Claude. This addresses issues #1252, #641, #607, and relates to the previously closed but unmerged PR #753.

### Root Causes Fixed

| # | Issue | File | Fix |
|---|-------|------|-----|
| 1 | SIGTERM/SIGKILL ignored on Windows | `agent-process.ts` | Use `taskkill /f /t` to kill process trees |
| 2 | `killAllProcesses()` resolves immediately | `agent-process.ts` | Wait for process exit events with 10s timeout |
| 3 | PTY daemon never killed on shutdown | `pty-daemon-client.ts` | Kill daemon process in `shutdown()` |
| 4 | App-updater interval never cleared | `app-updater.ts` | Store interval ID and clear on quit |

### Changes

- **`agent-process.ts`**: Windows-aware `killProcess()` using `taskkill /f /t` fallback after `.kill()`, and `killAllProcesses()` that properly waits for process exit events
- **`pty-daemon-client.ts`**: Kill PTY daemon process on shutdown using platform-appropriate method
- **`app-updater.ts`**: Store periodic check interval ID and export `stopPeriodicUpdates()` function
- **`index.ts`**: Call `stopPeriodicUpdates()` in `before-quit` handler
- **`subprocess-spawn.test.ts`**: Update tests to handle platform-specific kill behavior

### Implementation Details

The fix follows the existing pattern from `worktree-handlers.ts` (lines 3033-3061) and uses the centralized platform abstraction (`isWindows()` from `platform/index.ts`) as documented in CLAUDE.md.

**Windows behavior:**
```typescript
// Windows: .kill() then taskkill fallback (SIGTERM/SIGKILL are ignored)
agentProcess.process.kill();
spawn('taskkill', ['/pid', pid.toString(), '/f', '/t'], {
  stdio: 'ignore',
  detached: true
}).unref();
```

**Unix behavior:**
```typescript
// Unix: SIGTERM then SIGKILL
agentProcess.process.kill('SIGTERM');
setTimeout(() => {
  agentProcess.process.kill('SIGKILL');
}, 5000);
```

body:
## Base Branch

- [x] This PR targets the `develop` branch (required for all feature/fix PRs)
- [ ] This PR targets `main` (hotfix only - maintainers)

## Description

Fixes a Time-Of-Check-To-Time-Of-Use (TOCTOU) race condition in the frontend spec number lock mechanism. The redundant `existsSync()` check before `writeFileSync(..., { flag: 'wx' })` allowed concurrent processes to both pass the check and attempt to create the lock file, leading to duplicate spec numbers (e.g., multiple `006-*` directories).

- [x] N/A - Feature is complete and ready for all users

## Breaking Changes

**Breaking:** No

## Root Cause Analysis

The original code had a TOCTOU vulnerability:

```typescript
// BEFORE - Race condition between check and create
if (!existsSync(this.lockFile)) {          // Process A & B both pass this check
  writeFileSync(this.lockFile, ..., { flag: 'wx' });  // Both try to create
}
```

The fix removes the redundant check and relies solely on the atomic `flag: 'wx'`:

```typescript
// AFTER - Atomic operation, no race condition
writeFileSync(this.lockFile, String(process.pid), { flag: 'wx' });
// Throws EEXIST if file exists - handled in catch block
```

This matches the Python backend's correct implementation using `os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL`.

title: Incorrect backend path resolution in subprocess-runner.ts breaks GitHub PR features
body:
## What happened?

GitHub PR review and other GitHub automation features fail with the error:
```
"GitHub automation module not installed. This project does not have the GitHub runner configured."
```

**Root cause:** The `getBackendPath()` function in `subprocess-runner.ts` used 5 parent directory traversals (`..`) instead of 3, causing it to look for the backend in a non-existent location outside the repository.

The compiled frontend output is flattened to `apps/frontend/out/main/index.js`, so `__dirname` resolves to `apps/frontend/out/main/`. To reach `apps/backend/` requires only 3 `..` traversals, not 5.

**File:** `apps/frontend/src/main/ipc-handlers/github/utils/subprocess-runner.ts`

**Incorrect code (line 261-262):**
```typescript
// Dev mode: from dist/main -> ../../backend (apps/frontend/out/main -> apps/backend)
path.resolve(__dirname, '..', '..', '..', '..', '..', 'backend'),
```

**Correct code:**
```typescript
// Dev mode: from out/main -> ../../backend (apps/frontend/out/main -> apps/backend)
path.resolve(__dirname, '..', '..', '..', 'backend'),
```

## Steps to reproduce

1. Clone the repo and run `npm run install:all`
2. Run `npm run dev`
3. Open a project that has GitHub PRs
4. Try to use PR review feature
5. See error in console: "GitHub automation module not installed"

## Expected behavior

The GitHub PR features should work correctly by finding the backend at `apps/backend/` relative to the compiled frontend at `apps/frontend/out/main/`.

## Logs / Screenshots

```
[GitHub PR] PR review failed {
  prNumber: 33,
  error: 'GitHub automation module not installed. This project does not have the GitHub runner configured.'
}
```

## Environment

- **OS:** macOS
- **Version:** latest commit from development branch ( 2.7.4)

title: fix(worktree): prevent cross-worktree file leakage via environment variables
body:
## Summary

Fixes a critical bug where files from one git worktree would mysteriously appear as untracked files in other worktrees or the main repository.

## Root Cause

The pre-commit hook sets `GIT_DIR` and `GIT_WORK_TREE` environment variables when running in a worktree context. However, these variables were:

1. **Not cleared** when running in the main repo (where `.git` is a directory, not a file)
2. **Persisting** across shell sessions or being inherited by child processes
3. **Causing git commands** in the version sync section to target the wrong repository

This was confirmed by **5 independent investigation agents** that all converged on the same root cause.

## Changes

- **Clear `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE`** when NOT in a worktree context (lines 25-29)

- **Add comprehensive documentation** explaining the bug and fix

title: fix(pr-review): allow re-review when previous review failed
body:
## Summary

- Failed PR reviews no longer block retry attempts
- Bot detector now distinguishes between successful and failed reviews
- Adds test coverage for the new behavior

## Problem

When a PR review failed (e.g., SDK validation error), the system would:
1. Save a review result with `success=false` and mark the commit SHA as "reviewed"
2. On subsequent review attempts, detect "already reviewed commit" and return the failed review
3. Report "Review failed: None" instantly without actually retrying

## Solution

Modified the orchestrator's skip logic to check `existing_review.success` before returning a cached review. Failed reviews are now treated as "not reviewed" and allow a fresh review attempt.

title: UnicodeDecodeError in subprocess.run() during merge - missing errors parameter
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched existing issues and this hasn't been reported

### Area

Frontend

### Operating System

macOS

### Version

latest (January 2026)

### What happened?

When merging a task branch, the app crashes with a `UnicodeDecodeError` if git output contains non-UTF-8 bytes (e.g., binary files, files with different encodings).

**Error:**
```
UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xe2 in position 1: invalid continuation byte
```

**Location:**
`backend/merge/file_evolution/modification_tracker.py` line 227 in `refresh_from_git()`

**Root Cause:**
All `subprocess.run()` calls use `text=True` without specifying an `errors` parameter. When git commands return content with non-UTF-8 bytes, Python's default strict decoding fails.

**Fix:**
Add `errors="replace"` to all `subprocess.run()` calls that use `text=True`:

```python
# Before
subprocess.run([...], text=True, check=True)

# After
subprocess.run([...], text=True, errors="replace", check=True)
```

**Affected files:**
- `backend/merge/file_evolution/modification_tracker.py` (6 occurrences)
- `backend/merge/file_evolution/baseline_capture.py` (2 occurrences)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Have a git repository with files containing non-UTF-8 bytes (e.g., binary files, or text files with Latin-1/Windows-1252 encoding)
2. Create a task in Auto-Claude that modifies files
3. Try to merge the task branch back to main
4. The merge fails with `UnicodeDecodeError` in `modification_tracker.py`

**Full traceback:**

title: Kanban task stuck in "Human Review" after external worktree merge
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched existing issues and this hasn't been reported

### Area

Frontend

### Operating System

macOS

### Version

2.7.4




## What happened?

When a worktree is merged and deleted externally (via terminal/Claude Code, not through auto-claude's "Merge with AI" button), the Worktrees page correctly shows the worktree is gone, but the Kanban Board still shows the task in "Human Review" instead of automatically moving it to "Done".

This creates a confusing UX where:
- The Worktrees section is empty (correct)
- The Kanban Board shows the task in "Human Review" (incorrect - should be "Done")

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create a task in auto-claude and let it complete (moves to "Human Review" with worktree)
2. Open a **separate** terminal session (not through auto-claude)
3. Navigate to the project directory
4. Merge the worktree manually:
   ```bash
   git merge auto-claude/{task-spec-id} --no-edit
   git worktree remove .auto-claude/worktrees/tasks/{task-spec-id}
   git branch -D auto-claude/{task-spec-id}
   ```
5. Return to auto-claude and click "Refresh" on the Worktrees page
6. Observe: Worktrees page is empty (correct)
7. Navigate to Kanban Board
8. Observe: Task is still in "Human Review" column (incorrect)

## Expected behaviour

When a worktree is deleted and its branch has been merged into main, the corresponding Kanban task should automatically transition to "Done" status, regardless of whether the merge was performed through auto-claude's UI or externally.

The system should reconcile worktree state with task state on:
- Task loading/refresh
- Worktrees page refresh
- Kanban board refresh

## Root cause analysis

Auto-claude updates task status to "done" **only** when merging through its own UI (via `mergeWorktree` IPC handler). The status update happens in two places:

1. **`implementation_plan.json`** - persisted status file updated at `worktree-handlers.ts:2252-2259`
2. **`TASK_STATUS_CHANGE` IPC event** - sent at `worktree-handlers.ts:2314`

Neither mechanism fires when merging externally because:
- The backend code path is never executed
- There's no file watcher or reconciliation logic to detect external changes

The Worktrees page works correctly because it queries `git worktree list` directly, while the Kanban Board relies entirely on the persisted `implementation_plan.json` status.

## Proposed fix (high-level)

Add a worktree-task reconciliation step when loading tasks:

```
For each task with status == "human_review":
  1. Check if associated worktree still exists (via git worktree list)
  2. If worktree is deleted:
     a. Check if task branch was merged into main (git branch --merged main)
     b. If merged → update task status to "done" and persist to implementation_plan.json
     c. If not merged → keep current status (user may have discarded changes)
```

This could be implemented in:
- `loadTasks()` in `task-store.ts`
- A new `reconcileWorktreeStatus()` IPC handler called on Kanban/Worktrees refresh
- Background periodic sync (less preferred due to complexity)

**Files likely to modify:**
- `apps/frontend/src/renderer/stores/task-store.ts`
- `apps/frontend/src/main/ipc-handlers/task/worktree-handlers.ts`

title: Feature: Auto-detect and use target project's Python venv
body:
## Problem

When Auto-Claude agents work on Python projects, they use the system Python (or Auto-Claude's detected `pythonPath`) instead of the target project's virtual environment. This causes:

1. **`ModuleNotFoundError`** - packages installed in the project's venv aren't available
2. **Version mismatches** - system Python may differ from project requirements
3. **Silent failures** - wrong packages/versions can cause subtle bugs

### Current Workaround

Users must add explicit instructions to each project's `CLAUDE.md`:

```markdown
## ⚠️ MANDATORY: Python Environment ⚠️

NEVER use `python`, `python3`, `pip`, or `pytest` directly.

ALWAYS use this exact prefix:
unset PYTHONPATH && /path/to/project/.venv/bin/python
```

This is error-prone and must be repeated for every project.

## Proposed Solution

Auto-Claude should automatically detect and use the target project's Python environment:

### Detection Priority
1. **`.venv/` or `venv/` directory** → Use `{project}/.venv/bin/python`
2. **`.python-version` file** → Use pyenv: `~/.pyenv/versions/{version}/bin/python`
3. **`pyproject.toml` with `tool.poetry`** → Use `poetry run python`
4. **`Pipfile`** → Use `pipenv run python`
5. **Fall back** to `pythonPath` setting or system Python

### Implementation Options

**Option A: Inject into agent prompts**
- Add a `{{PYTHON_EXECUTABLE}}` variable to prompts
- Replace bare `python` commands in built-in prompts with this variable
- Populate based on detection logic above

**Option B: Environment wrapper**
- Before spawning Claude SDK, detect project venv
- Set `PATH` to prepend the venv's `bin/` directory
- Agents' `python` commands naturally resolve to venv

**Option C: Per-project settings**
- Add `pythonPath` to project-level settings (not just global)
- Auto-populate from detection, allow manual override
- Pass to agents via prompt injection

## Additional Context

The global `pythonPath` setting currently only affects display/detection - it doesn't propagate to agent commands. The prompts in `apps/backend/prompts/` use bare `python`/`python3` calls:

```python
# From prompts/validation_fixer.md
python3 -c "import json; json.load(open('[file]'))"

# From prompts/planner.md  
"command": "python -c \"from src.models.analytics import Analytics; print('OK')\""
```

## Benefits

- **Zero-config for most projects** - venv detection handles common cases
- **Eliminates CLAUDE.md boilerplate** - no more copy-pasting Python warnings
- **Reduces user confusion** - "why is Auto-Claude using the wrong Python?"
- **Safer multi-project workflows** - each project uses its own environment

title: fix(terminal): add require polyfill for ESM/Sentry compatibility
body:
## Summary

- Fixes terminal creation failing with "ReferenceError: require is not defined" on all platforms
- Root cause: Sentry's `require-in-the-middle` hooks expect `require.cache` which doesn't exist in ESM context
- Fix: Add `createRequire` polyfill at the top of `index.ts` before Sentry initializes

## Root Cause

This bug was introduced when Sentry packages were bundled into the main process in commit `e7b38d49` (hotfix/sentry-backend-build).

**The problem chain:**
1. Sentry packages (`@sentry/electron`, `@sentry/node`) are bundled into the ESM main process
2. Sentry uses `require-in-the-middle` to instrument module loading
3. This hook patches `Module.prototype.require` and expects `require.cache` to exist
4. Main process runs as ESM (`"type": "module"` in package.json)
5. In ESM context, `require` and `require.cache` are undefined
6. When node-pty tries to load native `.node` bindings via `require()`, Sentry's hook intercepts and crashes

**Affected:** All platforms (Windows, macOS, Linux) - terminal creation fails completely.

title: Ideation context analyzer incorrectly categorizes merged/completed specs as "planned_features"
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched existing issues and this hasn't been reported

### Area

Frontend

### Operating System

macOS

### Version

2.7.4



## 2. What Happened?

When running ideation generation, the `ideation_context.json` file labels ALL spec titles from `.auto-claude/specs/` as `planned_features`, regardless of whether the associated worktree has been merged (completed work).

This means completed features that have already been shipped are misrepresented as "planned" work, misleading the AI during idea generation.

Example from `ideation_context.json`:
```json
{
  "planned_features": [
    "Add trailing stop-loss agent code",  // Actually MERGED/COMPLETED
    "Implement backtesting module",       // Actually MERGED/COMPLETED
    ...
  ]
}
```

## 3. Steps to Reproduce

1. Have a project with completed specs (worktrees that have been merged into main)
2. Delete the `.auto-claude/ideation/` folder to force fresh generation
3. Click "Generate Ideas" in the Ideation UI
4. Check `.auto-claude/ideation/ideation_context.json`
5. Observe that `planned_features` contains titles of specs whose worktrees are already merged

## 4. Expected Behaviour

Specs should be categorized based on their completion status:
- **Completed specs** (merged worktrees) → `existing_features`
- **In-progress specs** (active worktrees) → `in_progress_features`
- **Planned specs** (no worktree yet) → `planned_features`

## 5. Root Cause Analysis

**File:** `source_code/apps/backend/ideation/analyzer.py` lines 104-117

The `gather_context()` method blindly reads all spec directories and extracts their titles without checking completion status:

```python
# Current buggy code - NO status filtering
specs_dir = self.project_dir / ".auto-claude" / "specs"
if specs_dir.exists():
    for spec_dir in specs_dir.iterdir():
        if spec_dir.is_dir():
            spec_file = spec_dir / "spec.md"
            if spec_file.exists():
                # Extract title from spec.md
                title = ...
                context["planned_features"].append(title)  # Always "planned"!
```

There is **zero filtering** for:
- Spec status (backlog, in_progress, done, etc.)
- Worktree merge status
- Git branch state

## 6. Proposed Fix (High-Level)

1. **Determine spec completion status** by checking:
   - `task_metadata.json` in the spec directory (if it tracks status)
   - Git branch existence/merge status for the associated worktree
   - Or a `state.json` file if one exists

2. **Categorize specs appropriately** in `analyzer.py`:
   ```python
   if spec_is_merged(spec_dir):
       context["existing_features"].append(title)
   elif spec_has_active_worktree(spec_dir):
       context["in_progress_features"].append(title)
   else:
       context["planned_features"].append(title)
   ```

3. **Update `ideation_context.json` schema** to include the new `in_progress_features` field

title: Linux Build Failing Due to Node.js v24 and tar Module Incompatibility
body:
Summary

What: Linux packaging fails with a SyntaxError when @electron/rebuild attempts to import the tar module using a default import, which is incompatible with tar v7.5.3's named export structure.

Where: npm run package:linux → electron-builder → @electron/rebuild

Impact: Cannot build Linux packages (AppImage, deb, flatpak) for distribution.

Problem Description

The recent security fix for CVE-2026-23745 (PR #1289, commit 0b2cf9b0) upgraded tar from v6.x to v7.5.3. This version is a pure ESM module that uses named exports instead of a default export. However, @electron/rebuild@4.0.2 (the latest available version) internally uses import tar from 'tar' in clang-fetcher.js:5, which fails because tar v7.5.3 does not provide a default export.

Error output:

SyntaxError:

1. The requested module 'tar' does not provide an export named 'default'

This occurs during electron-builder's native dependency rebuild step. The CI in PR #1289 did not catch this because it only ran electron-vite build, not the full electron-builder --linux packaging step.

Affected Areas

* /opt/dev/Auto-Claude/apps/frontend/package.json:142 - electron-builder build configuration (needs npmRebuild: false)
* /opt/dev/Auto-Claude/node_modules/@electron/rebuild/lib/clang-fetcher.js:5 - Problematic import (external dependency)

Steps to Reproduce

1. Run npm run install:all (completes successfully)
2. Run npm run package:linux
3. Observe: Build fails during @electron/rebuild step with SyntaxError about tar default export

Expected Behavior

Linux package builds complete successfully, producing AppImage, deb, and flatpak artifacts.

Actual Behavior

Build fails with tar import error in @electron/rebuild.

Proposed Solution

Add "npmRebuild": false to the electron-builder configuration in apps/frontend/package.json. This will skip the redundant rebuild step during packaging since native modules are already rebuilt by postinstall.cjs:

```
"build": {
  "npmRebuild": false,
  "appId": "com.autoclaude.ui",
  ... rest of config
}
```

Rationale: The postinstall.cjs script already handles native module rebuilding during npm install, making electron-builder's rebuild step redundant.

Code References

* /opt/dev/Auto-Claude/apps/frontend/package.json:141-236 - electron-builder configuration
* /opt/dev/Auto-Claude/apps/frontend/scripts/postinstall.cjs - Already handles native module rebuilding

Additional Notes

* Security context: The tar upgrade to v7.5.3 was intentional to fix CVE-2026-23745
* npm audit status: Currently shows 0 vulnerabilities
* Cross-platform impact: This affects all platform builds (Linux, macOS, Windows)
* CI gap: PR #1289 test plan listed "Frontend build passes" but only tested electron-vite build, not electron-builder packaging
* No @electron/rebuild update available: Version 4.0.2 is the latest; no fix from upstream is imminent
* tar v7.5.3 export structure: Named exports only (export \* from './create.js'), no default export
* @electron/rebuild@4.0.2 incompatible import: import tar from 'tar' expects default export

title: fix(backend): update task status to done after merge (#1294)
body:
## Summary
Fixes issue #1294 where merged tasks disappear from the Kanban board instead of moving to the Done column.

## Problem
When a task was merged via `--merge`, the backend successfully merged the code but **didn't update the task status** in `implementation_plan.json` from `human_review` to `done`. The frontend Kanban board relies on this status to determine which column to display tasks.

## Solution
Added `_update_task_status_after_merge()` function that:
1. Finds the spec directory (supports both `.auto-claude/specs/` and `auto-claude/specs/` locations)
2. Loads the `ImplementationPlan` using the proper data model
3. Updates `status` from `human_review`/`ai_review`/`in_progress` to `done`
4. Updates `planStatus` to `completed`
5. Saves with **atomic write** and **automatic timestamp update** via `ImplementationPlan.save()`

The function is called after successful merge in all three code paths:
- After AI-resolved conflicts/direct copy
- After standard git merge (smart merge path)
- After fallback to standard git merge

## Technical Details
- Uses `ImplementationPlan.load()` and `plan.save()` for consistency with codebase patterns

title: fix: remove unsupported --max-tokens extra_args causing agent failures
body:
## Problem

All spec creation agents were failing with:
```
error: unknown option '--max-tokens'
Fatal error in message reader: Command failed with exit code 1
```

This caused:
- Complexity assessment phase failures
- Spec writing phase failures
- All agent operations to fail completely

## Root Cause

The `extra_args: {"--max-tokens": "63000"}` configuration in `core/client.py` was attempting to pass `--max-tokens` to the Claude CLI, but the CLI doesn't support this option.

This was originally added as a workaround for the SDK's max_tokens limit on Opus 4.5 (64000 vs 65537), but it breaks agent execution since the CLI rejects the unknown flag.

## Solution

Removed the `extra_args` configuration entirely. The Claude SDK handles `max_tokens` internally, so the workaround is unnecessary.

- ✅ Complexity assessment phase completes
- ✅ Spec writing phase completes

title: fix(changelog): validate Claude CLI exists before generation
body:
## Summary

- Fixes FileNotFoundError when generating changelog without Claude CLI installed
- Uses `getToolInfo('claude')` to properly detect if Claude CLI was found (instead of checking if path equals fallback string `'claude'`)
- Provides clear error message with install instructions when CLI is missing

## Root Cause

When Claude CLI is not found by the detection logic, `getToolPath('claude')` returns the fallback string `'claude'`. The previous validation logic:
```typescript
if (this.claudePath !== 'claude' && !existsSync(this.claudePath)) {
  throw new Error(...);
}
```

This skipped validation when the fallback was returned, causing the code to proceed and spawn a Python subprocess that tries to execute `['claude', ...]` which fails with `FileNotFoundError: [WinError 2]`.

## Fix

Now uses proper detection:
```typescript
const claudeInfo = getToolInfo('claude');
if (!claudeInfo.found) {
  throw new Error(`Claude CLI not found. Please install Claude Code from https://claude.ai/download. ${claudeInfo.message || ''}`);
}
```

title: Silent IPC failure after update - requires manual rebuild to fix
body:
# Bug Report: Silent IPC failure after update - requires manual rebuild to fix

## Summary

After pulling the latest updates, the Kanban board drag-to-start functionality stops working silently. Tasks can be dragged to "In Progress" visually, but no agent execution occurs. The UI shows 0% progress indefinitely with "No logs yet" message. No error is displayed to the user.

## Environment

- **OS:** macOS (Darwin 25.2.0)
- **Auto-Claude Version:** 2.7.5
- **Node.js Version:** (run `node -v` to fill in)
- **Recent commits pulled:** Biome migration (#1289), Token Decryption fix (#1283), and others

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Pull latest changes from the repository (`git pull`)
2. Start the app with `npm run dev` or `npm start`
3. Open a project with existing tasks
4. Drag a task from Backlog/Planning to "In Progress" column
5. Observe: Task card moves visually, but nothing happens - no logs, no progress, no agent starts

## Expected Behavior

- Task should start executing
- Logs should appear in the task detail view
- Progress should update from 0%
- Console should show `[TASK_UPDATE_STATUS] Auto-starting task:` log

## Actual Behavior

- Task appears stuck at 0% progress
- "No logs yet - Logs will appear here when the task runs" message persists
- No console logs related to task execution appear
- DevTools console shows normal app startup but NO IPC-related logs when dragging tasks
- Debug info panel shows old EPIPE errors (not directly related)

## Root Cause Analysis

The IPC (Inter-Process Communication) bridge between the renderer process and main process appears to silently fail. When `persistTaskStatus()` is called from the Kanban board, the `ipcRenderer.invoke()` call either:
- Never reaches the main process handler
- Returns without triggering the auto-start logic

This is likely caused by a mismatch between the compiled JavaScript bundles and the updated source code after pulling changes.

## Workaround / Fix

Running a full rebuild resolves the issue:

```bash
cd /path/to/Auto-Claude
npm run build
# Then restart the app
npm run dev
```

After rebuild, tasks start executing normally.

## Suggested Improvements

1. **Auto-rebuild detection:** Check if source files are newer than compiled output on startup, and trigger rebuild if needed

2. **IPC failure handling:** Add error handling/timeout for IPC calls so users see an error message instead of silent failure:
   ```typescript
   // In task-store.ts persistTaskStatus()
   const result = await Promise.race([
     window.electronAPI.updateTaskStatus(taskId, status, options),
     new Promise((_, reject) =>
       setTimeout(() => reject(new Error('IPC timeout')), 5000)
     )
   ]);
   ```

3. **Startup validation:** Add a simple IPC ping/pong check on app startup to verify the bridge is working

4. **Documentation:** Add a note in README or CONTRIBUTING about running `npm run build` after pulling updates

## Screenshots

### Before fix - Task stuck at 0%
Task shows "In Progress" status but with:
- 0/11 subtasks
- 0% progress
- "No logs yet" message

### After fix - Task completes normally
Task progresses through all phases and moves to "AI Review" at 100%

## Additional Context

The issue appeared after pulling updates that included the Biome migration (ESLint to Biome, #1289). The migration touched many files which may have contributed to the build cache invalidation issue.

The most confusing aspect was the **complete silence** - no errors, no warnings, no indication that something was broken. The app appeared to work normally except tasks wouldn't start.

title: Task continues executing after being moved to Planning column
body:
## Bug Description

When a user drags a running task from "In Progress" back to "Planning" column, the task's UI status changes to Planning but the underlying process continues executing.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a new task
2. Start the task (begins spec creation phase)
3. While spec creation is running, drag the task back to Planning column
4. Observe: UI shows task in Planning, but execution logs continue appearing

## Expected Behavior

Task process should be terminated when moved out of "In Progress" status.

## Actual Behavior

Process continues running despite UI showing "Planning" status.

## Root Cause

**Task ID mismatch between spec creation and task execution tracking.**

In `apps/frontend/src/main/ipc-handlers/task/execution-handlers.ts`:

- **Spec creation** (line 213) registers process under `task.specId`:
  ```typescript
  agentManager.startSpecCreation(task.specId, ...)
  ```

- **Task execution** (lines 228, 244) registers process under `task.id`:
  ```typescript
  agentManager.startTaskExecution(taskId, ...)
  ```

- **Auto-stop logic** (line 687) only checks `task.id`:
  ```typescript
  if (status !== 'in_progress' && agentManager.isRunning(taskId)) {
    agentManager.killTask(taskId);
  }
  ```

When spec creation is running, `agentManager.isRunning(taskId)` returns `false` because the process is registered under `task.specId`, not `task.id`. The kill logic is skipped.

### Secondary Issue

The auto-stop path also doesn't call `fileWatcher.unwatch(taskId)` unlike the TASK_STOP handler.

## Recommended Fix

### 1. Use consistent task ID for startSpecCreation calls

Change lines 213, 756, and 1124 from:
```typescript
agentManager.startSpecCreation(task.specId, ...)
```
To:
```typescript
agentManager.startSpecCreation(taskId, ...)
```

### 2. Add fileWatcher.unwatch() to auto-stop path

After line 689, add:
```typescript
fileWatcher.unwatch(taskId);
```

## Environment

- OS: macOS
- Auto-Claude version: Latest

title: Fix: Ultrathink mode exceeds Claude API max_tokens limit (64001 > 64000)
body:
## Bug Description

When using Ultrathink mode with `claude-opus-4-5-20251101`, the API returns an error:

```
API Error: 400 {"type":"error","error":{"type":"invalid_request_error","message":"max_tokens: 64001 > 64000, which is the maximum allowed number of output tokens for claude-opus-4-5-20251101"}}
```

## Root Cause

The `ultrathink` thinking budget was set to exactly `64000` tokens. However, the Claude API internally adds 1 to the thinking budget to ensure at least 1 output token can be generated. This causes `max_tokens` to become `64001`, which exceeds the hard limit of `64000`.

## Files Affected

- `apps/backend/phase_config.py` - Line 28
- `apps/frontend/src/shared/constants/models.ts` - Line 31

## Fix

Reduce the `ultrathink` budget from `64000` to `63999`:

```python
# Before
"ultrathink": 64000,  # Maximum reasoning depth (within Claude API's 64000 token limit)

# After  
"ultrathink": 63999,  # Maximum reasoning depth (64000 - 1 to avoid API limit when +1 is added for output)
```

```typescript
// Before
ultrathink: 64000 // Maximum reasoning depth (Claude API hard limit)

// After
ultrathink: 63999 // Maximum reasoning depth (64000 - 1 to avoid API limit when +1 is added for output)
```

## Impact

This bug affects all Ultrathink operations including:
- Spec creation (discovery, spec_writing, self_critique phases)
- Complex Tasks profile (all phases use ultrathink)
- Any manual selection of "Ultra Think" thinking level

## Reproduction Steps

1. Create a new task with the "Complex Tasks" profile (or any profile using Ultrathink)
2. Start the spec creation process
3. Observe API error during any phase that uses extended thinking

title: fix: prevent tree-shaking from removing globalThis.require
body:
## Summary

- Fix "require is not defined" error on Windows when installing Claude Code CLI
- Use `Object.defineProperty()` instead of simple assignment to prevent tree-shaking

## Problem

The simple assignment `globalThis.require = require` was being removed by the bundler's tree-shaking optimization because it appeared to be dead code with no visible usage in the same module.

This caused the error:
```
Failed to open terminal for installation: require is not defined
```

## Solution

Replace:
```typescript
globalThis.require = require;
```

With:
```typescript
Object.defineProperty(globalThis, "require", { value: require, writable: true, enumerable: true, configurable: true });
```

`Object.defineProperty()` is a function call with side effects that the bundler cannot remove, while maintaining semantic equivalence with the original assignment.

## Testing

- [x] Verified patch survives tree-shaking in production build
- [x] Confirmed `globalThis.require` present in compiled output
- [x] Tested on Windows 11 - Claude Code CLI now detected and installable

## Related Issues

Fixes #1139
Fixes #1195  
Fixes #1221

```typescript
  { value: 'high', label: 'High', description: 'Deep thinking' },
  { value: 'ultrathink', label: 'Ultra Think', description: 'Maximum reasoning depth' }  // Available
] as const;
```

Users can select this in: **Settings → Feature Model Settings → GitHub PR Review → Thinking Level**

### 2. GitHub Runner Rejects 'ultrathink'

**File:** `apps/backend/runners/github/runner.py` (lines 678-684)

```python
parser.add_argument(
    "--thinking-level",
    type=str,
    default="medium",
    choices=["none", "low", "medium", "high"],  # Missing 'ultrathink'
    help="Thinking level for extended reasoning",
)
```

### 3. Other Backend Runners Accept 'ultrathink'

**Comparison of all backend runners:**

| Runner | File | Accepts 'ultrathink'? |
|--------|------|----------------------|
| spec_runner.py | apps/backend/runners/spec_runner.py:185 | YES |
| ideation_runner.py | apps/backend/runners/ideation_runner.py | YES |
| roadmap_runner.py | apps/backend/runners/roadmap_runner.py:71-76 | YES |
| insights_runner.py | apps/backend/runners/insights_runner.py | YES |
| **github/runner.py** | apps/backend/runners/github/runner.py:682 | **NO** |
| gitlab/runner.py | apps/backend/runners/gitlab/runner.py:279 | **NO** |

**Example from spec_runner.py (CORRECT):**
```python
choices=["none", "low", "medium", "high", "ultrathink"],
```

### 4. Backend Core Supports 'ultrathink'

**File:** `apps/backend/phase_config.py` (lines 23-29)

```python
THINKING_BUDGET_MAP: dict[str, int | None] = {
    "none": None,
    "low": 1024,
    "medium": 4096,
    "high": 16384,
    "ultrathink": 63999,  # Fully supported
}
```

The backend infrastructure already handles 'ultrathink' correctly - only the GitHub runner's argparse validation is missing it.

---

## Root Cause

**Incomplete implementation:** When `ultrathink` was added to the codebase for deep reasoning in spec creation, most backend entry points were updated to accept it in their argparse choices, but `github/runner.py` and `gitlab/runner.py` were overlooked.

### Data Flow

```
User selects "Ultra Think" in Settings UI
         ↓
Settings stored: featureThinking.githubPrs = 'ultrathink'
         ↓
GitHub PR follow-up review triggered
         ↓
Frontend: getGitHubPRSettings() reads 'ultrathink'
         ↓
Frontend: buildRunnerArgs() constructs: ['--thinking-level', 'ultrathink']
         ↓
Spawns: python runner.py --thinking-level ultrathink followup-review-pr 79
         ↓
Python argparse validates argument
         ↓
ERROR: invalid choice: 'ultrathink' (choose from 'none', 'low', 'medium', 'high')
```

---

## Impact

**Severity:** Medium
**Frequency:** Whenever a user customizes GitHub PR thinking level to "Ultra Think"

**Affected users:**
- Anyone who selects "Ultra Think" for GitHub PR reviews in Settings
- Anyone using agent profiles that set `githubPrs` thinking to `ultrathink`

**Cross-platform:** Confirmed to affect **Windows, macOS, and Linux** equally (argparse validation is platform-independent)

---

## Reproduction Steps

1. Open Auto Claude
2. Go to Settings → Feature Model Settings
3. Find "GitHub PR Review" section
4. Set Thinking Level dropdown to "Ultra Think"
5. Try to run a GitHub PR follow-up review
6. Observe error: `invalid choice: 'ultrathink'`

---

## Proposed Fix

Add `"ultrathink"` to the argparse choices list in two files:

### Fix 1: GitHub Runner

**File:** `apps/backend/runners/github/runner.py` (line 682)

```python
# Before
choices=["none", "low", "medium", "high"],

# After
choices=["none", "low", "medium", "high", "ultrathink"],
```

### Fix 2: GitLab Runner (for consistency)

**File:** `apps/backend/runners/gitlab/runner.py` (line 279)

```python
# Before
choices=["none", "low", "medium", "high"],

# After
choices=["none", "low", "medium", "high", "ultrathink"],
```

This aligns both runners with the choices used by `spec_runner.py`, `ideation_runner.py`, `roadmap_runner.py`, and `insights_runner.py`.

---

## Testing Verification

After applying the fix:

```bash
# 1. Update GitHub runner choices
# 2. Set GitHub PR thinking to "Ultra Think" in Settings
# 3. Run GitHub PR follow-up review
# 4. Verify: No argparse error, review runs successfully
```

---

## Environment

- **Auto Claude Version:** develop branch (latest)
- **Affected Component:** GitHub PR runner (`apps/backend/runners/github/runner.py`)
- **Platform:** Cross-platform (Windows, macOS, Linux)
- **Python Version:** 3.12+

---

## Related Issues

- Issue #1218, #1222, #1212, #1201, #1309, #1171, #1226: Different bug (ultrathink token budget exceeds API limit)
- This issue: argparse validation missing 'ultrathink' choice

---

## Additional Context

This bug was discovered through a 6-agent parallel investigation that confirmed:
1. Frontend defines and offers 'ultrathink' as a valid option
2. GitHub/GitLab runners have outdated choices lists
3. All other backend runners accept 'ultrathink'
4. Backend core (`phase_config.py`) fully supports 'ultrathink'
5. The issue is cross-platform (not Windows-specific)

The fix is a simple one-line change to align the GitHub and GitLab runners with the other backend entry points.

title: feat: General-purpose Launch App with process tracking and multi-language support
body:
## Summary

Extend the "Launch App" feature from Node.js-only to support all major programming languages and frameworks, with proper process tracking and cleanup capabilities.

## Problem

The current Launch App implementation (#1313) has several limitations:

1. **Node.js Only**: Only detects `package.json` and npm/pnpm/yarn commands
2. **No Process Tracking**: Spawned dev servers are "fire and forget" - no way to stop them
3. **Port Conflicts**: Multiple launches can pile up on ports 5173, 5174, etc.
4. **No Stop Button**: Users must manually find and kill processes
5. **Stale Processes**: Closing Auto-Claude doesn't terminate spawned dev servers
6. **Single-Instance Conflicts**: Apps with mutex locks (like Pyloid) fail if old instance exists

## Proposed Solution

### Phase 1: Process Tracking (P0)

Track all spawned processes per task/worktree to enable clean shutdown.

```typescript
interface TrackedProcess {
  pid: number;
  taskId: string;
  worktreePath: string;
  command: string;
  startedAt: Date;
  port?: number;
  type: 'node' | 'python' | 'rust' | 'go' | 'java' | 'dotnet' | 'other';
}

// In-memory registry with optional persistence
const processRegistry: Map<string, TrackedProcess[]> = new Map();
```

**Features:**
- Register PIDs when launching
- Unregister when processes terminate
- Query processes by task/worktree
- Persist to file for crash recovery

### Phase 2: Stop App Button (P1)

Add UI to terminate running dev servers.

**UI Changes:**
- "Stop App" button appears when dev server is running for the task
- Confirmation dialog for safety
- Loading state during termination
- Toast notification on success/failure

**Backend:**
- `TASK_WORKTREE_STOP_APP` IPC handler
- Graceful shutdown (SIGTERM) with fallback to force kill (SIGKILL)
- Clean up process registry

### Phase 3: Multi-Language Project Detection (P1-P2)

Detect project type from files and use appropriate commands.

| Project Type | Detection Files | Install Command | Launch Command |
|--------------|-----------------|-----------------|----------------|
| **Node.js** | `package.json` | `npm/pnpm/yarn install` | `npm run dev/start` |
| **Python (uv)** | `pyproject.toml` + `uv.lock` | `uv sync` | `uv run python main.py` |
| **Python (pip)** | `requirements.txt` | `pip install -r requirements.txt` | `python main.py` / `flask run` / `uvicorn` |
| **Python (poetry)** | `pyproject.toml` + `poetry.lock` | `poetry install` | `poetry run python main.py` |
| **Rust** | `Cargo.toml` | `cargo build` | `cargo run` |
| **Go** | `go.mod` | `go mod download` | `go run .` |
| **Java (Maven)** | `pom.xml` | `mvn install` | `mvn spring-boot:run` / `mvn exec:java` |
| **Java (Gradle)** | `build.gradle` | `gradle build` | `gradle bootRun` / `gradle run` |
| **.NET** | `*.csproj` / `*.sln` | `dotnet restore` | `dotnet run` |
| **Ruby** | `Gemfile` | `bundle install` | `rails server` / `ruby app.rb` |
| **PHP** | `composer.json` | `composer install` | `php artisan serve` / `php -S` |

**Implementation:**
```typescript
interface ProjectConfig {
  type: ProjectType;
  packageManager: string | null;
  installCommand: string | null;
  launchCommand: string | null;
  launchScript?: string;  // For Node.js: 'dev', 'start', etc.
  processPatterns: string[];  // Regex patterns for cleanup
  ports: number[];  // Default ports to check
}

function detectProjectType(worktreePath: string): ProjectConfig {
  // Check files in priority order
  // Return first match with full config
}
```

### Phase 4: System-Wide Cleanup (P2)

Nuclear option to kill all Auto-Claude-spawned processes.

**Features:**
- "Kill All Dev Servers" button in settings or toolbar
- Cleans up all tracked processes across all tasks
- Useful when switching contexts or debugging port issues
- Optional: Run on Auto-Claude startup to clean stale processes

**Implementation:**
- Persist process registry to `~/.auto-claude/process-registry.json`
- On startup: check if registered PIDs are still running, clean stale entries
- On quit: optionally terminate all tracked processes

### Phase 5: UI Enhancements (P3)

**Running Indicator:**
- Green dot or badge on tasks with active dev servers
- Hover shows: command, port, uptime

**Port Display:**
- Show which port the dev server is running on
- Click to open in browser

**Logs Panel (stretch goal):**
- Stream dev server stdout/stderr in UI
- Collapsible panel below workspace status
- Search/filter capabilities

## Implementation Plan

### Milestone 1: Core Process Tracking
- [ ] Create `ProcessRegistry` class with CRUD operations
- [ ] Persist registry to file with debounced writes
- [ ] Register processes on launch
- [ ] Add `TASK_WORKTREE_STOP_APP` IPC handler
- [ ] Add "Stop App" button to WorkspaceStatus

### Milestone 2: Python Support
- [ ] Add Python project detection (uv, pip, poetry)
- [ ] Detect Python launch commands from `pyproject.toml`
- [ ] Handle virtual environment activation
- [ ] Test with Pyloid apps (VoiceFlow)

### Milestone 3: Additional Languages
- [ ] Rust detection and launch
- [ ] Go detection and launch
- [ ] Java/Gradle/Maven detection
- [ ] .NET detection

### Milestone 4: Polish
- [ ] Running indicator on task cards
- [ ] Port display in UI
- [ ] System-wide cleanup button
- [ ] Startup cleanup of stale processes

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Can launch Node.js, Python, Rust, and Go projects
- [ ] "Stop App" button terminates the dev server
- [ ] Launching twice kills the first instance automatically
- [ ] Closing Auto-Claude cleans up spawned processes
- [ ] Process registry survives app restart
- [ ] UI shows which tasks have running dev servers

## Related Issues/PRs

- #1313 - Launch App with dependency handling (Node.js only)
- #1120 - Original Launch App button
- #1119 - Launch App feature request

## Technical Notes

### Cross-Platform Considerations

**Windows:**
- Use `taskkill /F /PID` for force kill
- Process tree may need `/T` flag
- PowerShell for process queries

**macOS/Linux:**
- Use `kill -TERM` then `kill -9` as fallback
- May need to kill process group with `-` prefix
- Use `pgrep`/`pkill` for pattern matching

### Process Groups

When spawning terminal windows, the actual dev server runs as a child of the terminal. We may need to:
1. Track the terminal PID
2. Find child processes of that PID
3. Kill the entire process tree

### Port Detection

For showing ports in UI:
- Parse stdout for "listening on port X" patterns
- Or query `netstat`/`lsof` filtered by PID
- Store detected port in process registry

---

title: [BUG] Windows: GitHub PR reviews fail with WinError 206 (command line too long) for large diffs
body:
## Bug Description GitHub PR follow-up reviews fail on **Windows** when the PR diff is large, causing the Claude Agent SDK to exceed Windows' command line length limit. **Error:** ``` FileNotFoundError: [WinError 206] The filename or extension is too long CLINotFoundError: Claude Code not found at: D:\...\claude_agent_sdk\_bundled\claude.exe ``` This prevents Windows users from performing PR reviews on PRs with large diffs (>8KB-32KB of changes). --- ## Evidence ### User's Error Log ``` [GitHub PR] STDERR: [ParallelFollowup] Review failed: Claude Code not found at: D:\Koding\Autoclaude\apps\backend\.venv\Lib\site-packages\claude_agent_sdk\_bundled\claude.exe [GitHub PR] STDERR: Traceback (most recent call last): [GitHub PR] STDERR: File "D:\Koding\Autoclaude\apps\backend\.venv\Lib\site-packages\claude_agent_sdk\_internal\transport\subprocess_cli.py", line 403, in connect [GitHub PR] STDERR: self._process = await anyio.open_process( [GitHub PR] STDERR: File "C:\Users\sondree\AppData\Local\Programs\Python\Python312\Lib\subprocess.py", line 1538, in _execute_child [GitHub PR] STDERR: hp, ht, pid, tid = _winapi.CreateProcess(executable, args, [GitHub PR] STDERR: FileNotFoundError: [WinError 206] The filename or extension is too long ``` **PR context:** * PR with 6 files changed * Diff size: up to 100,000 characters (current limit in `parallel_followup_reviewer.py:368`) * Subagents: 4 specialist agents defined for parallel review --- ## Root Cause ### 1\. Claude Agent SDK Passes Large Data as Command Line Args **File:** `claude_agent_sdk/_internal/transport/subprocess_cli.py` (line 175) ```python cmd.extend(["--agents", json.dumps(agents_dict)]) # ← Passes entire JSON as arg ``` The SDK constructs a command like: ```bash claude.exe --agents "{massive JSON with 100KB diff + 4 agent definitions + context}" ``` ### 2\. Windows Command Line Limit Windows `CreateProcess()` API has a **command line length limit**: * **32,767 characters** maximum (including executable path and all arguments) * Some contexts limit it further to **8,191 characters** ### 3\. PR Review Prompts Are Massive **File:** `apps/backend/runners/github/services/parallel_followup_reviewer.py` ```python # Line 368 MAX_DIFF_CHARS = 100_000 # Up to 100KB diff_content = context.diff_since_review # Line 373-418 - Builds massive prompt followup_context = f""" ### Diff Since Last Review ```diff {diff_content} # ← 100KB diff here ``` """ # Line 446 - Full prompt with diff + 4 agent definitions prompt = self.\_build_orchestrator_prompt(context) # Line 525 - SDK tries to pass this as command line await client.query(prompt) ``` **Total command line size:** - Executable path: ~100 chars - Agent definitions (4 agents): ~10KB - Orchestrator prompt: ~5KB - PR diff: up to 100KB - **Total: 115KB+ → Exceeds 32K Windows limit** --- ## Impact **Severity:** High (blocks Windows users from reviewing PRs with large diffs) **Affected Users:** - ✅ Windows users running from source - ✅ Windows users running packaged .exe - ❌ macOS users (Unix has much higher limits ~2MB) - ❌ Linux users (Unix has much higher limits ~2MB) **Why .exe is also affected:** The issue is in the **Claude Agent SDK** spawning `claude.exe` via `subprocess.Popen()` / Windows `CreateProcess()` API. The packaging method (source vs .exe) doesn't matter - Windows API limits apply regardless of how Auto Claude itself is run. --- ## Reproduction Steps 1. Open Auto Claude on Windows 2. Navigate to a GitHub PR with substantial changes (e.g., 6+ files, 500+ lines changed) 3. Click "Follow-up Review" 4. Observe error: `WinError 206: The filename or extension is too long` 5. PR review fails at 40% ("Orchestrator delegating to specialist agents...") --- ## Upstream Issue **This is a known issue in the Claude Agent SDK:** 🔗 [anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python#238 - "multi subagents with long prompt do not work on windows"](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/issues/238) **SDK Issue Details:** - SDK passes `--agents` as command line arg with full JSON content - Windows cmd has 8,191 character limit (or 32,767 for CreateProcess) - Workaround: Write agents to temp file, pass `--agents @file.json` instead --- ## Workarounds ### Option 1: Reduce Diff Size (Quick Fix) **File:** `apps/backend/runners/github/services/parallel_followup_reviewer.py` (line 368) ```python # Before MAX_DIFF_CHARS = 100_000 # After MAX_DIFF_CHARS = 20_000 # Reduce to stay under Windows limit ``` **Pros:** Simple one-line change
**Cons:** Truncates large diffs, may miss issues in truncated code ### Option 2: Apply Monkey Patch (Temporary) Use the workaround from SDK issue [#238]() - write agents to temp file instead of passing as args. **Location:** Before calling `create_client()` in `parallel_followup_reviewer.py` ```python import tempfile import json from claude_agent_sdk._internal.transport import subprocess_cli # Monkey patch the SDK's subprocess_cli module original_connect = subprocess_cli.SubprocessCLITransport.connect async def patched_connect(self): if self._options.agents: agents_file = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile( mode='w', delete=False, suffix='.json', dir=tempfile.gettempdir() ) agents_file.write(json.dumps(self._options.agents)) agents_file.close() # Modify command to use file reference self._options.agents = None if not hasattr(self, '_agents_file'): self._agents_file = agents_file.name # Add to command: --agents @file.json return await original_connect(self) subprocess_cli.SubprocessCLITransport.connect = patched_connect ``` **Pros:** Allows full diff review
**Cons:** Monkey patch may break with SDK updates ### Option 3: Wait for SDK Fix (Long-term) Anthropic needs to update the SDK to: 1. Use stdin for large prompts instead of command line args 2. Write agents to temp files by default 3. Use `--agents @file.json` syntax Track: [SDK Issue #238]() --- ## Proposed Fix **Short-term (for next Auto-Claude release):** * Apply Option 1: Reduce `MAX_DIFF_CHARS` to 20,000 or 30,000 * Add warning in logs when diff is truncated * Document Windows limitation in user-facing docs **Long-term (when SDK is fixed):** * Update `claude-agent-sdk` dependency to fixed version * Restore `MAX_DIFF_CHARS = 100_000` * Remove workarounds --- ## Testing Verification ### Test Case 1: Small PR (should work) * Create PR with 1-2 files, <100 lines changed * Run follow-up review * ✅ Expect: Success ### Test Case 2: Medium PR (may fail on current version) * Create PR with 5-10 files, 500+ lines changed * Run follow-up review * ❌ Expect: WinError 206 (before fix) * ✅ Expect: Success (after fix) ### Test Case 3: Large PR (should work with workaround) * Create PR with 20+ files, 2000+ lines changed * Run follow-up review * ✅ Expect: Success with truncated diff warning --- ## Environment * **Platform:** Windows 10/11 * **Python Version:** 3.12 * **Claude Agent SDK Version:** Check `apps/backend/requirements.txt` for `claude-agent-sdk` version * **Auto Claude Version:** develop branch (latest) * **Affected Component:** GitHub PR runner (`apps/backend/runners/github/services/parallel_followup_reviewer.py`) --- ## Related Issues ### Upstream (Claude Agent SDK): * [#238]() - Multi subagents with long prompt do not work on windows (DIRECT MATCH) * [#208]() - ClaudeSDKClient hangs on Windows during initialization * [#252]() - WinError 193 - SDK fails to detect claude.cmd on Windows ### Auto-Claude: * Issue #1316 (we just created) - Different bug (argparse rejects 'ultrathink') * This issue - Windows command line length limit --- ## Additional Context **Why this happens:** 1. PR reviews use parallel orchestrator with 4 specialist subagents 2. Each agent needs its own prompt definition 3. Orchestrator prompt includes full PR diff (up to 100KB) 4. SDK serializes all of this into command line args 5. Windows CreateProcess rejects commands >32KB **Why it's Windows-specific:** * Unix systems (macOS, Linux) have much higher command line limits (typically 2MB+) * Windows `CreateProcess()` API enforces 32,767 character limit * This is a fundamental Windows OS limitation, not a Python or SDK bug **Data flow:** ``` PR Review Requested ↓ parallel_followup_reviewer.py builds prompt (100KB) ↓ create_client() with 4 agent definitions (10KB) ↓ Claude Agent SDK serializes to command line ↓ subprocess.Popen() → CreateProcess(claude.exe --agents {...}) ↓ ❌ Windows CreateProcess: WinError 206 (command too long) ``` --- ## Recommendation **Immediate action:** 1. Reduce `MAX_DIFF_CHARS` to 30,000 in `parallel_followup_reviewer.py:368` 2. Add this to release notes as a known Windows limitation 3. Monitor upstream SDK issue [#238]() for fix **User communication:** * Document in README that Windows PR reviews are limited to smaller diffs * Suggest using web UI or macOS/Linux for large PR reviews * Provide workaround instructions for advanced users **Future:** * Update SDK when fix is available * Remove `MAX_DIFF_CHARS` reduction * Announce full Windows support for large PR reviews
